Definition

Input an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, a twice continuously
differentiable $f:U\to\mathbb R$, an initial point $x_0\in U$, target
$\varepsilon\ge0$, outer trial cap $N\in\mathbb N_0$, and an exact-Hessian
cubic-model solver $S$. Other inputs are $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$\gamma_{up}>1$, $0<\gamma_{down}<1$, $0<\kappa<1$,
$0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_0\le\sigma_{max}$, $0<\kappa_\theta<1$,
and the finite inner cap $J\in\mathbb N_0$. On input of the model, $J$,
and $\kappa_\theta$, the solver $S$ returns `no-candidate` or proposes a
vector. A proposed vector is admissible when it passes the model-solution
checks below. The solver may return `no-candidate` if it cannot certify such
a vector within its cap. Exact global minimizers are an admissible special
case; the local criterion also permits inexact steps satisfying the stated
conditions of [[lem-global-cubic-model-minimizer-decrease]].

The output is the last accepted iterate and one of `stationary`,
`target-achieved`, `outer-budget-exhausted`, `model-solver-failure`,
`inconsistent-model-solver`, `domain-exit`, or
`regularization-cap-exhausted`.

For $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, in order:

1. Compute $g_k:=\nabla f(x_k)$. If $g_k=0$, return $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$.
   If $\|g_k\|_2\le\varepsilon$, return $(x_k,\texttt{target-achieved})$.
   If $k=N$, return $(x_k,\texttt{outer-budget-exhausted})$.
2. Set $B_k:=\nabla^2 f(x_k)$ and form the model
   $m_k(s)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,s\rangle+\tfrac12s^TB_ks+
   \tfrac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_2^3$ of
   [[def-adaptive-cubic-regularization-model]]. By
   [[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]], $B_k$ is symmetric. Put
   $a_k:=\|g_k\|_2$, $q_k:=g_k^TB_kg_k$, and compute the cubic Cauchy
   step
   $$s_{C,k}:=-t_{C,k}g_k,\qquad t_{C,k}:=\frac{-q_k+\sqrt{q_k^2+4\sigma_ka_k^5}} {2\sigma_ka_k^3}.$$
   Call $S(m_k,J,\kappa_\theta)$. If it returns `no-candidate`, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{model-solver-failure})$. For a proposed $s_k$, recompute
   $\operatorname{pred}_k:=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)$ and
   $\nabla m_k(s_k):=g_k+B_ks_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2s_k$. Check
   $$g_k^Ts_k+s_k^TB_ks_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2^3=0, \qquad s_k^TB_ks_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2^3\ge0,$$
   $$\|\nabla m_k(s_k)\|_2\le \kappa_\theta\min\{1,\|s_k\|_2\}\|g_k\|_2, \qquad m_k(s_k)\le m_k(s_{C,k}).$$
   If any check fails, or if $s_k=0$ or
   $\operatorname{pred}_k\le0$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{inconsistent-model-solver})$.
3. If $x_k+s_k\notin U$, return $(x_k,\texttt{domain-exit})$ without
   evaluating $f$ there. Otherwise evaluate $f(x_k+s_k)$ and set
   $\rho_k:=[f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)]/\operatorname{pred}_k$.
   If $\rho_k<\eta_1$, reject the step and keep $x_{k+1}:=x_k$. If
   $\sigma_k=\sigma_{max}$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{regularization-cap-exhausted})$; otherwise set
   $\sigma_{k+1}:=\min\{\gamma_{up}\sigma_k,\sigma_{max}\}$ and continue.
4. If $\rho_k\ge\eta_1$, accept and set $x_{k+1}:=x_k+s_k$. If
   $\rho_k>\eta_2$ and
   $\|s_k\|_2\ge\kappa\|g_k\|_2/\sigma_k$, set
   $\sigma_{k+1}:=\max\{\sigma_{min},\gamma_{down}\sigma_k\}$;
   otherwise set $\sigma_{k+1}:=\sigma_k$.

The finite cap, solver failure, inconsistent-solver, domain-exit, and
regularization-cap branches are explicit. The model-solution checks include
the two cubic conditions (4.1)–(4.2), residual condition TC.s, and the
Cauchy-model decrease condition of Cartis–Gould–Toint, Part II, §4. The
procedure alone makes no unconditional convergence or evaluation-complexity
claim.

Definition

Assume AC and use the coefficient, Brownian, and initial-value conventions of
[[alg-euler-maruyama]]. The inputs are $T>0$, the coefficients $b,\sigma$,
the Brownian path or increment source, an initial value $X_0$, a deterministic
maximum step $h_{\max}>0$, and a deterministic work budget
$B\in\mathbb N_0$. Stopped Brownian values are measurable at their stopped
sigma-algebras by [[lem-continuous-adapted-process-at-bounded-stopping-time]],
and each stopping time $\tau_n$ is $\mathcal F_{\tau_n}$-measurable by the
event tests of [[def-continuous-time-stopping-time]]. Since $h_n$ is
$\mathcal F_{\tau_n}$-measurable, Borel coefficient evaluation and the
predictable-grid update keep $Y_n$ measurable at $\mathcal F_{\tau_n}$ by
induction. The continuous interpolation is adapted as well: at each fixed
$t$, the active-interval events are in $\mathcal F_t$ by the stopping-time
tests, and each term uses stopped values restricted to $\{\tau_n\le t\}$. Choose
one of the following modes.

1. **Predictable-grid mode.** Supply a finite predictable grid
   [[def-predictable-stopping-time-grid]] with
   $h_n\le h_{\max}$ on every active interval. Initialize $Y_0=X_0$ and
   process its intervals in order until the grid reaches $T$ or the budget
   is exhausted. Each interval uses the actual Brownian increment and update
   $$Y_{n+1}=Y_n+b(\tau_n,Y_n)h_n+ \sigma(\tau_n,Y_n)(W_{\tau_{n+1}}-W_{\tau_n}).$$
   The continuous interpolation on the interval is
   $$Y_t=Y_n+b(\tau_n,Y_n)(t-\tau_n)+ \sigma(\tau_n,Y_n)(W_t-W_{\tau_n}).$$
   This is the Euler–Maruyama update of [[alg-euler-maruyama]] with the
   supplied interval length; the fixed-grid supplier itself makes no
   variable-grid convergence assertion.

2. **Endpoint-refinement mode.** Supply a total Borel-measurable Boolean-valued
   accept/reject rule on the finite-dimensional current trial data. Initialize a queue with a finite partition
   $0=u_0<\cdots<u_J=T$ whose root intervals have lengths at most
   $h_{\max}$, together with their sampled Brownian increments. Pop the
   earliest interval $[u,u+\ell]$, form the Euler trial
   $Y^*=Y+b(u,Y)\ell+\sigma(u,Y)\Delta W$, and apply the supplied
   accept/reject rule. If accepted, set $Y\leftarrow Y^*$, append the
   right-endpoint/state pair to the accepted path record, and advance to the
   interval's right endpoint. If rejected, retain its parent increment,
   split it with [[alg-dyadic-brownian-bridge-increment-tree]], and put its
   left then right children at the front of the queue; do not update $Y$ on
   the rejected parent and do not redraw the parent or either child. This
   branch preserves the sampled path tree, but an endpoint-dependent
   acceptance rule is not a predictable-grid controller;
   the strong-error theorem on this page makes no error claim for this branch.

For either mode, initialize `current_time=0`, `current_state=X_0`, and
`trial_count=0`. Maintain `current_time` and `current_state` as the endpoint
and Euler state of the accepted path. In endpoint-refinement mode, also
initialize the accepted path record with $(0,X_0)$; append each
right-endpoint/state pair only when its interval is accepted.
Count every trial node, accepted or rejected, as one work unit; after each
trial, increment `trial_count` by one. Before the first trial and after every
trial, first check whether the mode's completion condition holds: the supplied
grid has reached $T$ in predictable-grid mode,
or the queue is empty and the accepted path reaches $T$ in endpoint-refinement
mode. If so, return with `status: complete`. Otherwise, if the count has
reached $B$, return with `status: inconclusive`; if not, perform the next
trial. Thus a budget $B=0$ returns `inconclusive`, and a last trial that
reaches $T$ returns `complete`.

Both statuses use the output record
`(mode, status, current_time, current_state, approximation, pending_work,
trial_count)`. On completion, `current_time=T`, `current_state=Y_T`, and
`pending_work` is empty. The `approximation` is the full continuous Euler
interpolation in predictable-grid mode; in endpoint-refinement mode it is the
accepted ordered endpoint/state record together with the retained increment
tree. On an inconclusive return, `trial_count=B`, `current_state` is the state
at `current_time`, and `approximation` is the partial output through that
time: the continuous interpolation restricted to $[0,\texttt{current\_time}]$
in predictable-grid mode, and the accepted endpoint/state record and retained
tree in endpoint-refinement mode. `pending_work` is the remaining ordered grid
suffix or the current ordered tree queue, respectively. The tree assigns no
values at non-dyadic times, so endpoint-refinement mode returns its accepted
node record rather than a continuous interpolation. A finite budget never
changes an inconclusive result into a successful certificate.

Definition

Input $0<\alpha<1$, a step size $h>0$, an integer $N\ge1$, $\lambda\ge0$,
an initial value $u_0$, and forcing values $F^1,\ldots,F^N$. If any
admissibility condition fails, return `invalid-input`. Set $\omega_0=1$ and
compute $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N$ in increasing order by

$$\omega_j:=\frac{j-1-\alpha}{j}\,\omega_{j-1}.$$

Set $V^0=0$ and $U^0=u_0$. For $n=1,\ldots,N$ in increasing order, compute

$$V^n:=\frac{F^n-\lambda u_0-h^{-\alpha}\sum_{j=1}^n\omega_jV^{n-j}}{h^{-\alpha}+\lambda},\qquad U^n:=u_0+V^n.$$

For any sequence $V^0,\ldots,V^N$ with $V^0=0$, use the notation

$$\bar\partial_h^\alpha V^n:=h^{-\alpha}\sum_{j=0}^n\omega_jV^{n-j}.$$

Return $U^0,\ldots,U^N$. A finite-precision implementation that cannot
certify a scalar solve returns `solve-failed` without reporting a value. No
FFT or truncated-memory error claim is included.

Definition

Use the equation and conventions of [[def-underdamped-langevin-equation-and-canonical-gibbs-density]]. Given a valid state $(q_n,p_n)\in\mathbb R^{2d}$, a step $h>0$, and a fresh independent vector $\xi_n\sim N_d(0,I_d)$, put $a=e^{-\gamma h}$ and execute exactly these five substeps in order:

1. **B half kick:** $p^{(1)}=p_n-\tfrac h2\nabla V(q_n)$.
2. **A half drift:** $q^{(1)}=q_n+\tfrac h2M^{-1}p^{(1)}$.
3. **O full thermostat:** $p^{(2)}=a p^{(1)}+\sqrt{\beta^{-1}(1-a^2)}M^{1/2}\xi_n$.
4. **A half drift:** $q_{n+1}=q^{(1)}+\tfrac h2M^{-1}p^{(2)}$.
5. **B half kick:** $p_{n+1}=p^{(2)}-\tfrac h2\nabla V(q_{n+1})$.

The output is $(q_{n+1},p_{n+1})$. If any required gradient is undefined or any input violates $h>0$, $\beta>0$, $\gamma>0$, or positive definiteness of $M$, return `failure` without an updated state. For a differentiable $V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ and finite valid state, both gradient calls are defined; reusing the stored value $\nabla V(q_{n+1})$ as the next step's first force means one new force evaluation per subsequent step. The random-vector cost is one fresh $d$-dimensional standard normal per step.

Definition

Input an integer bit budget $b\ge1$, two disjoint ideal fair-bit subsequences as in
[[thm-independent-fair-bit-streams-produce-uniforms]], and a fixed deterministic
configuration consisting of finite dyadic format parameters, positive integer
series truncation indices $N\ge1$ and nonnegative integer total split budgets
$B\ge0$ for the log/root interval evaluators, positive dyadic log/root width
targets, and phase parameters $0<\tau\le1/4$, integer exponent limits
$e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$, integer precisions $2\le p_0\le p_{\max}$,
and a positive integer elementary-series cap $J\ge1$. Every call uses
these fixed parameters; a failed call returns `inconclusive` with its supplier
status. No success at a requested width is promised for arbitrary fixed budgets.
The midpoint convention is [[thm-midpoint-bit-stream-coupling-and-error]], and
the exact reference transform is [[lem-box-muller-product-density-and-radius-moment]].

1. Take the first $b$ bits from each subsequence and form the exact dyadics
   $u_j=(K_j+1/2)2^{-b}$. Enclose $u_1$ by directed dyadic endpoints in the
   selected format. If this is non-finite or its lower endpoint is not
   positive, return `inconclusive`; underflow may not turn a log argument
   into an accepted interval containing zero.

2. Apply [[alg-budgeted-validated-range-evaluation]] to the logarithm DAG on
   that interval with the configured finite parameters and log width target.
   On `certified(L,X)`, write $L=[L_-,L_+]$ and set
   $\widehat\ell=L_-$, $\eta_\ell=L_+-L_-$. The natural logarithm equals
   the integral logarithm by [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]], so
   $L_-\le\log u_1<0$. Compute the exact dyadic $q=-2\widehat\ell\ge0$.

3. Enclose $q$ by directed endpoints in the configured format; reject
   non-finite endpoints or a negative lower endpoint. Apply the same budgeted
   procedure to its square-root DAG with the root width target. On a
   certified interval $S=[S_-,S_+]$, set $\widehat r=S_-$ and
   $\eta_s=S_+-S_-$. The range guarantee of
   [[thm-budgeted-range-evaluation-terminates-and-is-sound]] gives
   $|\widehat\ell-\log u_1|\le\eta_\ell$ and
   $|\widehat r-\sqrt q|\le\eta_s$. Width differences and the products in
   these instructions are exact dyadic arithmetic.

4. Call [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] on the exact rational
   $q_{\rm phase}=2u_2$ and configured phase parameters. On its certified
   return $(\widehat w,\epsilon)$, set
   $\widehat t=(\Re\widehat w,\Im\widehat w)$ and $\eta_t=\epsilon$.
   By [[thm-na-certified-unit-circle-phase-enclosure]],
   $\|\widehat t-(\cos(2\pi u_2),\sin(2\pi u_2))\|_2\le\eta_t$,
   including pi, angle, truncation and directed-endpoint errors. This is the
   existing phase routine, with its existing canonical-pi bridge.

5. Return the exact dyadic vector $\widehat Z=\widehat r\,\widehat t$ and
   the dyadic certificates $\eta_\ell,\eta_s,\eta_t$. If any preceding
   supplier call has a non-finite status, propagate it as `inconclusive`.
   Final vector multiplication is exact dyadic multiplication; rounding it
   further requires a separate added error certificate.

The output is the dyadic vector together with the reported evaluator certificates.
Its arithmetic suppliers provide neither an IID source nor exact normal output.

rows.current_statement_or_definition:
Definition

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:D\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$,
let $x\in D$, and let $p\in\mathbb R^n$ be arbitrary. Fix $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$ and finite
budgets $E,Z\in\mathbb N$ for expansion and zoom trials. After the direction check passes, use the functions
$\phi(t)=f(x+tp)$ and $\phi'(t)=\langle\nabla f(x+tp),p\rangle$ from
[[def-wolfe-and-strong-wolfe-conditions]]. **Output:** either a positive
strong Wolfe step, or one of `invalid-direction`, `domain-exit`, and
`evaluation-budget-exhausted`.

1. If $\langle\nabla f(x),p\rangle\ge0$, return `invalid-direction`.
   Set $a:=0$ and $t:=1$. For at most $E$ expansion trials, in order:
   - If $x+tp\notin D$, return `domain-exit` without evaluating the trial.
   - Evaluate $\phi(t)$ and $\phi'(t)$. If
     $\phi(t)>\phi(0)+c_1t\phi'(0)$ or $\phi(t)\ge\phi(a)$, call the zoom
     procedure below with the ordered endpoint pair $(a,t)$ and return its
     output.
   - If $|\phi'(t)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|$, return $t$ as a strong Wolfe step.
   - If $\phi'(t)\ge0$, call zoom with the reversed endpoint pair $(t,a)$ and
     return its output.
   - Otherwise set $a:=t$ and $t:=2t$.
2. If the expansion budget is exhausted, return `evaluation-budget-exhausted`.

For `zoom(a,b)`, preserve the endpoint order even when $b<a$. For at most
$Z$ zoom trials, in order:

1. Set $m:=(a+b)/2$. If $x+mp\notin D$, return `domain-exit` without
   evaluating the trial.
2. Evaluate $\phi(m)$ and $\phi'(m)$. If
   $\phi(m)>\phi(0)+c_1m\phi'(0)$ or $\phi(m)\ge\phi(a)$, set $b:=m$.
   Otherwise, if $|\phi'(m)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|$, return $m$ as a strong Wolfe
   step. In the remaining branch, if $\phi'(m)(b-a)\ge0$, first set
   $b:=a$; then set $a:=m$.
3. If the zoom budget is exhausted, return `evaluation-budget-exhausted`.

The procedure returns a step only after both strong Wolfe inequalities have
been checked. Finite budgets and domain exits may return failure even when a
strong Wolfe step exists; no convergence claim follows from the procedure
alone.

Definition

Input a nonempty compact, closed, and convex set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, an exact force evaluator $f:[0,T]\times C\to\mathbb R^d$, $T>0$, integer step count $N\ge1$, initial state $x_0\in C$, tolerances $\varepsilon_k\ge0$, finite budgets $B_k\in\mathbb N$ for $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, and a projection-certificate provider $S$. The explicit closedness condition matches [[def-projected-contact-dynamics-and-euler-step]]. An admissible provider, queried with $(C,y,\varepsilon,B)$, returns either `unresolved` after at most $B$ candidate checks or `certified(p,\Pi)` with a finite exact certificate $\Pi$ proving $p\in C$ and

$$\sup_{z\in C}\langle y-p,z-p\rangle\le\varepsilon^2.$$

Set $h=T/N$, $t_k=kh$, and start with the given $x_0$. For $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, form $y_k=x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)$ and call $S(C,y_k,\varepsilon_k,B_k)$. If the response is `unresolved` or is not a sound `certified(p,\Pi)` response of the stated form, stop and return `unresolved` with the valid prefix $x_0,\ldots,x_k$. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=p$ and continue. After all $N$ calls succeed, return `complete`, the nodes, their affine interpolant, and the per-step tolerances. The procedure assumes exact force evaluations and sound exact certificates; arithmetic and force-evaluation errors are not included. With $\varepsilon_k=0$, a successful step satisfies the exact projection-Euler recurrence by [[lem-projected-euler-projection-residual-certificate]].

The algorithm makes at most $N$ provider calls, each with its stated finite candidate-check budget. Failure to certify a projection is reported; no convergence or accuracy is inferred from an unverified stopping tolerance. The provider is an explicit input: this definition does not construct a solver for arbitrary compact convex sets.

rows.current_statement_or_definition:
Definition

The input is a finite sequence of deterministic $C^1$ transitions $F_j:U_j\subseteq E_{j-1}\to E_j$, $j=1,\ldots,T$, between compatible finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces with open domains, a starting state $x_0\in E_0$, and a terminal cotangent $\bar x_T\in E_T$. Every transition is evaluated on one fixed strict branch and has its exact local reverse rule. For $T\ge1$, require the last transition's output space to be $E_T=\mathbb R$; when that scalar output is the objective, take $\bar x_T=1$. For $T=0$, the terminal value is $x_0$ and its matching cotangent $\bar x_0$ is supplied. A transition tape stores the local values needed by its exact reverse rule. A deterministic replay applies the same transition maps, in the same order, to the identical checkpoint state and therefore reproduces the same values and local derivative inputs. The procedure returns the terminal value and cotangent at $x_0$; an invalid domain evaluation returns DOMAIN_ERROR, and a branch boundary returns NONDIFFERENTIABLE. A checkpoint schedule is permitted only when its saved states and all deterministic replays lie in these declared domains.

**Uniform-block mode.** For $T=0$, return $x_0$ and the supplied cotangent without work. For $T\ge1$, require an integer slot budget $m\ge1$, set $q=\lceil T/m\rceil$, and during one forward pass save $x_{jq}$ for $j=0,\ldots,\lceil T/q\rceil-1$ (all indices are below $T$). This uses at most $m$ saved states. Partition the steps into blocks $[a,b]$ with $a=jq$ and $b=\min(a+q,T)$. Process the blocks from last to first. Within one block, for $\ell=b,b-1,\ldots,a+1$, restore $x_a$, replay $F_{a+1},\ldots,F_{\ell-1}$ without recording, evaluate $F_\ell$ once while recording its local tape, apply its reverse rule to the current cotangent, and discard the one-step tape and replay workspace. Retain only the checkpoint states, the live state/cotangent, and the ordinary one-step reverse tape. Do not infer any optimality property of this schedule.

**Binomial mode.** Define $C(d,0)=C(0,t)=1$, and $C(d,t)=C(d-1,t)+C(d,t-1)$ for integers $d,t\ge1$. The top-level call takes nonnegative integer budgets $d,t$ satisfying $T\le C(d,t)$. The recursive procedure REVERSE$(a,N,d,t,x_a,\bar x_{a+N})$ requires integer indices $0\le a\le a+N\le T$, nonnegative integer budgets $d,t$, the capacity condition $N\le C(d,t)$, and a known starting state $x_a$. If $N=0$, return the pair $(x_a,\bar x_a)$, the known terminal state and unchanged cotangent. If $N=1$, evaluate and record the unique transition, apply its local reverse rule, and return its output and input cotangents. If $N\ge2$, then $d,t\ge1$. Put $L=\min(N-1,C(d,t-1))$, $R=N-L$; replay the first $L$ transitions from $x_a$ without recording and save the resulting midpoint state $x_{a+L}$. Call REVERSE$(a+L,R,d-1,t,x_{a+L},\bar x_{a+N})$ on the right block. Release the midpoint checkpoint, restore the caller's supplied $x_a$, and call REVERSE$(a,L,d,t-1,x_a,\bar x_{a+L})$ on the left block, where $\bar x_{a+L}$ is the cotangent returned by the right call. Return the right call's terminal value and the left call's cotangent at $x_a$. The top-level call uses $a=0,N=T$, with the input terminal cotangent. A recursive call with $N>1$ and $d=0$ or $t=0$ is a schedule failure; the capacity condition makes that branch unreachable.

The parameter $d$ bounds the number of simultaneously saved state snapshots. The parameter $t$ bounds, for each transition, the number of additional unrecorded forward evaluations beyond its one recorded evaluation. Both are finite integer inputs. This mode provides no numerical error estimate or optimality guarantee for arbitrary nonuniform primitive costs. For the storage count in the paired theorem, $R_s$ bounds scalar storage for one full primal state. The binomial recursion may reuse one mutable cotangent workspace: each call consumes its terminal cotangent and returns the cotangent at its start, reusing the same buffer through both children. Let $G$ bound the largest one-step tape and local reverse scratch, the constant number of live cotangent/work vectors, and the scalar call-frame records; it excludes the $d$ saved primal states and one live primal state.

Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian conventions of
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] on $[0,T]$ with
$U=(0,\infty)$. The input consists of $\kappa,\theta,\sigma>0$ satisfying
the Feller condition $2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$, a step $h>0$, a current
transformed value $z_n\ge0$, and a finite Brownian increment $\Delta W_n$.
Set
$$a=\frac{4\kappa\theta-\sigma^2}{8},\qquad A=1+\frac{\kappa h}{2},\qquad c=z_n+\frac{\sigma}{2}\Delta W_n.$$
For valid parameters, $a>0$ and $A>0$. Compute
$$z_{n+1}=\frac{c+\sqrt{c^2+4Aah}}{2A},\qquad x_{n+1}=z_{n+1}^2.$$
This is the positive-root solution of
$$A z_{n+1}^2-cz_{n+1}-ah=0,$$
which is the drift-implicit Euler equation for the Lamperti variable
$Z=\sqrt X$ in the CIR model
$dX_t=\kappa(\theta-X_t)dt+\sigma\sqrt{X_t}\,dW_t$.

Return `invalid-input` for parameters outside the stated domain or a
non-finite input. Otherwise return `success` with $(z_{n+1},x_{n+1})$. In
exact real arithmetic the discriminant is strictly positive and the displayed
root is finite and positive for every $z_n\ge0$ and $\Delta W_n\in\mathbb R$;
the algorithm has no rejected root branch. A floating-point implementation
that cannot verify a finite positive root returns `solve-failure` and does
not advance the state. This is a specific implicit square-root update, not
the ordinary Euler–Maruyama update for $X$.

Inputs are a transcription record from [[alg-ctrl1-runge-kutta-shooting-and-collocation-transcription]], a primal initial iterate $z_0$ and full multiplier iterate $\mu_0=(
u_0,\lambda_0)$ in the fixed equality/inequality constraint ordering, an optional strict primal/slack/dual start in canonical QP coordinates, an SQP model builder, and finite nonnegative tolerances $	au_p,	au_d,	au_c,	au_{stage},	au_{quad}$. Also supply an SQP update cap $K\ge0$, QP update cap $N\ge0$, positive penalty/backtracking caps $R,J_{max}\ge1$, merit parameters $ho_0>0$, $\gamma>1$, $0< eta,\sigma<1$, and the finite-budget exact-Hessian branch selector and identified active set when that branch is requested. The IVP estimator uses its own declared controller tolerances; its status is not treated as an error certificate.

The SQP model builder is a deterministic finite procedure which, at each queried full state $(z_k,
u_k,\lambda_k)$, returns either a failure status or the finite NLP data $f_k,h_k,g_k,Dh_k,Dg_k$, its objective gradient, a symmetric positive-definite SQP model matrix $W_k$ when the merit branch is selected, and the exact Lagrangian Hessian when the exact-Hessian branch is selected. u_k$, active inequality multipliers $(\lambda_k)_I$, and zero inactive multipliers; its required positivity is the separate reduced-curvature condition of the exact step, not full positive definiteness. It must use $g_i\le0$ and nonnegative inequality multipliers. In the merit branch, the associated quadratic subproblem is exactly $\min_p 
abla f_k^Tp+	frac12p^TW_kp$ subject to $h_k+Dh_kp=0$ and $g_k+Dg_kp\le0$. For that branch, the builder also supplies the active equality/inequality row data required by [[alg-sqp-merit-globalization-with-finite-budgets]]. Solver tolerances are used as follows: $	au_p$ bounds the norm of equality and positive inequality violations, $	au_d$ bounds the stationarity residual, and $	au_c$ bounds multiplier-feasibility and complementarity residuals. The stage and quadrature tolerances are passed to the transcription's corresponding residual and certified-error checks. The IVP estimator uses its own declared controller tolerances and has a separate status; its embedded difference is not a certified error bound. Any called builder, evaluator, canonicalizer, or solver returns a value or failure status in finite time.

First audit the transcription dimensions, sampled domains, and data status fields. If stage construction failed, return the partial record with its stage and NLP statuses and do not call a solver. If the model satisfies [[lem-ctrl1-lqr-transcription-is-a-convex-quadratic-program]], map its finite quadratic objective and affine constraints to canonical LP/QP form: replace each free variable $z_i$ by $z_i^+-z_i^-$ with $z_i^+,z_i^-\ge0$; for each affine inequality $a_i^Tz+d_i\le0$, add a slack $s_i\ge0$ and equality $a_i^Tz+s_i=-d_i$; retain existing equalities; and transform the quadratic objective by substitution. The transcription record supplies finite stored coefficient arrays. Canonicalize using exact rational arithmetic on their dyadic values, then round each resulting coefficient once to the nearest normal representable value under [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], preserving exact zeros; any range failure makes the QP route inapplicable. Check the resulting equality matrix by exact rational row elimination; if it is rank deficient or the conversion is otherwise inadmissible, mark the QP route inapplicable and proceed to SQP. The optional start is in these converted coordinates and is checked constructively: require the primal and slack coordinates strictly positive and a finite dual vector of the right dimension. If it is absent or fails this check, record `strict-start-unavailable` and proceed to SQP; do not infer infeasibility or decide whether some other strict start exists. If it passes, call [[alg-primal-dual-newton-residual-method-for-lp-qps-and-symmetric-cones]] once with centering and fraction-to-boundary parameters both $1/2$, tolerances $	au_p,	au_d,	au_c$ and cap $N$. If it returns `invalid-input` or `strict-start-unavailable`, record that QP status and proceed to SQP. Return every other status and audited residuals. `certified-gap` certifies the resulting stored canonical floating-point QP, interpreted as exact dyadic rationals, under [[thm-fraction-to-boundary-and-primal-dual-gap-certificates]]; it is not a certificate for the unsampled continuous problem. A `residual-candidate` remains a candidate. No other QP status is reinterpreted as success.

If the QP route is inapplicable or lacks a supplied strict start, run the SQP branch only when the transcription status is solver-ready `constructed`; otherwise return its `not-smooth-nlp` or model-construction status without an SQP call. Initialize $(z,
u,\lambda)=(z_0,
u_0,\lambda_0)$ and verify the full multiplier dimensions. An invalid state returns `model-build-failure` with its last available record. For $k=0,1,\ldots,K$, in order, query the model builder at the entire current state $(z_k,
u_k,\lambda_k)$, propagating any builder failure without changing that state, and compute
$$r_p=(h_k,[g_k]_+),\quad r_d=
abla f_k+Dh_k^T
u_k+Dg_k^T\lambda_k,\quad r_\lambda=[-\lambda_k]_+,\quad r_c=(\lambda_{k,i}g_{k,i})_i,$$
where positive parts are componentwise. u_k,(\lambda_k)_I))$ with inactive multipliers set to zero, using the exact Hessian evaluated at that same pair. On its successful full Newton-pair return $(z^+,\mu^+)$, use $z^+$, place the equality and active-inequality components of $\mu^+$ into the full vectors $(
u,\lambda)$, and set inactive inequality components to zero; any failure stops with that status without changing the current state. This procedure is restricted to a smooth, unconstrained-interior control branch. Let the smooth data be those of [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]], with no active path constraints, and let $H(t,x,p,u)=L(t,x,u)+p^Tf(t,x,u)$. Supply a pointwise-defined twice continuously differentiable feedback $\psi(t,x,p)$ on an open tube such that $H_u(t,x,p,\psi(t,x,p))=0$ and $\psi(t,x,p)\in\operatorname{int}U_c$ throughout that tube; differentiability uses the convention of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Every successful IVP evaluation must keep its trajectory in this tube. If the evaluator cannot certify that condition for a queried trajectory, return `inadmissible-interior-branch` with no shooting result. Define $H_x^{\mathrm{fix}}(t,x,p,u):=D_x[L(t,x,u)+p^Tf(t,x,u)]$, with the derivative taken holding $u$ fixed, and only then substitute $u=\psi(t,x,p)$. Define $z=(x,p)\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ and
$$G(t,z)=\begin{pmatrix} f(t,x,\psi(t,x,p))\\-H_x^{\mathrm{fix}}(t,x,p,\psi(t,x,p))\end{pmatrix},\qquad B(z_{\mathrm{init}},z_{\mathrm{term}})=\begin{pmatrix}x_{\mathrm{init}}-x_0\\p_{\mathrm{term}}-\phi_x(x_{\mathrm{term}})\end{pmatrix},$$
where $z_{\mathrm{init}}=(x_{\mathrm{init}},p_{\mathrm{init}})$ and $z_{\mathrm{term}}=(x_{\mathrm{term}},p_{\mathrm{term}})$.
The **indirect shooting procedure** takes a certified differentiable IVP evaluator for $z'=G(t,z)$, an initial trial $z_0$, residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and correction cap $M\in\mathbb N_0$, and calls [[alg-single-shooting-for-nonlinear-bvps]] on the square BVP $(G,B)$. It returns that algorithm's trajectory and status without changing the root-tolerance meaning. In particular, `root-tolerance-met` certifies only the computed boundary residual for the numerical IVP map; it is not an exact BVP, optimality, global-optimality, or discretization-error certificate. If the control is on a boundary or no such smooth feedback is supplied, this procedure is inapplicable.

Definition

**Inputs.** Supply pointwise smooth data on $[0,T]$ from [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]], an original mesh, a piecewise-constant control parameterization, an explicit tableau from [[def-explicit-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-map]] or a possibly implicit tableau from [[def-ctrl1-runge-kutta-tableau-and-stage-collocation]], one of `single-shooting`, `multiple-shooting`, or `collocation` mode, a finite smooth representation of the control constraints when a solver-ready NLP is requested, finite sets of declared path-constraint times, endpoint constraints, the tableau quadrature rule, an initial decision vector $z_0$ and multiplier vector $\mu_0$, a stage residual tolerance $\tau_s\ge0$, a quadrature error tolerance $\tau_q\ge0$, a stage Newton correction cap $M_s\in\mathbb N_0$, and a maximum number of mesh nodes. Supply a deterministic derivative evaluator for the actual returned stage maps and resulting finite NLP on an open neighborhood of the queried candidate. On a locally fixed strict stopping branch of the finite stage-iteration procedure, differentiate that finite graph, including when the residual happens to be exactly zero at the queried point. Implicit differentiation as in [[thm-implicit-differentiation-forward-and-adjoint-formulas]] is permitted only when the selected returned stage map is certified to agree on that neighborhood with the exact local solution branch and its residual Jacobian is nonsingular there; an exact residual at the queried point alone does not establish this agreement. Return `derivative-failure` when no derivative of the actual returned map is available. Supply a quadrature error evaluator which returns a certified upper bound for the objective quadrature discrepancy or `unavailable`. Each supplied evaluator returns a value or failure in finite time. An optional trajectory-estimation request supplies the inputs of [[alg-bounded-adaptive-runge-kutta-controller]].
$$X_{j,i}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_{k<i}a_{ik}F_{j,k},\quad t_{j,i}=t_j+c_ih_j,\quad F_{j,i}=f(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j),\quad \Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_i b_iF_{j,i}.$$

**Mesh and constraints.** Check $0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T$, all declared constraint and quadrature times in $[0,T]$, and all stage times $t_j+c_i h_j$ in $[0,T]$ before querying $f$ or $L$. An invalid time returns `mesh-domain-failure` with no evaluation. Insert every declared path-constraint time not already a node into the mesh, unless this exceeds the supplied node cap, in which case return `mesh-budget-exhausted`. Tie each inserted subcell's control to its original containing cell, so the parameterization is unchanged. A path constraint is evaluated at its declared times, now mesh nodes; an endpoint constraint is evaluated at its declared endpoint. This is finite sampling and does not assert continuous-path feasibility.

**Stage evaluation.** On each cell write $h_j=t_{j+1}-t_j$ and $u_j$ for its tied constant control. For an explicit tableau, form the stages recursively by the displayed equations. Before each query of $f$ or $L$, check that the time is in $[0,T]$, the state lies in $\Omega_x$, and the control lies in $\Omega_u$; a failed membership check returns `stage-domain-failure`, and an unavailable function value returns `stage-evaluation-failure` with the cell and stage index. Apply the same checks to every declared path-constraint evaluation.

For an implicit tableau, do not leave the collocation stages as outer NLP decision variables. Form the coupled slope residual
$$R_j(K;X_{j,0},u_j)_i=K_i-f\!\left(t_j+c_ih_j,X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_k a_{ik}K_k,u_j\right),\quad i=1,\ldots,s.$$
Its open domain consists of stage vectors for which every state-control input is in the smooth-data tube. In the sampled linear-quadratic branch, form the finite matrix $M_j$ with blocks $(M_j)_{ik}=\delta_{ik}I-h_ja_{ik}A(t_{j,i})$ and right-hand side $r_i=A(t_{j,i})X_{j,0}+B(t_{j,i})u_j$. Use exact Gaussian elimination on the stored sample coefficients: scan columns left to right, pivot on the first nonzero entry at or below the current row, swap, eliminate below, and back-substitute. If no pivot is available, return `singular-stage-matrix`; otherwise the exact solution of $M_jK=r$ is the stage vector and the nonlinear-solve status is `exact-linear-stage-solve`. In all other smooth cases, form the deterministic initial guess $K_i^{(0)}=f(t_j,X_{j,0},u_j)$ after checking that this query is defined. Before calling Newton, check that the entire seed $K^{(0)}$ belongs to the declared open domain of $R_j$, equivalently that every induced stage state lies in $\Omega_x$ and every required control lies in $\Omega_u$. If this check fails, return `stage-domain-failure` with the failing cell and stage index, the partial result record, and no objective candidate. Otherwise call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $R_j$ with that open evaluation domain, tolerance $\tau_s$ and cap $M_s$. Record its iterate, residual vector, and exact status for each cell. Only `root` supplies a stage candidate; it means $\|R_j\|_2\le\tau_s$, not an exact root unless $\tau_s=0$. Any other status returns the partial result record with `nlp_status=stage-solve-failure`, the failing cell, and no objective candidate. On a returned stage vector use $X_{j,i}=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_k a_{ik}K_k$ and $\Phi_j=X_{j,0}+h_j\sum_i b_iK_i$. A singular stage Jacobian or failed stage query is reported, not interpreted as lack of an exact solution.

**Transcription modes.** In single shooting, the decision variables are the original-cell controls; set $X_{0,0}=x_0$ and recursively compute $X_{j+1,0}=\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)$. In multiple shooting, the decision variables are node states and controls; fix $X_{0,0}=x_0$ and define defects $d_j=X_{j+1,0}-\Phi_j(X_{j,0},u_j)$. In collocation mode, use the same node/control variables and solved internal stage states; the collocation equations are solved internally by the implicit-stage procedure above. Explicit stages are likewise internal deterministic evaluations. In every mode the finite feasible set includes $u_j\in U_c$ for each original cell. The finite objective is $\sum_j h_j\sum_i b_iL(t_{j,i},X_{j,i},u_j)+\phi(X_{N,0})$, and the finite constraints are exactly the declared node/time constraints, the represented control constraints, and endpoint constraints. If $U_c$ is available only as a compact set-membership constraint and has no finite smooth representation, return the finite set-constrained model with `nlp_status=not-smooth-nlp`; the dispatcher must not treat it as an SQP-ready NLP. A QP solver route additionally requires the sampled control constraints to be affine.

**Output.** Evaluate the supplied initial candidate and return a record containing its ordered decision variables, defect residuals, per-cell implicit-stage residuals, path/endpoint constraint residuals, KKT residuals, and objective value, when available. For equality residual $h$, inequality residual $g\le0$, and multiplier pair $(\nu,\lambda)$, report $r_p=(h,[g]_+)$, $r_d=\nabla J_N+Dh^T\nu+Dg^T\lambda$, $r_\lambda=[-\lambda]_+$, and $r_c=\lambda\odot g$. Include a model that can reevaluate these quantities at a later solver candidate. Return separate `nlp_status`, per-cell `implicit_stage_status`, optional `ivp_status`, `quadrature_status`, `mesh_status`, and `budget_status` fields. A quadrature bound at most $\tau_q$ is `bound-met`; a larger bound is `bound-not-met`; an unavailable bound is `unavailable`. The build-stage budget field is `not-run`; the solver dispatcher fills its final value. A failed derivative evaluation leaves KKT residuals unavailable with its exact status. An unevaluated optional IVP estimate is `not-requested`; if requested, report the adaptive controller's exact finite status, not an error certificate.

This direct transcription samples pointwise data; an $L^\infty$ equivalence class without a chosen representative and sampling rule is not stage-evaluable. For a single-shooting reduced objective represented as the finite state-step graph of [[def-parameterized-finite-state-step-objective]], its exact real-arithmetic reduced gradient is given by [[thm-discrete-adjoint-gradient-recursion]]. Agreement with the continuous ODE adjoint gradient is only conditional on the weighted discrete-gradient representation and the separate state, adjoint, derivative-data, endpoint, and quadrature estimates in [[thm-discrete-continuous-gradient-error-order-p]]. The optional adaptive RK estimate is separate from the fixed NLP and its embedded difference is not a certified global error bound. The algorithm makes no continuous-path feasibility, convergence-rate, global-optimality, or unconditioned discrete-adjoint accuracy claim.

Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be twice
continuously Fréchet differentiable. Write $g(x)=\nabla f(x)$ and
$H(x)=\nabla^2 f(x)$ using [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]. The Hessian is symmetric by
[[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]].

**Inputs:** $x_0\in U$, a Newton-decrement tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, and
line-search parameters $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$. **Output:**
when the procedure stops, return the last valid iterate $x_k$ and one of the
statuses `stationary`, `decrement`, or
`positive-definite solve unavailable`.
If none of these stopping conditions occurs, the sequence continues and there
is no finite return.

At iteration $k$ with current iterate $x_k$:

1. Compute $g_k:=g(x_k)$. If $g_k=0$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$.
2. If $H_k:=H(x_k)$ is not positive definite, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{positive-definite solve unavailable})$ without a Newton
   update. Otherwise compute its Cholesky factorization $H_k=L_kL_k^T$, solve
   $L_kw=-g_k$ and $L_k^Tp_k=w$, and set
   $$\lambda_k^2:=-\langle g_k,p_k\rangle=g_k^TH_k^{-1}g_k>0.$$
3. Before line search, if $\lambda_k^2/2\le\varepsilon$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{decrement})$. This is the Newton-decrement stopping test.
4. Start with $t=1$ and repeatedly replace $t$ by $\beta t$ until
   $x_k+t p_k\in U$ and
   $f(x_k+t p_k)\le f(x_k)+\alpha t\,\langle g_k,p_k\rangle$.
5. Set $x_{k+1}:=x_k+t p_k$ and continue at iteration $k+1$.

The Cholesky factor exists and is unique when the symmetric Hessian is positive
definite by
[[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]].
Its positive diagonal makes both triangular solves unique. The backtracking
branch terminates whenever it is reached, since $g_k\ne0$ and $H_k$ is
positive definite, by
[[lem-armijo-backtracking-terminates-for-strict-descent-directions]]. This
procedure makes no global-optimality claim.

Definition

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$ ([[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]) with Jacobian $J_F$ as in
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. The matrix of $DF(x)$ in the standard
basis is $J_F(x)$ by
[[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Define
the residual merit
$\Phi(x):=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2$. **Inputs:** $x_0\in U$, residual tolerance
$\varepsilon\ge0$, update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$, sufficient-decrease
parameter $\alpha\in(0,1)$, reduction factor $\beta\in(0,1)$, and finite
backtrack budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$. **Output:** the last valid iterate and one
of `root`, `singular-jacobian`, `invalid-trial`, `line-search-exhausted`, or
`iteration-budget-exhausted`.

At iteration $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, apply these instructions in order:

1. Evaluate $F(x_k)$. If $\|F(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{root})$. This status records the residual test only.
2. If $k=N$, return $(x_k,\texttt{iteration-budget-exhausted})$.
3. Call [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]] with
   $A=J_F(x_k)$ and $r=F(x_k)$. If it returns `singular-jacobian`, return
   that status. Otherwise let $s_k$ be its correction.
4. For $j=0,1,\ldots,B$, set $t=\beta^j$ and trial $y=x_k+t s_k$. If
   $y\notin U$, reject the trial and continue. If $y\in U$, evaluate
   $\Phi(y)$ and accept the first trial satisfying
   $$\Phi(y)\le\Phi(x_k)-\alpha t\|F(x_k)\|_2^2.$$
   On acceptance set $x_{k+1}=y$ and continue at iteration $k+1$.
5. If no trial was accepted, return `invalid-trial` if every tested point was
   outside $U$; otherwise return `line-search-exhausted`.

The residual-merit test is defined directly for a vector root problem. A finite
backtrack budget can return failure; no global convergence or quadratic-rate
claim is made.

Input a finite-dimensional $C^1$ map $G(z,\theta)$, a $C^1$ initial-state map $z_0(\theta)$, a parameter $\theta$ in an open subset of $\mathbb R^p$, and an integer budget $K\ge0$; the states lie in $\mathbb R^m$, with $p,m\ge0$. Evaluate $z_0(\theta)$ and then $z_{k+1}(\theta)=G(z_k(\theta),\theta)$ for $k=0,\ldots,K-1$. A primitive-domain failure returns DOMAIN_ERROR; a branch boundary or ambiguous active branch returns NONDIFFERENTIABLE and no derivative. The admissible case requires every evaluation to remain in its declared domain and, for piecewise primitives, on a unique strict active branch.

Allocate an $m\times p$ Jacobian array $J$. For each state coordinate $a=1,\ldots,m$, form the finite scalar-output graph for $f_a(\theta)=(z_K(\theta))_a$ by appending the coordinate projection to the finite recursion. For each parameter coordinate $\ell=1,\ldots,p$, call [[alg-forward-mode-automatic-differentiation]] on this graph at $\theta$ with direction $e_\ell$, the $\ell$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^p$, and put its returned tangent in $J_{a\ell}$. Propagate any DOMAIN_ERROR or NONDIFFERENTIABLE status from a call. Return $(z_K(\theta),J)$ with status ITERATES_DIFFERENTIATED. For $K=0$ the recursion contains only the initial-state map. If $m=0$ or $p=0$, the corresponding loops are empty and $J$ has the specified empty shape; the primal recursion is still evaluated. This procedure differentiates the $K$-step map actually specified by $G,z_0,K$; it does not substitute the derivative of an exact fixed point.

Input a quadratic trust-region model of
[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]] with positive-definite $B$
([[def-definite-and-indefinite-hessian-quadratic-forms]]) and radius
$\Delta>0$. If $g=0$, return $p=0$ with status `stationary`. Otherwise
compute the Cauchy step $p_C$ by [[alg-trust-region-cauchy-step]] and the
Newton-model step $p_N$ by solving $Bp_N=-g$.

1. If $\|p_N\|_2\le\Delta$, return $p_N$.
2. If $\|p_C\|_2=\Delta$, return $p_C$.
3. Otherwise put $d:=p_N-p_C$, $a:=\|d\|_2^2$,
   $b:=2\langle p_C,d\rangle$, and $c:=\|p_C\|_2^2-\Delta^2<0$. Compute
   $$t:=\frac{-b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}.$$
   Set $p_D:=p_C+td$, the boundary intersection on the segment from the
   Cauchy step to the Newton-model step.
4. Compare the two model values. Return $p_D$ if $m(p_D)\le m(p_C)$ and
   return $p_C$ otherwise.

The status is `step` in the nonstationary branches.

Definition

Assume AC and the Brownian conventions of
[[def-locally-lipschitz-ito-sde-and-maximal-solution]] on $[0,T]$ with
$U=\mathbb R^d$. An admissible mathematical input has finite dimensions
$d,m\ge1$, $T>0$, $N\ge1$ with $h=T/N\le1$, an autonomous continuous drift
$b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$, a finite-valued Borel diffusion
$\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$, and a finite
$\mathcal F_0$-measurable initial state $\xi$. It also has a constant
$\mu\ge0$ such that
$$\langle x-y,b(x)-b(y)\rangle\le-\mu|x-y|^2\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^d).$$
This global condition is a precondition on the mathematical input, not a
runtime test over all $x,y$. For $h>0$, set $H_h(x)=x-hb(x)$ and let
$R_h=H_h^{-1}$, which is defined uniquely on all of $\mathbb R^d$ by
[[thm-backward-euler-dissipative-resolvent-contraction]].

First check that $d,m$ are positive integers, $T$ is finite and positive,
$N$ is a positive integer, $0<h=T/N\le1$, and $\xi$ is finite. If any of
these checks fails, return `invalid-input`. An exact execution then sets
$Y_0=\xi$ and, for $n=0,\ldots,N-1$, computes
$$u_n=Y_n+\sigma(Y_n)(W_{t_{n+1}}-W_{t_n}),\qquad Y_{n+1}=R_h(u_n).$$
It returns the grid values, the left-endpoint step process
$$\bar Y_t=Y_n\quad(t_n\le t<t_{n+1}),\qquad \bar Y_T=Y_N,$$
and the continuous interpolation
$$Y_t=Y_n+(t-t_n)b(Y_{n+1})+\sigma(Y_n)(W_t-W_{t_n}), \qquad t_n\le t\le t_{n+1}.$$
This is a pathwise continuous extension of the grid values. At each shared
endpoint the interpolation agrees with the grid update.

A finite implementation may instead receive a root-solver interface $S$ and
an integer work cap $M\ge0$. Each call $S(H_h,u_n,M)$ must terminate after at
most $M$ declared solver iterations and return either
`certified-root(z, proof)` or `no-certificate(last-iterate, residual)` (with
`last-iterate = null` if the cap permits no iterate). The
supplied exact verifier must terminate and accepts a certificate precisely when it proves that
$z\in\mathbb R^d$ is finite and $H_h(z)=u_n$. At the first call returning
`no-certificate`, or at the first certificate rejected by the verifier, stop
and return `solve-failure` with zero-based failed index $n$, the valid grid prefix through
$Y_n$, the step process on $[0,t_n]$, the interpolation on $[0,t_n]$, and the
solver diagnostic. For `no-certificate`, retain its last iterate and residual;
for a rejected certificate with candidate $z$, report $z$ and residual
$H_h(z)-u_n$. If the diagnostic has no finite candidate, its iterate and
residual are null. Do not assign $Y_{n+1}$ or continue. A
verified root equals $R_h(u_n)$ by uniqueness. If every call is verified,
return `success` and the exact grid, step process, and interpolation above.
The global dissipativity condition remains an admissibility precondition and
is not tested by these finite-value checks. Thus a failed finite solve records
failure of certification, not absence of a mathematical root.
The algorithm makes no convergence or mean-square stability claim.

Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice as in the finite-dimensional Gaussian and Brownian
interfaces. Let $m\ge1$ be a finite integer. A node represents an interval
$[u,u+h]$, where $h>0$, and has an already sampled parent increment
$\Delta W\in\mathbb R^m$. Draw a fresh
vector $Z\sim N_m(0,(h/4)I_m)$ independently of the parent and of every
innovation used at another node. Store the two child increments
$$\Delta W_L=\tfrac12\Delta W+Z,\qquad \Delta W_R=\tfrac12\Delta W-Z.$$

For a finite ordered list of $q\in\mathbb N_0$ split requests, each naming an
existing leaf, apply the rule once to each requested leaf and retain every
parent. Process a rejected trial's left child before its right child; if a
child is later refined, draw a new independent innovation for it. Each request
replaces one leaf by two children, so the result is a finite rooted tree with
the sampled increments, interval lengths, and left-to-right order. Never
discard a sampled parent and redraw a replacement for the same interval. The
procedure assigns increments at dyadic tree nodes; it does not by itself
define values at nondyadic times or prove that the node-selection rule is
predictable. In an adaptive run, a finite work budget supplies a finite list
of requests.

Conditional on a fixed parent, the child sum is fixed and their conditional
cross-covariance is $-(h/4)I_m$, so they are not conditionally independent.
The exact unconditional Brownian increment laws at fixed dyadic depth are
proved separately on the A page; this procedure makes no law claim for a
data-dependent set of requested leaves.

Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice and use the finite-dimensional Brownian-motion
convention of [[def-d-dimensional-brownian-motion]]. Let the state dimension
$d$ and noise dimension $m$ be positive finite integers, and fix $T>0$ and
$N\in\mathbb N$ with $N\ge1$. Set $h=T/N>0$ and $t_k=kh$ for
$0\le k\le N$. Let
$b:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$\sigma:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be jointly Borel.
Write $|\cdot|$ for the Euclidean norm and $\|\cdot\|_F$ for the Frobenius
norm. Suppose finite constants $L,K$ satisfy, for every $s,t\in[0,T]$ and
$x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|b(t,x)-b(t,y)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(t,y)\|_F\le L|x-y|,$$
$$|b(t,x)|^2+\|\sigma(t,x)\|_F^2\le K^2(1+|x|^2),$$
and
$$|b(t,x)-b(s,x)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(s,x)\|_F\le K(1+|x|)|t-s|^{1/2}.$$
Let $W$ be an adapted standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion on a filtered
probability space, with $W_t-W_s$ independent of $\mathcal F_s$ and law
$N_m(0,(t-s)I_m)$ whenever $0\le s<t\le T$. Let $X_0$ be
$\mathcal F_0$-measurable, independent of future Brownian increments, and
$\mathbb E|X_0|^2<\infty$.

The **Euler–Maruyama algorithm** takes these data as input and returns
$Y_0,\ldots,Y_N$:

1. Set $Y_0=X_0$.
2. For $k=0,\ldots,N-1$, form $\Delta W_k=W_{t_{k+1}}-W_{t_k}$ and set
   $$Y_{k+1}=Y_k+b(t_k,Y_k)h+\sigma(t_k,Y_k)\Delta W_k.$$

The output is the grid approximation for the coefficient pair $(b,\sigma)$.
The companion step-process and interpolation definition uses this same grid
and endpoint convention.

Definition

Assume AC. Fix finite integers $d,m\ge1$, $T>0$, and $N\ge1$ such that
$h=T/N\le1$. Work on a filtered probability space whose filtration is
right-continuous and contains every $P$-null subset of $\mathcal F$ in
$\mathcal F_0$. Let $W$ be an adapted standard
$m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments after time $s$ are
independent of $\mathcal F_s$. Let $X_0$ be finite, $\mathcal F_0$-measurable,
and independent of $\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$.
Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be $C^1$. Assume finite constants
$\mu,c,D\ge0$ and an integer $q\ge1$ satisfy, for all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$\langle x-y,f(x)-f(y)\rangle\le\mu|x-y|^2,\qquad \|g(x)-g(y)\|_F^2\le c|x-y|^2,$$
$$|f(x)-f(y)|^2\le D(1+|x|^q+|y|^q)|x-y|^2.$$
Here $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm and $\|\cdot\|_F$ is the Frobenius
norm.

Set $t_k=kh$ and construct the grid approximation recursively by
$$Y_0=X_0,\qquad Y_{k+1}=Y_k+f(Y_k)h+g(Y_k)(W_{t_{k+1}}-W_{t_k}),\quad 0\le k<N.$$
The output also includes the left-endpoint step process
$$\bar Y_t=Y_k\quad(t_k\le t<t_{k+1}),\qquad \bar Y_T=Y_N,$$
and the continuous interpolation
$$Y_t=Y_k+f(Y_k)(t-t_k)+g(Y_k)(W_t-W_{t_k})\quad(t_k\le t\le t_{k+1}).$$
The recursion makes the two interpolation formulas agree at every shared
endpoint. The finite recursion is defined pathwise: $C^1$ coefficients are
finite-valued, each $Y_k$ is finite almost surely by induction, and Brownian
paths are continuous. This algorithm defines no moment or convergence claim.

Definition

**Inputs.** A dimension $d\ge1$; $P\ge2$ spheres with centers $q_i$, velocities
$v_i$, masses $m_i>0$, radii $r_i>0$ and fixed restitution coefficients
$e_{ij}\in[0,1]$; an initial state and horizon $T>0$; a positive time-bracket
tolerance $\epsilon_{\rm time}$, a separate positive guard-residual tolerance
$\epsilon_{\rm guard}$, an event-separation bound $\delta>0$, a certified
finite event-count bound $N_{\rm evt}\in\mathbb N$, an event budget
$B\in\mathbb N$, an endpoint policy $\pi_T\in\{\texttt{include},\texttt{pre-impact}\}$,
and a finite-budget certificate provider. The exact smooth-mode reference dynamics are
$$q_i'=v_i,\qquad v_i'=F_i(t,q,v),$$
where $F=(F_1,\ldots,F_P)$ is a specified $C^1$ force field on an open
neighborhood of an admitted compact tube. The exact reference initial state is
nonpenetrating: $\gamma_{ij}(0):=\|q_i(0)-q_j(0)\|_2-r_i-r_j\ge0$ for every
pair. A completed provider must certify that the exact reference states remain
nonpenetrating on each smooth segment and after every exact reset; a failed or
undecidable nonpenetration check returns `unresolved`. Throughout each certified
incoming/outgoing tube every pair distance is at least a stated $\sigma>0$.
The provider supplies finite relative-velocity bounds $V$ and state/field bounds
wherever they are used below.

The provider is an explicit admissible input, not an automatically constructed
oracle for arbitrary $C^1$ fields. It must supply the following valid data,
with any failed or undecidable certificate test returning `unresolved`.

1. From the last reported reset, a continuous accumulated dense reconstruction
   $U$ and a certified uniform error $\eta_{\rm loc}$ relative to the exact
   smooth-mode solution launched from that reported state. It also supplies
   a bound $E$ on the discrepancy from the reference hybrid trajectory at
   the same aligned segment-start time, initially $E=0$. On a common mode
   prefix of duration $H$, supply a state-Lipschitz constant $L$ and the common
   solution/tube hypotheses of [[lem-ode-flow-lipschitz-on-a-tube]], and use
   $\eta_{\rm ref}=\eta_{\rm loc}+e^{LH}E$. A finite cover of certified
   convex mode tubes may be used with its propagated bounds. A Jacobian bound
   on a nonconvex compact set alone is not a substitute for these hypotheses.

2. For every pair $i<j$, exact-reference guard enclosures for
   $\gamma_{ij}(t)=\|q_i(t)-q_j(t)\|_2-r_i-r_j$, and a certificate covering
   the whole interval since the last processed event that proves
   $\gamma_{ij}\ge0$ throughout and accounts for every possible zero. Every
   zero is either the just-processed segment-start root for that pair (which may
   be ignored once) or a candidate root bracket satisfying item 3; any other
   possible zero, including a grazing or zero-speed zero, or any possible
   negative guard value returns `unresolved`. At the initial simulation time, a
   zero must be processed as an enabled incoming root or the result is
   `unresolved`. Thus a no-event result requires certified nonpenetration and
   exclusion of every unlisted zero over the whole interval, not merely
   exclusion of incoming roots. A sufficient explicit sampling assumption may
   replace a range cover only when its stated variation/domain assumptions
   justify the same exclusion. Endpoint signs or an unsuccessful sign scan
   alone do not certify absence. Dense-guard enclosures must include the
   state-error inflation $\sqrt2\eta_{\rm ref}$ as well as guard-evaluation
   and rounding error; the bound follows from
   [[lem-sphere-contact-guard-normal-and-reset-lipschitz-bounds]].

3. For each candidate event, a bracket $[a,b]$ containing exactly one root
   $\tau$ of the exact reference guard, with
   $b-a\le\epsilon_{\rm time}$ and $b-a<\delta/3$. On the entire bracket,
   certify the incoming inequality
   $\dot\gamma_{ij}(t)\le-\nu<0$, not just a derivative value at its root.
   Supply disjoint ordering certificates identifying the unique earliest
   event among all pairs. If $b=T$, certify whether the exact root is $\tau=T$;
   an undecided endpoint equality returns `unresolved`. A grazing/uncertain derivative, ambiguous overlap
   or simultaneous multi-contact is unresolved; lexicographic inspection
   does not settle physical simultaneous impacts.

4. At $\widehat\tau=b$, a certified bound
   $\epsilon_{\rm obs}\ge|\gamma_{ij}(\widehat\tau,U(\widehat\tau))|$
   with $\epsilon_{\rm obs}\le\epsilon_{\rm guard}$. The provider includes
   all evaluation errors in this bound. The actual lag is nonnegative and
   bounded by
   $$\Delta:=\min\left\{b-a,\frac{\sqrt2\eta_{\rm ref}+\epsilon_{\rm obs}}{\nu}\right\}$$
   by [[lem-transverse-hybrid-event-time-error]]. Require certified bounds
   $M^-,M^+$ for the incoming/outgoing fields through this lag, and reset
   domain/tube checks. For the selected pair use the state-reset bound $L_R$
   from [[lem-sphere-contact-guard-normal-and-reset-lipschitz-bounds]], with
   a velocity bound valid for both compared reset inputs. This reset has no
   explicit time dependence. If the reset formula is evaluated inexactly, the
   computed full-state output $\widehat R(U(b))$ must come with a separate
   $\epsilon_R\ge0$ satisfying
   $\|\widehat R(U(b))-R(U(b))\|_2\le\epsilon_R$, where the norm is on the
   full state $(q,v)$; for an exact reset set $\epsilon_R=0$.

5. A certificate that the matched isolated exact events have separation at
   least $\delta$ and count at most $N_{\rm evt}$ under the input endpoint
   policy. For an exact event at $T$, policy `include` processes the reset and
   counts it; policy `pre-impact` reports the endpoint before reset and excludes
   that endpoint event from the processed-event count. Process an initial enabled root at most once. Missing
   endpoint/count/separation bookkeeping is unresolved. In particular $e=0$
   does not establish another isolated transverse event after the reset.

**Procedure.** Request these certificates for every unordered pair on each
smooth segment, inspecting the pair list in increasing lexicographic order.
If the provider certifies no further zero except the permitted just-processed
segment-start root, with nonpenetration and no unlisted zero through the chosen
horizon endpoint, return that segment, its accumulated error bound and its
certificates. Otherwise
select the certified unique earliest pair and use its upper bracket endpoint
$\widehat\tau=b$. If the provider certifies $\tau=T$ and $\pi_T=\texttt{pre-impact}$,
return the certified trajectory ending at $T$ before reset. In every other
event case, evaluate the binary impulse formula of
[[thm-frictionless-sphere-binary-impact-impulse-laws]] as the smooth reset
extension at $U(b)$; keep positions fixed and update only the selected two
velocities. The impulse theorem's exact contact/momentum/restitution/energy
laws concern the reference exact incoming contact. A reported approximate
state is not asserted to be exactly at contact; its reset error is recorded.

By [[lem-reset-error-after-a-mistimed-hybrid-event]], set the next aligned
reset-state error bound to
$$E\leftarrow L_R\eta_{\rm ref}+(L_RM^-+M^+)\Delta+\epsilon_R.$$
The outgoing $M^+\Delta$ term accounts for the reference trajectory's flow
from its earlier true reset to the reported time. Restart the smooth integrator
at $b$ with the reported reset state, discard the previous local reconstruction,
and start the next accumulated dense-error ledger. These recurrences compare
only matched smooth-mode prefixes and post-reset states at aligned times; they
make no same-clock state-error assertion between an exact jump and its later
reported jump.

Stop at $T$ or after $B$ accepted events. If another event is required after
the budget, return `unresolved` with the certified partial trajectory. A
completed run requires $B\ge N_{\rm evt}$ or a certified no-further-event result
before the budget is exhausted. Any missing enclosure, margin, ordering,
separation/count or restart certificate, failed reset domain, or depleted
provider budget returns `unresolved` without an event-absence claim.

The search enumerates $P(P-1)/2$ pairs per smooth segment. Root-solve guard
evaluations, dense reintegration and restart-error calculation are charged
separately from one inspection per pair. No neighbor-search acceleration,
frictional solver, or simultaneous-contact solver is specified.

Definition

This is an ideal one-step line-search oracle that uses the negative-gradient direction of [[alg-gradient-descent]] and replaces only its step-selection rule. It is not a second definition of the gradient-descent iteration.

**Inputs:** an open convex set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, a $C^2$ objective $f:U\to\mathbb R$, an initial point $x_0\in U$ whose sublevel set $K:=\{y\in U:f(y)\le f(x_0)\}$ is compact, and a current point $x\in K$. **Admissible conditions:** for some $0<m\le M$, there is a convex open set $V\subseteq U$ containing $K$ on which the Hessian satisfies $mI\preceq H_f(y)\preceq MI$. **Output:** if $\nabla f(x)=0$, return $(x,\texttt{stationary})$. Otherwise set $g:=\nabla f(x)$ and return $(x-t_*g,\texttt{exact-step})$, where $t_*$ is the unique minimizer of $t\mapsto f(x-tg)$ over all $t\ge0$ with $x-tg\in U$. The set $K$ is nonempty because $x_0\in K$, and the continuous restriction $f|_K$ attains a minimum at some $x^*\in K$ by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]. Every $y\in U\setminus K$ satisfies $f(y)>f(x_0)\ge f(x^*)$, so $x^*$ is an attained global minimizer of $f$ on $U$. Thus the algorithm inputs supply the minimizer premise of [[thm-exact-line-search-gradient-descent-global-contraction]], whose remaining hypotheses are stated above.

The minimization is an exact real-valued oracle; this definition gives no finite evaluation procedure or floating-point accuracy claim. A finite implementation must report its own search status and error bounds.

Definition

Let $F_A(z)=0$ be the active KKT system of a finite-dimensional reduced FE control problem, where $z=(x,\mu)$ stacks the control and active multipliers. Given $z_0$, an ordered finite list of proposed active sets $A_0,\ldots,A_{m-1}$, maximum budget $N\ge1$, residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a terminating exact-storage routine satisfying the input contract of [[alg-sqp-finite-precision-kkt-qr-solve-and-residual-check]], and the floating-point hypotheses of [[alg-sqp-finite-precision-kkt-qr-solve-and-residual-check]], process at most $\min(m,N)$ candidates:

1. For candidate $A_j$, form $F_{A_j}(z_j)$ and its exact-Hessian active KKT Jacobian $K_j=DF_{A_j}(z_j)$.
2. Use the active KKT-map/Jacobian convention and rank/reduced-curvature applicability conditions of [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]]. Do not invoke its exact linear solve. Set $b_j=-F_{A_j}(z_j)$ and call [[alg-sqp-finite-precision-kkt-qr-solve-and-residual-check]] exactly once on the intended system $K_js=b_j$, supplying the terminating exact-storage routine. Before numerical factorization or residual evaluation, that call must verify stored entries equal to the intended $K_j,b_j$; unavailable or unverified admission is a failed QR solve with no residual certificate. A failed applicability check or QR solve records `numerical-failure`, sets $z_{j+1}=z_j$, and proceeds.
3. On a successful QR return, let $(\widehat s_j,\eta_j)$ be its step vector and residual bound. Set $z_j^+=z_j+\widehat s_j$ and $z_{j+1}=z_j^+$. The QR vector $\widehat s_j$ is the only step used by this wrapper. If $\eta_j\le\tau$, return $(z_j^+,A_j,\texttt{active-kkt-residual-certified},\eta_j)$; otherwise proceed.

If the finite list or budget is exhausted, return `budget-exhausted` with the smallest successfully computed residual bound, or `inconclusive` if no solve succeeded. This status concerns the active KKT equation residual only. Box feasibility, multiplier signs, global optimality, and forward accuracy require separate validated checks; none follows from a small linear-system residual alone.

Definition

Let $U_h\subset U=L^2(E)$ be the finite-dimensional space of cellwise-constant controls on a finite affine mesh, and let $Q_h=U_h\cap Q_{ad}$ be nonempty with bounds constant on each control cell. The target is the **exact continuous reduced objective** $\widehat J$ of [[def-linear-elliptic-pde-constrained-control-problem]], restricted to $Q_h$; write $Ju(q)=c+Sq$ and $g(q)=\nabla\widehat J(q)=B^*p(q)+\alpha q$. Choose a certified $L_h\ge\|S|_{U_h}\|^2+\alpha>0$. Given a finite budget $N\ge1$, tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and initial $q_0\in Q_h$, repeat for $k=0,\ldots,N-1$:

An additional input is a residual-evaluation routine $\mathcal C$. For every queried $q_k$, it must return in finite time either a valid tuple $(\tilde u_k,\tilde p_k,\varepsilon_{u,k},\varepsilon_{p,k})$ or `failure`. A valid tuple has $\tilde u_k,\tilde p_k\in V_h$, nonnegative finite bounds that dominate the complete primal and adjoint first-Strang right-hand sides, and an adjoint load defect that includes the state-error contribution $\|J\|^2\varepsilon_{u,k}$. The finite-return condition is part of the algorithm's admissible input contract.

A second input is a projection-evaluation routine $\mathcal P$. Write $q_{k,K}:=q_k|_K$. For every queried $(q_k,\tilde p_k,L_h)$ it must return in finite time either `failure` or finite real cell values $z_{k,K}$ and a finite real $r_k\ge0$ satisfying
$$z_{k,K}=\operatorname{clip}_{[q_a|_K,q_b|_K]}\left(q_{k,K}-\frac{\alpha q_{k,K}+|K|^{-1}\int_K B^*\tilde p_k}{L_h}\right),\qquad r_k^2=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T_h}|K|\,|q_{k,K}-z_{k,K}|^2.$$
Thus the returned cellwise function is exactly $P_{Q_h}(q_k-\tilde g_k/L_h)$ and $r_k$ is its exact step norm by [[lem-p0-box-projection-is-clipped-cell-average]]. Computing the required cell averages, clipped values and norm is part of this finite-return backend contract; it is not inferred from boundedness of $B$, and no finite representation of the entire function $B^*\tilde p_k$ is assumed. Unavailable exact values must be reported as `failure`, not left pending.

1. Call $\mathcal C(q_k)$. If it returns `failure` or no valid bounds, return $(q_k,\texttt{inconclusive},+\infty)$. Otherwise use its conforming finite-element state and adjoint approximations $\tilde u_k,\tilde p_k$ and complete Strang bounds $\varepsilon_{u,k},\varepsilon_{p,k}$, including form, geometry, quadrature, and load defects. Set $\delta_k=\|B\|\varepsilon_{p,k}$ and $\tilde g_k=B^*\tilde p_k+\alpha q_k$.
2. Call $\mathcal P(q_k,\tilde p_k,L_h)$. If it returns `failure` or no valid cell values and norm, return $(q_k,\texttt{inconclusive},+\infty)$. Otherwise set $\tilde q_{k+1}|_K=z_{k,K}$ and $\tilde\rho_k=r_k$ from its valid return.
3. If $\tilde\rho_k+\delta_k/L_h\le\tau$, return $(q_k,\texttt{certified},\tilde\rho_k+\delta_k/L_h)$.
4. Otherwise set $q_{k+1}=\tilde q_{k+1}$ and continue.

Let $U,V$ be as in [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** $x_0\in U$, a unit vector $v_0$, finite-difference distance $\epsilon>0$, force-evaluation error bound $\eta\ge0$, rotation step $\alpha>0$, rotation tolerance $\tau_{\rm rot}\ge0$, force tolerance $\tau_F\ge0$, rotation cap $J\in\mathbb N_0$, translation step $\sigma>0$, and translation cap $K\in\mathbb N_0$. Return the last point, direction, reported residuals, and a status from `force-tolerance`, `mode-unverified`, `rotation-cap`, `translation-cap`, `geometry-failure`, `rotation-failure`, or `nonfinite-evaluation`.

Initialize the translation-update counter $k=0$, the current point $x=x_0$, and the current unit direction $v=v_0$. At each translation iteration, start with the current $v$, set the rotation-update counter $j=0$, and repeat the following residual test and possible update:

1. If $x\pm\epsilon v\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`. Evaluate approximate gradients $\widehat g_\pm$ at $x\pm\epsilon v$ with the declared error bound, and form $D_\epsilon=(\widehat g_+-\widehat g_-)/(2\epsilon)$. Nonfinite data return `nonfinite-evaluation`.
2. Set $r_{\rm rot}=\|(I-vv^T)D_\epsilon\|_2$. If $r_{\rm rot}\le\tau_{\rm rot}$, end this rotation loop. If the test fails and $j=J$, return `rotation-cap` with the last direction. Otherwise set $w=v-\alpha(I-vv^T)D_\epsilon$. If $w=0$, return `rotation-failure`; else replace $v$ by $w/\|w\|_2$, set $j\leftarrow j+1$, and repeat the rotation test.

Thus $J$ counts direction updates, and the current direction is tested before the cap is returned, including when $J=0$. A small rotational residual by itself does not certify that the direction is the lowest eigenmode. If no validated spectral-gap or mode-tracking certificate is supplied, label the mode status `mode-unverified`.

After a rotation residual passes, evaluate $\widehat g(x)$ with error at most $\eta$. If it is nonfinite, return `nonfinite-evaluation`. If $\|\widehat g(x)\|_2\le\tau_F$, return `force-tolerance` together with the mode status. If $k=K$, return `translation-cap`; perform an update only when $k<K$.

$$x^+=x+\sigma\bigl[-\widehat g(x)+2(\widehat g(x)^Tv)v\bigr].$$

If $x^+\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`; otherwise set $x\leftarrow x^+$, set $k\leftarrow k+1$, and begin the next translation iteration. Thus $K$ counts translation updates; the force-tolerance test is made before the cap test, including when $K=0$. This finite procedure makes no arbitrary-start, termination, saddle-convergence, or global-transition claim.

Let $p\ge1$, let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty candidate set, and let $f_x\in\mathbb R^p$ be the feature vector for each $x\in\mathcal X$. An approximate design $\xi$ and information matrix $M(\xi)=\sum_x\xi_xf_xf_x^T$ use the convention of [[def-approximate-linear-model-design-and-optimality-criteria]]. The same vectors may be scalar-observation sensitivities at a fixed parameter, as in [[def-nonlinear-experimental-design-and-local-identifiability]], with a scalar precision absorbed into $f_x$. The procedure uses exact arithmetic.

**Input:** A finite nonempty $\mathcal X$, $p\ge1$, its feature vectors $(f_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$, an approximate initial design $\xi^{(0)}$, and a finite nonnegative integer budget $N$ counting weight updates.

**Procedure:** Form $M_0=M(\xi^{(0)})$. If $M_0$ is not positive definite, return $(\xi^{(0)},\text{undefined violation},\text{invalid initial design})$. Otherwise, for $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, with current $\xi^{(k)}$ and $M_k=M(\xi^{(k)})$, compute
$$s_x^{(k)}=f_x^TM_k^{-1}f_x\quad(x\in\mathcal X),\qquad v_k=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}s_x^{(k)}-p.$$
If $v_k=0$, return $(\xi^{(k)},v_k,\text{equivalence-certified})$. If $k=N$, return $(\xi^{(k)},v_k,\text{budget-exhausted})$. Otherwise set
$$\xi_x^{(k+1)}=\xi_x^{(k)}\frac{s_x^{(k)}}p\quad(x\in\mathcal X),$$
form $M_{k+1}=\sum_x\xi_x^{(k+1)}f_xf_x^T$, and continue. The proved update invariant keeps every later $M_k$ positive definite.

The budget guarantees at most $N$ updates and $N+1$ sensitivity scans. A nonzero returned violation is reported as-is; it is not an exact D-optimality certificate. The exact integer allocation problem remains separate from this approximate-weight procedure.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$ ([[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]) with Jacobian $J_F$ as in
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. The matrix of $DF(x)$ in the standard
basis is $J_F(x)$ by
[[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].
**Inputs:** $x_0\in U$, residual
tolerance $\varepsilon\ge0$, and update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$.
**Output:** the last valid iterate and one of `root`, `singular-jacobian`,
`invalid-trial`, or `iteration-budget-exhausted`.

For $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, in this order:

1. Compute $F(x_k)$. If $\|F(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{root})$. Here `root` means the residual tolerance was met; it
   does not certify an exact zero when $\varepsilon>0$.
2. If $k=N$, return $(x_k,\texttt{iteration-budget-exhausted})$.
3. Call [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]] with
   $A=J_F(x_k)$ and $r=F(x_k)$. If it returns `singular-jacobian`, return that
   status.
4. Let $s_k$ be its correction. If $x_k+s_k\notin U$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{invalid-trial})$. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$.

It makes no arbitrary-start, global-convergence, or discretization-error claim.

The input state is consistent, $(q,p)\in\mathcal M$. For $h=0$, return $(q,p)$ with status `exact-identity`. For nonzero $h$, fix a compact phase subset $C\subset\mathcal M$ over a compact regular configuration chart with $(q,p)\in C$ and $0<|h|<h_0(C)$, using branch balls $U_q,U_p$ supplied by [[lem-rattle-scaled-position-and-momentum-branches]]. The admissible inputs also include initial guesses $\lambda_{\mathrm{init}}\in U_q$, $\mu_{\mathrm{init}}\in U_p$, tolerances $\varepsilon_q,\varepsilon_p\ge0$, finite correction budgets $N_q,N_p\in\mathbb N_0$, and terminating exact factorization/solve backends $\mathcal B_q,\mathcal B_p$ for the two chord calls. Each backend accepts a square $m\times m$ Jacobian, returns a singularity report exactly when it is singular, and otherwise returns a retained factor object. For every right-hand side, solving on this object terminates with the exact unique solution for that matrix; factorization and retained-factor solves are separate operations, as in [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]]. All evaluations of $c,J,\nabla V$ and the displayed matrix operations in the updates, residual and exact residual-Jacobian evaluations, arithmetic, Euclidean norm evaluation/comparison, and domain-membership tests are returning primitives; no bound on their internal cost is specified. The multiplier domains $U_q,U_p\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ are open balls within the regular branch neighborhoods. Choose the balls so that $F_q$ is $C^1$ on $U_q$ and, for every $\lambda\in U_q$, the corresponding $F_p$ is $C^1$ on $U_p$ and all evaluations in the updates are defined and the corresponding positions remain in the ambient full-row-rank configuration region of the branch lemma. Inconsistent input, missing branch balls, or maps not defined on these domains are outside the algorithm's admissible inputs. On success the routine returns the approximate state, both multipliers, and both scaled residual norms; on failure it returns the residual solver's status, last valid multiplier iterate, and actual scaled residual norm, together with any position-stage values already computed.

1. Form
$$F_q(\lambda)=h^{-2}c\!\left(q+hM^{-1}\left(p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\lambda\right)\right).$$
Run [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]] on $F_q$ in chord mode with refresh period $1$, domain $U_q$, initial value $\lambda_{\mathrm{init}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_q$, budget $N_q$, and backend $\mathcal B_q$. If it returns anything other than `root`, return its exact status (`iteration-budget-exhausted`, `singular-jacobian`, or `invalid-trial`), last valid multiplier iterate, and actual scaled residual norm; do not continue.

2. For its returned $\widetilde\lambda$, compute $\widetilde p_{1/2}=p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\widetilde\lambda$ and $\widetilde q_1=q+hM^{-1}\widetilde p_{1/2}$. Form
$$F_p(\mu)=h^{-1}J(\widetilde q_1)M^{-1}\left(\widetilde p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(\widetilde q_1)-hJ(\widetilde q_1)^T\mu\right).$$
Run the same supplier procedure on $F_p$ in chord mode with refresh period $1$, domain $U_p$, initial value $\mu_{\mathrm{init}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_p$, budget $N_p$, and backend $\mathcal B_p$. If it returns anything other than `root`, return its exact status (`iteration-budget-exhausted`, `singular-jacobian`, or `invalid-trial`), last valid multiplier iterate, actual scaled tangency residual norm, and the successful position-stage values; do not continue.

3. If both calls meet their residual tolerances, set
$$\widetilde p_1=\widetilde p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(\widetilde q_1)-hJ(\widetilde q_1)^T\widetilde\mu$$
and return $(\widetilde q_1,\widetilde p_1,\widetilde\lambda,\widetilde\mu)$, the norms $\|F_q(\widetilde\lambda)\|_2$, $\|F_p(\widetilde\mu)\|_2$, and status “residual tolerances met”.

For nonzero $h$, leaving a branch ball returns `invalid-trial`, a singular factorization returns `singular-jacobian`, and exhausting either correction budget returns `iteration-budget-exhausted`; the supplier supplies the last valid iterate and its evaluated residual norm in each case. No undefined-evaluation status is needed because the admissible domains require all evaluations to be defined. A successful output with nonzero residuals need not lie in $\mathcal M$; applying the routine again requires a consistent input, for example one restored by [[lem-regular-holonomic-phase-residuals-control-distance-to-phase-manifold]]. The supplier status `root` means only that its stated residual tolerance was met; it does not certify an exact root or a forward-error bound. No finite budget is claimed to succeed on every admissible input.
