Definition

Input a candidate list $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_M)$, a horizon parameter $N$, an initial-list length $s$, a real-mean candidate $m$, a kernel candidate $k$, an observation-variance candidate $\sigma^2$, acquisition-coefficient candidates $b_t$, an initial data list $(x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^s$, an observation oracle $O$, and a deterministic candidate-selection routine. First validate that $X$ is nonempty, finite and ordered, $N$ and $s$ are integers with $N\ge0$ and $0\le s\le N$, every initial site lies in $X$, all mean, kernel, noise, coefficient and observation values are finite reals, the kernel matrix on $X$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, $\sigma^2\ge0$, and every $b_t\ge0$. If any validation fails, return inadmissible-model before computing a posterior. The observation oracle must finish each call in finite time and return either a finite real observation or observation-unavailable. For a true-posterior interpretation, the initial sites are fixed before their observations and each observation is $f(x_i)+\xi_i$ under this model, with errors independent centered Gaussian variables of variance $\sigma^2$ and independent of the entire process. Otherwise the procedure computes only the all-data-vector posterior kernel for the specified surrogate and makes no claim that it is the conditional law of an externally supplied data-generating process. The Axiom of Choice is included as required by [[thm-finite-gaussian-process-posterior-and-predictive-laws]].

Write $X_t=(x_1,\ldots,x_t)$, $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_t)$, $m_{X_t}=(m(x_i))_{i\le t}$, and $k_t(x)=(k(x_i,x))_{i\le t}$. The initial data list has length $s$, so the current history length starts at $t=s$ and the procedure selects at stages $t=s,\ldots,N-1$, stopping when the total history length reaches $N$. The output is the finite selected-site/observation trace, its current posterior state, and every verified acquisition error $\delta_t$. For $t=0$, use prior mean $\mu_0(x)=m(x)$ and variance $v_0(x)=k(x,x)$, with no matrix inverse. For $t\ge1$, form $K_t=(k(x_i,x_j))_{i,j\le t}$ and $C_t=K_t+\sigma^2 I$. If $C_t$ is not certified positive definite, return posterior-solve-unavailable with the last valid state and no posterior or acquisition at stage $t$. If $C_t$ is positive definite, compute the required solves by a Cholesky factorization $C_t=L_tL_t^T$ and forward/back substitution as in [[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]] and [[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]]. If a factorization or solve is unavailable, return the same status; never use a pseudoinverse or clip a negative variance.

For each candidate, compute
$$\mu_t(x)=m(x)+k_t(x)^T C_t^{-1}(y-m_{X_t})$$
$$v_t(x)=k(x,x)-k_t(x)^T C_t^{-1}k_t(x),\qquad s_t(x)=\sqrt{v_t(x)}$$
where the observed covariance and solves satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-finite-gaussian-process-posterior-and-predictive-laws]]. Its conditional covariance is positive semidefinite, so $v_t(x)\ge0$; [[thm-of-square-roots]] supplies the unique nonnegative square root used here. If nonnegativity of a computed $v_t(x)$ cannot be verified, return posterior-solve-unavailable. Form the acquisition value $a_t(x)=\mu_t(x)+b_t s_t(x)$ and inspect all $M$ candidates. The default routine returns the exact least-index maximizer with $\delta_t=0$. An optional approximate routine must be a deterministic measurable function of the finite observation history and return a candidate $x_{j_t}$ with a verified $\delta_t\ge0$ satisfying $a_t(x_{j_t})\ge\max_{x\in X}a_t(x)-\delta_t$. If no such comparison certificate is available, return acquisition-inconclusive. Record every $\delta_t$.

Call $O$ at the selected candidate. If it returns observation-unavailable, return that status with the current trace and last valid posterior state, without appending a value. Otherwise append the returned observation and repeat until the finite horizon is reached. A finite budget exhaustion returns the current trace and no unearned posterior status. For a deterministic simulator or a misspecified prior, these formulas describe only the chosen surrogate model; the algorithm asserts no generic regret, global-optimality, or model-truth result.

Let $U,V,a,b$ satisfy [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** an integer $M\ge2$, images $R_0=a,R_1,\ldots,R_{M-1},R_M=b$ in $U$, a step size $\eta>0$, force and spacing tolerances $\tau_F,\tau_s\ge0$, and a finite update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$. **Output:** the last image chain and one of `tolerances-met`, `geometry-failure`, `nonfinite-evaluation`, or `budget-exhausted`. A stop status is an algorithmic report, not a continuum-error certificate.

At iteration $k=0,\ldots,N$, perform the following in order.

1. For each interior $i=1,\ldots,M-1$, form the centered chord $c_i=R_{i+1}-R_{i-1}$. If $c_i=0$, return `geometry-failure`. Otherwise put $t_i=c_i/\|c_i\|_2$ and $F_i^\perp=-(I-t_it_i^T)\nabla V(R_i)$. If any force is nonfinite, return `nonfinite-evaluation`.
2. For the current chain set $\ell_i=\|R_i-R_{i-1}\|_2$ for $1\le i\le M$, $\bar\ell=M^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M\ell_i$, $r_F=\max_{1\le i<M}\|F_i^\perp\|_2$, and $r_s=\max_{1\le i\le M}|\ell_i-\bar\ell|$. If $r_F\le\tau_F$ and $r_s\le\tau_s$, return `tolerances-met`.
3. If $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`. Otherwise set $Y_0=a$, $Y_M=b$, and $Y_i=R_i+\eta F_i^\perp$ for interior images. Reject any nonfinite $Y_i$ with `nonfinite-evaluation`; if any $Y_i\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`.
4. Compute cumulative lengths $s_0=0$, $s_j=\sum_{i=1}^j\|Y_i-Y_{i-1}\|_2$, and total length $S=s_M$. If $S=0$ or any segment length is zero, return `geometry-failure`. For $j=1,\ldots,M-1$, place the new image at the unique point of the piecewise-linear polygon $Y_0,\ldots,Y_M$ whose cumulative length is $jS/M$; if that target is a vertex, use that vertex, and otherwise use linear interpolation on its unique containing segment. If any redistributed image lies outside $U$, return `geometry-failure`. Set $R_0^{k+1}=a,R_M^{k+1}=b$ and use the checked redistributed points as the new interior images.

This is the specified projected-force string variant. No convergence from arbitrary initial images, no automatic endpoint minimization, and no error estimate follow from the procedure alone.

Input a positive integer $n$, a nonempty complex matrix family $\mathcal M$ enclosed entrywise by finite dyadic real/imaginary rectangles, a dyadic center matrix $M_0$, a certified dyadic bound $\delta_A\ge\sup_{M\in\mathcal M}\|M-M_0\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$, and a simple positively oriented strictly convex polygon $\Gamma$ with dyadic vertices and filled interior $P$. Supply the dyadic disk cover and point preconditioners required by [[alg-complex-resolvent-cover-validator]], a positive integer $N$ for midpoint subdivisions of each edge, a positive integer $K_\pi$ for the arctangent series, and a finite arithmetic budget. The family may be the monodromy block of a validated shooting jet; no correlation between matrix entries is required. A complex rectangle here is the product of one closed dyadic real interval and one closed dyadic imaginary interval for each matrix entry.

1. Verify the polygon orientation/strict convexity exactly, then run the resolvent-cover validator on every edge for the entire family. If any segment is uncovered, an outward inequality is not strict, or no finite upper bound $m$ on $\|(zI-M)^{-1}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$ is returned, output `inconclusive`.
2. Subdivide each oriented edge $e_j=b_j-a_j$ into $N$ equal parts, with rational midpoints $z_{jk}=a_j+(k+1/2)e_j/N$. By exact rational complex elimination, compute $R^0_{jk}=(z_{jk}I-M_0)^{-1}$; a singular center matrix or an incomplete operation returns `inconclusive`. For each rational complex entry $a+ib$ of $R^0_{jk}$, use rational square-root bisection to find an upper bound for $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, then sum row bounds to obtain $b_{jk}\ge\|R^0_{jk}\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$. Use the same bisection to obtain $s_j\ge|e_j|$. If the finite budget does not produce these rational bounds, return `inconclusive`.
3. Form the exact center midpoint sum
$$S_0=\sum_j\frac{e_j}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\operatorname{tr}R^0_{jk},$$
and the outward error allowance
$$E=\frac{n m^2}{2N}\sum_j|e_j|^2+\frac{n m\delta_A}{N}\sum_{j,k}s_jb_{jk}.$$
The first term uses the exact rational squared modulus of each rational edge; the second uses the rational upper edge length $s_j$. The first term bounds midpoint quadrature error; the second bounds replacing each family resolvent by the center resolvent. All sums and products are exact rationals; if a required rational square-root upper bound is unavailable, return `inconclusive`.
4. Enclose $\pi$ using $\pi=4\arctan(1)$ and the alternating partial sum $4\sum_{k=0}^{K_\pi-1}(-1)^k/(2k+1)$ with tail radius $4/(2K_\pi+1)$. Require a positive lower endpoint. Using exact rational endpoint arithmetic, enclose $S_0/(2\pi i)$ and inflate its real and imaginary intervals by $E/(2\pi_{\rm low})$; call the resulting rectangle $I$.
5. Choose an integer $c$ and return `certified-count(c)` only if $0\le c\le n$, $\operatorname{Re}I\subset(c-1/2,c+1/2)$, $\operatorname{Im}I\subset(-1/2,1/2)$, and $0\in\operatorname{Im}I$. Otherwise return `inconclusive`. This operation counts roots with algebraic multiplicity in $\operatorname{int}P$ for every matrix in the supplied family; it does not classify a cluster touching the unit circle as stable or unstable.

For a simple separated multiplier, an optional left/right-conditioned finite enclosure may also be reported using [[lem-separated-simple-floquet-multiplier-perturbation-bound]]. The contour count remains the required path for clusters or unresolved individual eigenvectors.

The matrix family may be taken from the monodromy block of [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]]. Resolvent bounds use the complex infinity norm [[def-complex-infinity-matrix-norm]] and its product inequality [[lem-complex-infinity-matrix-norm-submultiplicative]]; the boundary cover is interpreted by [[thm-complex-resolvent-cover-validator-soundness]]. The root multiplicities are those of the characteristic polynomial by [[thm-complex-polynomial-has-exactly-degree-many-roots-counted-with-multiplicity]]. Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$
be $C^1$ in the sense of [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. Its Jacobian
$J_F(x)$ is the matrix of first partial derivatives from
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], and the matrix of $DF(x)$ in the standard
basis is $J_F(x)$ by
[[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. For
$x\in U$, supply increments $h=(h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1})\in\mathbb R^n$. For each
standard basis vector $e_i$ with $0\le i<n$, the admissible stencil conditions
are $h_i\ne0$ and $x+h_i e_i\in U$.

If any admissibility condition fails, return `invalid-stencil`. Otherwise form
the matrix $J_hF(x)$ column by column:
$$J_hF(x)e_i:=\frac{F(x+h_i e_i)-F(x)}{h_i},\qquad 0\le i<n.$$

procedure defines a forward-difference approximation; it asserts no accuracy
or convergence guarantee.

Input a $C^2$ graph, admissible $x$, and direction $v$. First run the forward tangent recurrence to compute every $\dot z_j=Dz_j(x)v$. Initialize every operation and input cotangent and tangent-cotangent accumulator to zero. $$c_{j,k}=A_{j,k}^{T}\bar z_j,\qquad \dot c_{j,k}=A_{j,k}^{T}\dot{\bar z}_j+\bigl(DA_{j,k}(z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,z_{p_{j,r_j}})[\dot z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,\dot z_{p_{j,r_j}}]\bigr)^{T}\bar z_j,$$
and add $c_{j,k}$ and $\dot c_{j,k}$ to the parent's cotangent and tangent-cotangent accumulators. Use $(\bar x_i,\dot{\bar x}_i)$ for input coordinate $i$ and $(\bar z_\ell,\dot{\bar z}_\ell)$ for operation node $\ell$. If the same parent occurs in multiple slots, add every slot contribution.
Return the input tangent of the gradient, $(\dot{\bar x}_1,\ldots,\dot{\bar x}_n)$. Repeated parent slots receive separate additions. Fix $T\ge1$, positive dimensions $d_0,\ldots,d_T$ and $p_1,\ldots,p_T$, open sets $U_t\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_t}$, and continuously differentiable maps $\Psi_{t-1}:U_{t-1}\to U_t$ and $G_t:U_t\to\mathbb R^{p_t}$. Let $m_b\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$, $B\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times d_0}$ be symmetric positive definite, $y_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t}$, and $\Gamma_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t\times p_t}$ be symmetric positive definite. In weak-constraint mode also require symmetric positive-definite $Q_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_t}$. The strong-constraint decision domain is $U_0$; the weak-constraint decision domain is $U_0\times\cdots\times U_T$. Both objectives are continuously differentiable on their stated open decision domains. For a positive-definite covariance $M$, write $\|v\|_{M^{-1}}^2=v^TM^{-1}v$.

In **strong-constraint 4DVAR**, choose the initial state $u_0$ and generate $u_t=\Psi_{t-1}(u_{t-1})$ for $1\le t\le T$. Minimize the trajectory objective
$$J_s(u_0)=\tfrac12\|u_0-m_b\|_{B^{-1}}^2+\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T\|y_t-G_t(u_t)\|_{\Gamma_t^{-1}}^2.$$

In **weak-constraint 4DVAR**, the decision variable is the full path $(u_0,\ldots,u_T)$. Given model-error covariances $Q_t\succ0$, minimize
$$J_w(u_0,\ldots,u_T)=\tfrac12\|u_0-m_b\|_{B^{-1}}^2+\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T\|y_t-G_t(u_t)\|_{\Gamma_t^{-1}}^2+\tfrac12\sum_{t=1}^T\|u_t-\Psi_{t-1}(u_{t-1})\|_{Q_t^{-1}}^2.$$

Select one objective, an initial decision vector in its stated decision domain, a finite iteration limit $M\ge0$, and either positive fixed steps or the backtracking parameters required by [[alg-gradient-descent]]. Run that algorithm on the selected objective for at most $M$ updates and return its last iterate (or report its domain failure). In strong mode return the trajectory generated from the last initial-state iterate; in weak mode return the last path iterate. This is a finite numerical procedure, not a guarantee that a global or local minimizer is reached. The page's BCS-20 hypotheses for gradient descent supply no general guarantee for these objectives.

Definition

Inputs are a $C^1$ objective $f:D\to\mathbb R$ on an open $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $x_0\in D$, consistent SPD matrices $B_0,H_0$ with $B_0H_0=H_0B_0=I$, a reset scale $\gamma>0$, constants $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$, finite line-search budgets $E,Z$, a finite iteration budget $K$, a direction mode exact or rounded-Cholesky, and an update mode undamped or Powell.

Initialize $k:=0$, $x_k:=x_0$, $B_k:=B_0$, $H_k:=H_0$, and $g_0:=\nabla f(x_0)$. If $g_0=0$, return stationary at $x_0$. While $k<K$, if $g_k=0$, return stationary at $x_k$. Use the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] in descent and curvature tests. In exact direction mode set $p_k:=-H_kg_k$. In rounded-Cholesky mode call [[alg-bfgs-hessian-direction-with-rounded-cholesky]] with $(B_k,g_k)$; if the factorization or triangular solve fails, return its failure status with $x_k$. If the computed direction is not descending, reset $B_k:=\gamma^{-1}I$, $H_k:=\gamma I$, and set $p_k:=-\gamma g_k$.

Call [[alg-bracketing-zoom-strong-wolfe-search]] with $(f,x_k,p_k,c_1,c_2,E,Z)$. If it returns a failure status, return that status and $x_k$. Otherwise take its positive strong Wolfe step $\alpha_k$, set $x_{k+1}:=x_k+\alpha_kp_k$, and compute $g_{k+1}:=\nabla f(x_{k+1})$. Define
$$ s_k:=\alpha_kp_k,\qquad y_k:=g_{k+1}-g_k. $$
In undamped mode set $\bar y_k:=y_k$. In Powell mode put $c_k:=s_k^TB_ks_k$ and use the damping rule of [[def-bfgs-curvature-pair-and-update-formulas]] to form $\bar y_k$. If $s_k^T\bar y_k\le0$, skip the matrix update and return curvature-rejected with $x_{k+1}$. Otherwise update both matrices by
$$ B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k} +\frac{\bar y_k\bar y_k^T}{s_k^T\bar y_k}, \qquad H_{k+1}=(I-\rho_ks_k\bar y_k^T)H_k(I-\rho_k\bar y_ks_k^T)+\rho_ks_ks_k^T, \quad \rho_k=(s_k^T\bar y_k)^{-1}. $$
If any required scalar or matrix operation is undefined, discard partial update results and return update-failure with $x_{k+1}$. After a successful update, commit $(x_{k+1},g_{k+1},B_{k+1},H_{k+1})$ as the state for the next iteration. If $g_{k+1}=0$, return stationary at $x_{k+1}$; if $k+1=K$, return iteration-budget-exhausted at $x_{k+1}$. Otherwise set $k:=k+1$ and continue from that committed state. A line-search failure returns its status with $x_k$. If the loop exits because $k=K$ without another return, return iteration-budget-exhausted with $x_k$; this covers $K=0$. The output is the last point and one of stationary, a line-search status, factorization/solve failure, curvature-rejected, update-failure, or iteration-budget-exhausted.

The mathematical exact direction mode and the BFGS matrix updates are interpreted over $\mathbb R$. The rounded-Cholesky direction mode specifies a computed factor-and-solve direction only; this item supplies no backward-error or convergence theorem for that mode. Its returned direction is checked for descent before the strong Wolfe search. The line-search procedure can fail within its finite budgets even when an acceptable step exists.

Definition

Input a stored residual $r\in\mathbb R^m$, a stored Jacobian $J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$ (using the convention of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), a factorization mode QR or SVD, an arithmetic mode (exact or computed), and a declared singular-value threshold $\tau\ge0$. A computed QR report may also carry a verified full-rank certificate $s>0$ asserting $\|Jv\|_2\ge s\|v\|_2$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$. The target exact step, when it is returned, is the unique minimizer of $\frac12\|r+Jp\|_2^2$ and hence solves $J^TJp=-J^Tr$; this target is asserted only on a full-column-rank branch. Do not form $J^TJ$ in either solve path.

For QR mode the exact and computed routes are disjoint. Exact mode requires a supplied exact reduced factorization $J=QR$ with $Q^TQ=I_n$; only this exact factorization may reach the exact-step branch. Computed mode consumes a computed QR report or forms one by setting $C=[J\mid-r]$ and, for $k=1,\ldots,n$, applying [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] to the active part of column $k$ and all trailing columns of $C$, including its last right-hand-side column. Propagate the first factorization failure. After a successful computed loop, the report consists of the computed upper-triangular block $\widehat R$ and the first $n$ entries $\widehat y$ of the transformed last column. These rounded outputs are not an exact factorization of $J$ and cannot be supplied to the exact branch. In exact mode, a zero diagonal in $R$ returns rank-deficient; otherwise solve $Rp=Q^T(-r)$ by backward substitution and return exact-step($p$). In computed mode, a zero diagonal returns rank-deficient-candidate. Otherwise initialize storage for $\widehat p_0,\ldots,\widehat p_{n-1}$ with all components unassigned, then for $i=n-1,n-2,\ldots,0$ compute $s_i$ by setting $s_i=0$ and, for $j=i+1,i+2,\ldots,n-1$ in increasing order, updating $s_i\leftarrow\operatorname{fl}(s_i+\operatorname{fl}(\widehat R_{ij}\widehat p_j))$; then compute $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat y_i-s_i)$ and $\widehat p_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/\widehat R_{ii})$. Any first arithmetic or range failure returns linear-solve-failure with its stage and indices. A nonzero computed diagonal without an independently verified full-rank certificate $s>0$ for the input matrix $J$ returns rank-unverified with the computed candidate but no full-rank claim. With that certificate, return computed-candidate($\widehat p$). A nonzero computed diagonal alone is not a full-rank certificate. The computed-QR backward-stability conclusion of [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] is attached only when all of that theorem's successful-execution, arithmetic, and nonsingularity hypotheses are supplied; otherwise no backward-stability conclusion is returned.

For SVD mode, the input includes an exact factorization $J=U\Sigma V^T$, or a computed report containing finite stored factors $\widehat U_1$, $\widehat\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\sigma_i)$ with nonnegative entries, and $\widehat V$, together with certified intervals $[\ell_i,u_i]$ satisfying $\ell_i\le\sigma_i(J)\le u_i$ for each of the $n$ singular values relevant to full column rank. In the exact case, if any $\sigma_i\le\tau$, return rank-below-threshold and no Gauss-Newton step. If every $\sigma_i>\tau$, return
$$p=-V\,\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\sigma_n^{-1})\,U_1^Tr,$$
where $U_1$ consists of the corresponding $n$ left singular vectors. For a computed report, if any $u_i\le\tau$, return rank-below-threshold; if any interval satisfies $\ell_i\le\tau<u_i$, return rank-unverified; if every lower endpoint exceeds $\tau$ but some stored $\widehat\sigma_i=0$, return factorization-failure; otherwise return the finite candidate
$$\widehat p=-\widehat V\,\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\sigma_1^{-1},\ldots,\widehat\sigma_n^{-1})\,\widehat U_1^Tr$$
with status computed-candidate and make no accuracy claim beyond the supplied report. The certified intervals determine only the threshold branch; no computed-SVD accuracy bound is asserted. A computed SVD routine is not defined here; the SVD branch consumes its report.

If $m<n$, return unsupported-shape; if the selected factorization reports failure, return factorization-failure; every status other than exact-step is explicitly not a certified exact full-rank Gauss-Newton step.

Definition

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be continuously
Fréchet differentiable. The gradient $\nabla f(x)$ is the vector of partial
derivatives in the Euclidean coordinates, with the convention of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]; differentiability is the Fréchet
condition of [[def-real-frechet-derivative-on-real-and-complex-matrix-spaces]].

**Inputs:** an initial point $x_0\in U$; either a positive fixed-step
sequence $(t_k)_{k\ge0}$ or backtracking parameters $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and
$\beta\in(0,1)$; and an optional caller stopping predicate
$S(k,x,g)\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, with
$S:\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\times U\times\mathbb R^d\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$.
If no predicate is supplied, use $S\equiv\mathrm{false}$. **Output:** when the
procedure stops, return the last valid iterate $x_k$ and the status
`stationary`, `caller-stop`, or `domain-failure`.
If no stopping status occurs, the sequence continues and there is no finite
return.
For example, an outer procedure's at-most-$M$-updates limit, for finite real
$M\ge0$, is implemented by $S(k,x,g):=(k+1>M)$.

At iteration $k$, where $k$ is the number of accepted updates so far and the
current iterate is $x_k$:

1. Compute $g_k:=\nabla f(x_k)$ and set $p_k:=-g_k$. If $g_k=0$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$.
2. If $S(k,x_k,g_k)$ is true, return $(x_k,\texttt{caller-stop})$. Check this
   predicate at the current iterate after its gradient is computed and before
   any step is selected.
3. In fixed-step mode, set $t=t_k$. If $x_k+tp_k\notin U$, return
   $(x_k,\texttt{domain-failure})$ without accepting that candidate.
4. In backtracking mode, start with $t=1$ and repeatedly replace $t$ by
   $\beta t$ until $x_k+tp_k\in U$ and
   $f(x_k+tp_k)\le f(x_k)+\alpha t\,\langle g_k,p_k\rangle$.
5. Set $x_{k+1}:=x_k+t p_k$ and continue at iteration $k+1$.

The fixed-step update map is $x\mapsto x-t_k\nabla f(x)$; at a stationary
point its value is $x$, which is the returned iterate. A backtracking search
that is reached at a nonstationary iterate is well-defined by
[[lem-armijo-backtracking-terminates-for-strict-descent-directions]]. The
procedure asserts no convergence or global-minimization property for an
arbitrary objective.

Definition

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$ be open and $H\in C^2(U)$. Write $z=(q,p)$ in canonical coordinates, set $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$, and define the finite-regularity coordinate field
$$F(q,p):=\bigl(\nabla_pH(q,p),-\nabla_qH(q,p)\bigr)=J\nabla H(q,p).$$
Given $z\in U$, for a signed step $h$, the **exact local implicit midpoint step** is defined by
$$Z=z+\frac h2F(Z),\qquad z^+=2Z-z,$$
using the locally unique solution $Z$ in a declared closed ball $\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$. The branch is admissible when certified bounds $M\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|F\|$ and $L\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|DF\|$ satisfy $|h|M/2\le\rho$ and $|h|L/2<1$. It returns `branch-not-certified` if the ball or bounds are unavailable, and `domain-failure` if the admitted ball is not contained in $U$.

For a finite iteration implementation of these exact operations, input an output tolerance $\tau>0$ and an update budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$. Use $\theta=|h|L/2$ and proceed as follows.

1. Set $Z_0=z$. If $B=0$, return `inconclusive` with current stage iterate $Z_0$, approximate output $z$, and output-error bound $2\rho$.
2. If $B\ge1$, compute $Z_1=z+(h/2)F(Z_0)$ and set $d_1=\|Z_1-Z_0\|$.
3. For $k=1,\ldots,B$, set $b_k=\theta^k d_1/(1-\theta)$ and the output radius $r_k=2b_k$. If $r_k\le\tau$, return the approximation $2Z_k-z$ with output-error certificate $r_k$. Otherwise, if $k<B$, compute $Z_{k+1}=z+(h/2)F(Z_k)$ and continue. If the check fails at $k=B$, return `inconclusive` with current stage iterate $Z_B$, approximate output $2Z_B-z$, and output-error bound $2b_B$.

When $\theta=0$, use $\theta^k=0$ for $k\ge1$; the procedure never evaluates $0^0$. These certificates concern the displayed exact recurrence and exact output operations; inexact evaluations require additional certified error accounting before a tolerance claim can be made. An approximate result is not asserted to be exactly symplectic. The exact map is the selected branch value $2Z-z$.

**Inputs.** Take a finite strictly increasing time grid $t_0<\cdots<t_N$, $N\ge1$, a vector field $f$ defined at every attempted evaluation, a method selector in {BE, the selected two-stage SDIRK, two-stage Radau IIA, variable-step BDF2}, and an initial state $Y_0$. Supply the exact residual derivative matrix whenever the selected solver requests a Jacobian; residual/Jacobian evaluations and domain tests are returning primitives. These per-call open domains are distinct from closed BDF2 root-selection balls; if a finite-solve BDF2 iterate is to remain on the selected branch, require its open residual domain to be contained in that branch ball. In chord mode that backend must satisfy the exact-solve interface of [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]]. For BDF2 supply $Y_1$, or select a BE startup and give that solve its own domain, initial iterate, tolerance, budget, mode, refresh period, and admissible backend. Also supply a closed BDF2 branch ball for each later BDF2 step.

**Procedure.** For BE, form the endpoint residual of [[def-backward-euler-step-equation]]. For SDIRK or Radau IIA, form the stage residual of [[def-implicit-runge-kutta-stage-equations]] with the selected tableau and update by its formula. Call [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]] for each finite solve. If it returns `root`, store the returned endpoint or stages, update the state, and record the returned residual norm and solver work; this status means only that the tolerance was met. On any other status, return immediately with the computed prefix, residual norm when available, and work log. An evaluation failure, singular Jacobian, invalid trial, or exhausted correction budget therefore cannot be reported as a successful step.

For an exact-root BDF2 run, call [[alg-variable-step-bdf2-with-selected-implicit-branch]] on the supplied starter pair for steps $n=1,\ldots,N-1$ with the supplied branch balls; it returns a computed prefix and `completed`, `no-root`, `ambiguous-branch`, or `evaluation-failure`. In a finite-solve BDF2 run, use the same branch balls for steps $n=1,\ldots,N-1$ and form the unscaled residual
$$G_n(Z)=(1+2r_n)Z-(1+r_n)^2Y_n+r_n^2Y_{n-1}-h_n(1+r_n)f(t_{n+1},Z),\qquad r_n=h_n/h_{n-1}.$$
Call the finite solver with this $C^1$ residual $G_n$, its supplied open domain $U_n$, initial iterate $z_{n,0}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_n$, correction budget $M_n$, mode, refresh period $q_n$, and backend; after a `root` status, store its approximate iterate and continue, labelling the run `completed-with-residual-tolerances` only after every requested step returns `root`. A finite residual status does not establish the exact-root completion of the BDF2 branch algorithm.

For BDF2, the order guarantee in [[thm-variable-step-bdf2-order-two-under-ratio-bound]] requires its smoothness, ratio, tube, unique-root, and $O(H^2)$ starter hypotheses. The exact-start BE estimate and branch conditions are proved in [[cor-constant-step-bdf2-order-two-with-consistent-start]]; a finite-tolerance startup must separately meet that result's starter error budget. For any method, a forward-error claim requires a separate residual-to-error estimate such as [[lem-small-step-implicit-rk-branch-and-residual-error]], [[thm-backward-euler-algebraic-update-residual-error-budget]] for BE/RK. The BDF2 order theorem concerns exact selected roots; it is not a residual-to-error bound for finite-solve BDF2 output, which requires its own additional stability and accumulated residual-error analysis.

**Work record.** Count every Jacobian assembly and factorization attempt at a refresh, every linear solve, and, for dense LU, each correction's forward and backward triangular solve. Reuse a chord factorization only for its declared refresh period. Sparse cost depends on the actual stage matrix and backend; this procedure assigns no sparse complexity bound. No general Newton convergence or forward-accuracy claim is part of the algorithm.

Definition

Let $U,V,a,b$ satisfy [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** an integer $M\ge2$, images $R_0=a,R_1,\ldots,R_M=b$ in $U$, spring constant $\kappa\ge0$, fixed step $\eta>0$, force and spacing tolerances $\tau_F,\tau_s\ge0$, an ordinary-step count $n_{\rm climb}\in\mathbb N_0$, and a finite update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$. Require $n_{\rm climb}\le N$. **Output:** the last chain and one of `tolerances-met`, `tangent-failure`, `geometry-failure`, `nonfinite-evaluation`, or `budget-exhausted`.

At each iteration, endpoints are fixed and only interior images are updated. For $i=1,\ldots,M-1$, write $\Delta_i^+=R_{i+1}-R_i$, $\Delta_i^-=R_i-R_{i-1}$, and $V_i=V(R_i)$. Select an unnormalized tangent by

$$\tau_i=\begin{cases}\Delta_i^+,&V_{i+1}>V_i>V_{i-1},\\\Delta_i^-,&V_{i+1}<V_i<V_{i-1},\\w_{\max}\Delta_i^+ + w_{\min}\Delta_i^-,&\text{otherwise and }V_{i+1}>V_{i-1},\\w_{\min}\Delta_i^+ + w_{\max}\Delta_i^-,&\text{otherwise and }V_{i+1}<V_{i-1},\\\Delta_i^++\Delta_i^-,&V_{i+1}=V_{i-1},\end{cases}$$

where $w_{\max}=\max(|V_{i+1}-V_i|,|V_{i-1}-V_i|)$ and $w_{\min}=\min(|V_{i+1}-V_i|,|V_{i-1}-V_i|)$. If $\tau_i=0$, return `tangent-failure`; otherwise set $t_i=\tau_i/\|\tau_i\|_2$. Nonfinite energies, gradients, or forces return `nonfinite-evaluation`.

Initialize the update counter $k=0$. At iteration $k$, use the ordinary force

$$F_i=-(I-t_it_i^T)\nabla V(R_i)+\kappa(\|\Delta_i^+\|_2-\|\Delta_i^-\|_2)t_i.$$

When $k\ge n_{\rm climb}$, choose the least index $i_*$ attaining the largest interior energy and replace that image's force by

$$F_{i_*}^{\rm CI}=-\nabla V(R_{i_*})+2(\nabla V(R_{i_*})^Tt_{i_*})t_{i_*};$$

the climbing image has no spring force. The remaining interior images retain the ordinary force. Thus iterations $k=0,\ldots,n_{\rm climb}-1$ use ordinary forces and the first climbing force is evaluated at iteration $k=n_{\rm climb}$. At each iteration report the maximum force norm and spacing residual $\max_i|\|\Delta_i^+\|_2-\|\Delta_i^-\|_2|$. Stop with `tolerances-met` only if both are within their declared tolerances. If a tolerance fails and $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`; only when $k<N$ update every interior image by $R_i^{k+1}=R_i^k+\eta F_i^k$. Leaving $U$ returns `geometry-failure`. After a valid update set $k\leftarrow k+1$ and repeat. The tolerance check precedes the budget check, so $N=0$ still checks the initial chain and $n_{\rm climb}=N$ uses a climbing force at the final residual check (without an update if the budget is then exhausted).

The finite stopping status does not assert convergence to a MEP, a saddle, or a continuum path.

Also input positive residual tolerances $\eta_d,\eta_a$, a finite Newton-correction budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, and an initial algebraic-residual bound $\eta_{a,0}\ge0$. Return invalid-grid if $h\le0$ or $N_t=0$, and invalid-input for incompatible dimensions, data outside the function domains, or $(X_0,Z_0)\notin\mathcal T_{t_0}$. Compute the starting algebraic residual once; return inconsistent-initial-data if $\|g(t_0,X_0,Z_0)\|_2>\eta_{a,0}$.

For $n=1,\ldots,N_t$, form the coupled update residual

$$
R_n(X,Z)=\bigl(X-X_{n-1}-h f(t_n,X,Z),\ g(t_n,X,Z)\bigr)
$$

and the scaled square residual

$$
\mathcal R_n(X,Z)=\left(\frac{X-X_{n-1}-h f(t_n,X,Z)}{h\eta_d},\ \frac{g(t_n,X,Z)}{\eta_a}\right).
$$

Use $(X_{n-1},Z_{n-1})$ as the Newton seed. Before calling Newton, if $(X_{n-1},Z_{n-1})\notin\mathcal T_{t_n}$, return invalid-trial with the already computed prefix. Otherwise call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $\mathcal R_n$ with residual tolerance $1$, budget $B$, and $\mathcal T_{t_n}$ as its evaluation domain. If the returned status is root and the candidate lies in $\mathcal T_{t_n}$, reevaluate $R_n$ once to retain both unscaled residuals, then append the candidate. Otherwise return the corresponding singular-Jacobian, invalid-trial, or iteration-budget-exhausted status and the already computed prefix. The input functions are defined on the selected tube, so no separate evaluation-failure branch is needed. If every step is accepted, return completed and the state sequence.

Let $U,V$ be as in [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** an initial point $x_0\in U$, a unit initial mode reference $v_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R^d$, a local-ball center $x_{\rm ref}\in U$, radius $r_{\rm loc}>0$, gradient tolerance $\tau_g\ge0$, eigenvalue margin $\gamma>0$, eigenpair residual tolerance $\tau_{\rm eig}\ge0$, mode-overlap threshold $0\le\tau_{\rm mode}<1$, and update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$. Return the last point, aligned lowest-mode reference and one of `geometry-failure`, `outside-local-basin`, `gradient-residual-tolerance`, `budget-exhausted`, `eigensolve-tolerance-failure`, `index-one-branch-failure`, `mode-tracking-failure`, or a status returned by the vector Newton correction. At each iterate $x_k$, the eigensolver supplies an orthogonal matrix $Q=[q_1,\ldots,q_d]$, ordered approximate eigenvalues $\widehat\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\widehat\lambda_d$, and validated intervals $I_j=[\ell_j,u_j]$ in the sense of [[def-validated-eigenvalue-enclosures-for-an-index-one-hessian]]. Require every residual $\|H(x_k)q_j-\widehat\lambda_jq_j\|_2\le\tau_{\rm eig}$, $\sqrt d\,\tau_{\rm eig}\le\gamma/2$, and $\widehat\lambda_j\in I_j$. The Hessian $H=\nabla^2V$ is symmetric by [[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]].

For $k=0,\ldots,N$, in order:

1. If $x_k\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`. If $x_k\notin B_2(x_{\rm ref},r_{\rm loc})$, return `outside-local-basin`. Compute $g_k=\nabla V(x_k)$. If $\|g_k\|_2\le\tau_g$, return `gradient-residual-tolerance`; if $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`.
2. If an eigenpair residual exceeds $\tau_{\rm eig}$, $\sqrt d\tau_{\rm eig}>\gamma/2$, or some $\widehat\lambda_j\notin I_j$, return `eigensolve-tolerance-failure`. If the validated intervals do not satisfy $u_1\le-\gamma$ and $\ell_j\ge\gamma$ for all $j\ge2$ (with the dimension-one convention in the definition), return `index-one-branch-failure`. If $|q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}|<\tau_{\rm mode}$, return `mode-tracking-failure`; otherwise replace $q_1$ by its sign-aligned representative with $q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}\ge0$ and use this as the next mode reference. This overlap check detects a mode-branch change but does not alter the Newton correction.
3. Call [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]] with $A=H(x_k)$ and $r=g_k$. If its Jacobian is singular, return `singular-hessian`. Its correction $p_k$ is the exact Newton solution of $H(x_k)p_k=-g_k$ in the mathematical model; the eigenpair data certifies the index-one branch but does not replace this linear solve.
4. If $x_k+p_k\notin U$ or lies outside $B_2(x_{\rm ref},r_{\rm loc})$, return `outside-local-basin`. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k$ and continue.

An approximate eigensolve has a finite residual-tolerance branch and an explicit failure status. The definition makes no global-convergence claim. Local quadratic behavior is stated separately and requires the hypotheses of [[thm-updated-jacobian-newton-local-quadratic-convergence]].

Definition

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$
be twice continuously differentiable, meaning that $f$ is $C^1$ and its
gradient is $C^1$.
Write $g(x):=\nabla f(x)$ and $H(x):=\nabla^2f(x)$ using
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
[[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]. The identity matrix $I_n$ and
matrix-vector products have the convention of
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]. Use the matrix-free access
model of [[def-matrix-free-access-model-for-krylov-methods]] for products
$v\mapsto(H(x)+\lambda I_n)v$.

**Linear-solver input:** a fixed deterministic Krylov procedure $K$ which accepts a
matrix-free linear operator $A$, a right-hand side $b$, a tolerance $\tau\ge0$,
and a finite inner-iteration budget $M\in\mathbb N_0$. It returns either
`no-candidate` or `candidate` with a vector $p$ and an iteration count
$m\in\{0,1,\ldots,M\}$ satisfying $p\in K_m(A,b)$, where $K_m$ is as defined
by [[def-krylov-subspace-of-a-matrix-and-start-vector]]. A candidate's residual
status is never trusted: this algorithm recomputes
the requested residual using the supplied operator. **Other inputs:** $x_0\in U$, outer update budget
$N\in\mathbb N_0$, forcing values $\eta_k\in[0,\bar\eta]$ for a fixed
$0\le\bar\eta<1$, descent parameter $\sigma\in(0,1)$, regularization factor
$\gamma>1$, initial shift $\lambda_0>0$, shift cap $\lambda_{\max}\ge\lambda_0$,
regularized-attempt budget $J\in\mathbb N_0$, inner budget $M$, and the
parameters and finite expansion/zoom budgets of
[[alg-bracketing-zoom-strong-wolfe-search]]. **Output:** the last valid
iterate and one of `stationary`, `iteration-budget-exhausted`,
`no-descent-direction`, or `line-search-failure`; in the last case also
return the underlying line-search failure cause.

At iteration $k=0,1,\ldots,N$:

1. Compute $g_k:=g(x_k)$. If $g_k=0$, return $(x_k,\texttt{stationary})$.
   If $k=N$, return $(x_k,\texttt{iteration-budget-exhausted})$.
2. Set $\lambda:=0$. For $j=0,1,\ldots,J$, call $K$ on
   $A_\lambda v:=H(x_k)v+\lambda I_nv$, right-hand side $-g_k$, tolerance
   $\eta_k\|g_k\|_2$, and budget $M$. A `no-candidate` result is a rejected
   attempt. If it returns a candidate $p$, compute
   $r:=(H(x_k)+\lambda I_n)p+g_k$. Accept this linear solve only when
   $\|r\|_2\le\eta_k\|g_k\|_2$ and
   $\langle g_k,p\rangle<-\sigma\|g_k\|_2\|p\|_2$; otherwise reject it.
   If the attempt is rejected and either $j=J$ or $\lambda=\lambda_{\max}$, stop the
   regularization loop. Otherwise set
   $\lambda:=\min\{\lambda_{\max},\lambda_0\}$ when $\lambda=0$, and
   $\lambda:=\min\{\lambda_{\max},\gamma\lambda\}$ when $\lambda>0$;
   then continue with the next $j$.
3. If no regularized attempt was accepted, set $p:=-g_k$ and check
   $\langle g_k,p\rangle<-\sigma\|g_k\|_2\|p\|_2$. If this check fails,
   return `no-descent-direction`. For the stated $\sigma$ and $g_k\ne0$ it
   passes, but the check remains part of the procedure.
4. Call [[alg-bracketing-zoom-strong-wolfe-search]] at $x_k$ in direction $p$.
   If it returns failure, return $(x_k,\texttt{line-search-failure},s)$, where $s$ is
   the returned line-search failure cause. Otherwise, for its returned strong Wolfe step $t_k$,
   set $x_{k+1}:=x_k+t_kp$ and continue.

The first unregularized system uses the forcing residual
$\|H(x_k)p+g_k\|_2\le\eta_k\|g_k\|_2$. A regularized attempt checks the
residual for the shifted system instead. Finite inner, regularization, and
line-search budgets can return failure; the procedure makes no global
convergence claim. The local rate theorem applies only to an unshifted
$\lambda=0$ sequence taking full steps $t_k=1$ and remaining in its stated
local tube. This algorithm does not assert that every run enters that branch.

Input $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ of class $C^1$ on an open convex $U$, a nonempty initial real box $X_0\subset U$, interval evaluators whose returned $F(x_0)$ and $J(Y)$ enclose the exact values at each processed box $Y$, a dyadic point matrix $C$, a rational matrix $W$, a minimum side width $\eta>0$, and a nonnegative integer box budget $B\ge0$. Check the inverse witness exactly by computing $WC$ and testing $WC=I$. If this test fails, return "inconclusive: preconditioner not certified nonsingular". For square matrices, a left inverse implies nonsingularity by rank-nullity ([[thm-rank-nullity]]).

Initialize a queue with $X_0$. Process at most $B$ boxes. For each box $Y$, take its coordinatewise midpoint $x_0$, evaluate a finite interval vector $F_0$ enclosing $F(x_0)$ and a finite interval Jacobian enclosure $J(Y)$, and compute
$$
K(Y)=x_0-CF_0+(I-CJ(Y))(Y-x_0)
$$
by outward real interval operations. If an evaluation or operation is non-finite, record that box as "unresolved" and continue with the remaining queue. If $K(Y)\cap Y=\varnothing$, record "root-free". If $K(Y)\subset\operatorname{int}Y$, compute $E=I-CJ(Y)$ and
$$
\bar q=\max_i\sum_j\max(|\inf E_{ij}|,|\sup E_{ij}|).
$$
Record "unique-root" if $\bar q<1$, and "existence-only" otherwise. In every other case, bisect a longest side at its midpoint and append the two closed halves if the maximum side width exceeds $\eta$; ties use the lowest coordinate index. If no side exceeds $\eta$, record "unresolved". When the budget is exhausted, record every remaining queued box as "unresolved". The overall status is "complete" only if every output box is root-free or unique-root; existence-only and unresolved outputs do not establish an all-roots result.

Definition

Inputs are a $C^1$ objective $f:D\to\mathbb R$ on an open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, an initial point $x_0\in D$, a positive integer memory length $m$, a fallback scale $\gamma_0>0$, line-search constants $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$, finite expansion and zoom budgets $E,Z$, and an iteration budget $K$. Initialize $k:=0$, the current point $x:=x_0$, the current gradient $g:=\nabla f(x_0)$, and an empty history list. If $g=0$, return stationary. Otherwise, while $k<K$, store at most $m$ pairs $(s_i,y_i)$ in chronological order, retaining only pairs with $s_i^Ty_i>0$. Let $\rho_i=(s_i^Ty_i)^{-1}$ for each stored pair.

At each nonstationary iterate $x$ with current gradient $g$, all inner products are the Euclidean ones of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Choose $\gamma=\gamma_0$ if the list is empty; otherwise choose
$$ \gamma=\frac{s_{\rm last}^Ty_{\rm last}}{y_{\rm last}^Ty_{\rm last}}. $$
If this scalar cannot be computed as a finite positive real in the arithmetic used, clear the list and use $\gamma_0$. Compute $r=H_k g$ by the following two loops, then set $p=-r$:

1. Set $q:=g$. Traverse the stored pairs from newest to oldest, setting $\alpha_i:=\rho_i s_i^Tq$ and then $q:=q-\alpha_i y_i$.
2. Set $r:=\gamma q$. Traverse the pairs from oldest to newest, setting $\beta_i:=\rho_i y_i^Tr$ and then $r:=r+s_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i)$.

If $g=0$, return stationary. If $g^Tp\ge0$, clear the list, set $p:=-\gamma_0g$, and return direction-failure only if this fallback is not a strict descent direction.

Call [[alg-bracketing-zoom-strong-wolfe-search]] with $(f,x,p,c_1,c_2,E,Z)$. If it returns a failure status, return that status with the current point. If it returns $\alpha>0$, set $x^+:=x+\alpha p$, compute $g^+:=\nabla f(x^+)$, and set $s:=x^+-x$, $y:=g^+-g$. If $s^Ty>0$, append $(s,y)$ and $\rho=(s^Ty)^{-1}$, dropping the oldest pair if the list would exceed $m$. If $s^Ty\le0$ or the pair arithmetic fails, skip that pair and preserve the existing valid list.

After either storing or skipping the new pair, commit the accepted step by setting $x:=x^+$ and $g:=g^+$, then increment $k:=k+1$. If the updated gradient is zero, return stationary at $x$; otherwise continue while $k<K$. When the iteration budget is exhausted, return the current point and iteration-budget-exhausted. A line-search failure returns its status with the current point, and the fallback branch returns direction-failure only if the fallback direction is not a strict descent direction. Finite line-search budgets may fail even when a strong Wolfe step exists.

Output the last point and one of stationary, the line-search status, direction-failure, or iteration-budget-exhausted.

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $G:U\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$, $z_0\in U$, residual tolerance $\varepsilon\ge0$, correction budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$, and refresh period $q\in\mathbb N$, $q\ge1$. Use the coordinate Jacobian convention of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. Since $G$ is $C^1$, [[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] identifies this Jacobian with the matrix of $DG(z)$; write it as $J(z)$. Residual and Jacobian evaluations, norm comparisons and domain tests are returning primitives; no bound on their internal cost is specified. In chord mode also supply a terminating exact linear-system backend: on each square Jacobian it reports singularity if the matrix is singular, and otherwise returns a retained factor object, and each solve on that object terminates with the exact unique solution for its right-hand side. Factorization and solve work are charged individually. The output is a last valid iterate $z\in U$, a status, and the actual residual norm $\|G(z)\|_2$.

In **updated-Newton mode**, invoke [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] with $G,z_0,\varepsilon,N$. It recomputes the Jacobian at every correction and returns its stated residual/budget/failure status. Re-evaluate $G$ at the returned iterate to provide the output residual norm. Count each Jacobian assembly, factorization attempt, and linear solve actually performed.

In **chord mode**, for $k=0,1,\ldots,N$, first evaluate $G(z_k)$ and put $r_k=\|G(z_k)\|_2$. If $r_k\le\varepsilon$, return $(z_k,\texttt{root},r_k)$; this status means only that the residual tolerance was met. If $k=N$, return $(z_k,\texttt{iteration-budget-exhausted},r_k)$. Otherwise, at $k=0,q,2q,\ldots$, refresh by forming $J_k=DG(z_k)$, attempting to factor it, and retaining the factorization until the next scheduled refresh. The factorization backend must either report singularity or return a factor object whose solve operation gives the exact unique solution of $J_k s=-G(z_k)$. If it reports singularity, return $(z_k,\texttt{singular-jacobian},r_k)$. At each correction obtain $s_k$ by calling the solve operation on that retained factor object with right-hand side $-G(z_k)$; do not refactor or invoke a fresh matrix-only solve. The exact-solve backend contract makes this the mathematical correction in [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]]. If the correction $s_k$ has $z_k+s_k\notin U$, return $(z_k,\texttt{invalid-trial},r_k)$; otherwise set $z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k$ and continue. A refresh period $q=1$ updates the Jacobian every correction; $q>1$ is a chord iteration.

Both modes make no claim that a finite budget reaches an exact root or that a small residual is a forward-error bound. Record the number of Jacobian assemblies, factorization attempts, and linear solves actually performed; a dense LU correction uses one forward and one backward triangular solve. Sparse cost depends on the actual stage matrix and factorization backend and is not bounded here.

Let $n\ge1$, let $A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ be a linear map, and let
$r\in\mathbb R^n$ be a residual vector. If $A$ is not invertible in the sense
of [[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]], return
$(\texttt{singular-jacobian},\varnothing)$. If $A$ is invertible, return
$(\texttt{correction},s)$, where $s$ is the unique vector solving
$$As=-r.$$

The output is a linear correction, not a claim that $r$ came from a nonlinear
function or that applying the correction decreases a residual.

Definition

Input a stored complex square matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$,
with the admissibility hypothesis $\sigma(A)\cap i\mathbb R=\varnothing$, a
finite iteration budget $N\ge0$, and finite Householder-QR controls including a nonnegative integer candidate-operation budget $K_H$. The
procedure does not itself certify the spectral hypothesis. Set $X_0=A$. For
$k=0,\ldots,N-1$:

1. Call [[alg-pade-denominator-solve-by-householder-qr]] on $X_kY=I$, passing $K_H$ to its instrumented kernel dispatcher. If it
   does not return verified-solution, return its failure status with the last
   candidate.
2. Compute $X_{k+1}=\operatorname{fl}((X_k+Y)/2)$ componentwise in the
   operationwise model of
   [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
   A range failure returns range-failure with the last candidate.

After $N$ completed steps, return $X_N$ with status budget-exhausted and the
number of completed steps. The exact Newton sequence is analyzed separately;
the procedure makes no forward-error or floating-point convergence claim.

Definition

Work in finite-dimensional real Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, with its standard inner product and norm ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:D\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$ ([[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]), and write $g(x)=\nabla f(x)$ using the gradient convention of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]].

The inputs are $x_0\in D$, a method choice $\mathrm{FR}$ or $\mathrm{PR+}$, constants $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$, an outer iteration limit $K\in\mathbb N$, and a line-search mode. In bounded-strong-Wolfe mode, also supply finite expansion and zoom limits $E,Z\in\mathbb N$. In exact-SPD-quadratic mode, supply a real symmetric positive-definite matrix $A$ and vector $b$ such that $D=\mathbb R^n$ and $f(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx$. The $\mathrm{PR+}$ choice also takes $\sigma,C>0$. Evaluations and arithmetic are exact real operations; this definition makes no finite-precision error claim.

1. Evaluate $g_0=g(x_0)$. If $g_0=0$, return status **stationary** with $x_0$. Otherwise set $d_0=-g_0$.

2. For $k=0,\ldots,K-1$, if $g_k=0$, return **stationary** with $x_k$. For $k\ge1$, set
   $$ \beta_{k-1}^{\rm FR}=\frac{\|g_k\|_2^2}{\|g_{k-1}\|_2^2},\qquad \beta_{k-1}^{\rm PR+}=\max\!\left\{0,\frac{g_k^T(g_k-g_{k-1})}{\|g_{k-1}\|_2^2}\right\}. $$
   Choose the selected coefficient and form $d_k^{\rm cand}=-g_k+\beta_{k-1}d_{k-1}$. For $k=0$, use $d_0$ above. Denominators are nonzero because the procedure has already returned at any zero gradient.

3. In the $\mathrm{PR+}$ method, test the candidate at the current point. If $g_k^Td_k^{\rm cand}>-\sigma\|g_k\|_2^2$ or $\|d_k^{\rm cand}\|_2>C\|g_k\|_2$, restart by setting $\beta_{k-1}=0$ and $d_k=-g_k$, and record that a restart occurred. Otherwise set $d_k=d_k^{\rm cand}$. In the $\mathrm{FR}$ method set $d_k=d_k^{\rm cand}$ without this safeguard. If $g_k^Td_k\ge0$, return **search-failure** with cause **invalid-direction**.

4. In bounded-strong-Wolfe mode, call [[alg-bracketing-zoom-strong-wolfe-search]] at $(f,x_k,d_k,c_1,c_2)$ with budgets $E,Z$. That procedure returns a step only after checking both strong Wolfe inequalities. If it instead returns **invalid-direction**, **domain-exit**, or **evaluation-budget-exhausted**, return **search-failure** with that cause.

5. In exact-SPD-quadratic mode, when $g_k^Td_k<0$, compute
   $$ t_k=-\frac{g_k^Td_k}{d_k^TAd_k}. $$
   If the denominator is nonpositive or the computed step is not positive, return **search-failure** with cause **invalid-exact-model**. Otherwise verify the strong Wolfe inequalities and return **search-failure** if either fails. This mode records the exact-line-search specialization; it does not replace the finite-budget search mode.

6. For an accepted step, set $x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k$ and evaluate $g_{k+1}$. If $g_{k+1}=0$, return **stationary** with $x_{k+1}$. After the loop, return **iteration-limit** with the last iterate, the accepted trace, and all restart flags. A failure or stationary status returns immediately with the trace so far.

The FR and safeguarded PR+ convergence statements concern infinite sequences following the respective recurrences and direction rules above, with a successful strong Wolfe update at every index; they do not concern an infinite execution of this finite-$K$ procedure. Each finite execution can realize only a prefix of such a sequence. A finite search budget can return **search-failure**; it does not certify convergence.

Definition

Input a finite complex matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ whose stored entries
are representable in the operationwise model, a Padé order $m\ge0$, an integer
scaling count $s\ge0$, finite nonnegative integer Householder-candidate and squaring-operation budgets,
finite scalar-series budgets, and an
error policy that is either candidate-only or certify. The procedure never
selects adaptive Higham parameters. Certification data, including contour
vertices and the radius, have exact dyadic or rational encodings.

1. Interpret the stored entries of $A$ as their exact real/imaginary values and
   form $B=2^{-s}A$ exactly. Evaluate $P=p_m(B)$ and $Q=q_m(B)$ by exact
   controller matrix arithmetic: increasing-index sums/products and finite
   polynomial powers with their rational coefficients. Use the exact real-RAM
   controller declared in [[alg-pade-denominator-solve-by-householder-qr]];
   the optional rational adapter is used only when all required actual
   encodings are supplied. No dyadic representation is assumed for the
   abstract floating model.
2. Call [[alg-pade-denominator-solve-by-householder-qr]] on $QX=P$, explicitly passing the supplied finite Householder-candidate operation budget $K_H$. Continue only if the returned record contains a complete finite stored $n\times n$ matrix, with all entries marked complete, and status `verified-solution` or `candidate-unverified`. A partial candidate or any budget, range, representation or other failure is propagated with its original status and available partial record; do not square it. Retain a complete unverified candidate only in candidate-only mode; certification mode returns denominator-unverified. A complete matrix accompanying a failure status does not authorize continuation.
3. For $j=0,\ldots,s-1$, compute the next matrix square in the operationwise
   model. A range failure returns range-failure with the last candidate.
   Retain their exact stored real values and form
   $D_j=\widehat X_{j+1}-\widehat X_j^2$ by the exact controller's finite
   matrix loops. Set
   $\delta_j=\max_i\sum_k(|\operatorname{Re}(D_j)_{ik}|
   +|\operatorname{Im}(D_j)_{ik}|)$; this exact nonnegative real number bounds
   $\|D_j\|_{\infty,\mathbb C}$.
4. In candidate-only mode, return the final candidate with status
   unevaluated-error-bound. Certification mode has these caller preconditions,
   which the procedure does not itself verify: (a) a supplied polygonal Cauchy
   cycle $\Gamma$ with dyadic vertices, trace in a disk $|z|\le\rho$ for
   dyadic $\rho>0$, $\sigma(B)\subset\{|z|<\rho\}$, disjointness from
   $\sigma(B)$, index one on $\sigma(B)$, and null-homology in that disk;
   (b) $d_m(\rho)>0$; (c) a supplied finite dyadic resolvent-cover input for
   the singleton family $\{B\}$; and (d) a finite term budget $K$.
   The contour-validator call
   [[alg-complex-resolvent-cover-validator]] must return
   certified-resolvent-cover with bound $M$, or the procedure returns
   inconclusive-resolvent. The validator checks resolvent inequalities and
   segment coverage only; it does not validate the caller's topological
   preconditions or count enclosed eigenvalues. Here $\sigma(B)$ denotes the
   eigenvalue set of $B$ from
   [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]].
5. For $x=\rho$ and for
   $\alpha=\max_i\sum_j(|\operatorname{Re}A_{ij}|+
   |\operatorname{Im}A_{ij}|)$, compute an upper bound $U(x)$ for $e^x$ as
   follows. If $x=0$, set $U(x)=1$. Otherwise, if $x\ge K+2$, return
   inconclusive-scalar-tail. If $x<K+2$, put
   $r=x/(K+2)$,
   $U(x)=\sum_{k=0}^Kx^k/k!+
   [x^{K+1}/(K+1)!]/(1-r)$.
   The scalar-tail inequality used by the error theorem is proved separately there; this step defines the finite expression, rather than treating a Definition sentence as its proof.
6. Write the supplied finite polygonal chain as $\Gamma=\sum_\nu m_\nu\gamma_\nu$, with integer coefficients. Let $\ell=\sum_\nu |m_\nu|\sum_{e\text{ in }\gamma_\nu}(|\Delta\operatorname{Re}e|+|\Delta\operatorname{Im}e|)$; then
   $\ell$ is an exact rational upper bound for the coefficient-weighted contour length $L_\Gamma=\sum_\nu|m_\nu|L(\gamma_\nu)$ (the supplied vertices have rational/dyadic encodings). Put
   $\epsilon=\rho^{2m+1}U(\rho)(m!)^2/
   ((2m)!(2m+1)!d_m(\rho))$. Since
   $\pi/4=\int_0^1(1+x^2)^{-1}\,dx$, the finite identity
   $1/(1+x^2)=\sum_{k=0}^7(-1)^kx^{2k}+x^{16}/(1+x^2)$ on $[0,1]$ gives
   $\pi/4>33976/45045>3/4$, hence $1/(2\pi)<1/6$. Set
   $E_0=\ell\epsilon M/6$.
7. For each squaring use
   $E_{j+1}=(2U(\alpha)+E_j)E_j+\delta_j$.
   If every computed certification check succeeded, the denominator solve
   returned verified-solution, and the caller preconditions hold, return the
   final candidate with status conditional-error-bound and bound $E_s$.
   Otherwise retain the candidate and return
   the corresponding inconclusive status.

The exact controller uses only prescribed finite field-expression trees and
loops over dimensions, $m,s$ and the finite scalar-series term budget $K$;
absolute values/maxima use exact comparisons. It performs no additional
unprovided certification call. Count every rounded real primitive of a square
in row-major/increasing inner-index order against an explicitly supplied
finite squaring-operation budget, and propagate `budget-exhausted` before an
unaffordable operation. The solve uses its separately supplied finite
candidate-operation budget. Exact controller work is separate: its values
need not be rational, and no bit-computability or total bit-cost bound for
arbitrary real encodings is claimed. For the optional rational adapter with
all values encoded, these same finite formulas use exact rational arithmetic.
All loops are finite. The conditional-error-bound status is sound
only under the caller preconditions in step 4 and does not mean that the
procedure checked contour topology or eigenvalue count. No floating-point
stability is asserted for the candidate alone.

Definition

Let $f(x,\mu)$ be a $C^2$ one-parameter family in the map convention of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], and let $G(x,T,\mu)$ be the parameterized phase-bordered shooting map of [[def-validated-periodic-shooting-jet-enclosure]]. Applying [[thm-c2-ode-flow-on-common-tube]] to its static-parameter augmented field $g(x,\mu)=(f(x,\mu),0)$ makes this shooting map $C^2$ on a common compact tube. The branch residual is $F=G:\mathbb R^{d+2}\to\mathbb R^{d+1}$. A finite periodic-orbit continuation request supplies a validated seed section root, a unit orientation, step size, requested step count, finite continuation/corrector budgets, residual tolerance, angle margin, and the sound flow/jet range provider.

At a certified root, a tangent routine must certify a unit vector in $\ker DF$ and a rank-$d+1$ condition. The predictor is advanced along that tangent. The corrector is [[alg-validated-periodic-orbit-corrector]] in section mode, which appends the pseudo-arclength plane and validates the resulting square residual by Krawczyk inclusion. Forward its complete finite input package: the candidate mode and its required pointwise evaluators if that mode uses them (or choose its enclosure-guided mode), rational initial candidate and validation box, validated-jet step counts and arithmetic caps, preconditioner and exact inverse witness, minimum Krawczyk box width, and box/update budgets. For possibly nonrational tangent/predictor data, forward certified outward rational enclosures of the affine section row and its derivative; unavailable row bounds return inconclusive. The arithmetic evaluator supplies exact or interval-enclosed $F$ and $DF$ from the validated shooting jet. The local inverse and chart interfaces are [[lem-phase-bordered-shooting-jacobian-invertibility]] and [[thm-pseudo-arclength-local-newton-correction]]. Run [[alg-pseudo-arclength-continuation-with-certified-local-corrector]] with these callbacks and its chart, angle, inverse, and finite-budget checks.

When the fixed-parameter phase-bordered $(x,T)$ Jacobian is certified invertible, the full derivative $DF$ has row rank $d+1$: its $(x,T)$ columns already span $\mathbb R^{d+1}$. Thus a fold in the parameter projection does not by itself make the branch singular. Missing tangent/rank evidence, tube exit, failed Krawczyk inclusion, unresolved angle, or exhausted finite budgets returns the corresponding inconclusive status; no global branch-completeness claim is made. Any requested fold certificate is emitted only when the generic continuation algorithm's separate fold checks succeed.

The generic section keeps the supplied previous unit orientation fixed as its normal during each attempt, while the predictor uses the current certified tangent candidate. Forward this previous normal and certify its angle with the current true kernel, along with the generic predictor-offset/chart inequalities. Finite termination is conditional on every invoked flow/jet, tangent, section and fold callback returning in finite time; an outer work budget is not a timeout for a nonreturning callback.

rows.current_statement_or_definition:
Definition

This procedure has two admissible modes. All input values are finite stored floating-point numbers. Audits interpret them as exact dyadic rationals, and rounded operations obey [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].

**LP/QP mode.** Let $n\ge1$, $p\ge0$, $Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive semidefinite, and $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ have full row rank. The supplied data are $A,b,c,Q$ for $\min\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx$ subject to $Ax=b$, $x\ge0$; LP is $Q=0$. The iterate inputs are $x>0$, $s>0$, and free $y$. Also supply $0<\sigma<1$, $0<\eta<1$, finite tolerances $\epsilon_p,\epsilon_d,\epsilon_g\ge0$, and an integer update cap $N\ge0$.

**Symmetric-cone mode.** Let $K$ be a nonempty finite product of nonnegative orthant, Lorentz, or positive-semidefinite cones, let $A$ have full row rank, and use the primal-dual pair of [[def-conic-optimization-primal-dual-models]]. Supply $A,b,c,G,h$, a point $x$ with $s=h-Gx\in\operatorname{int}K$, a dual point $z\in\operatorname{int}K^*$, and free $y$. Equality feasibility $Ax=b$ is checked as a residual, not required of the initial point. Also supply $0<\sigma<1$, $0<\eta<1$, finite tolerances $\epsilon_p,\epsilon_d,\epsilon_g\ge0$, and integer cap $N\ge0$. The positive barrier parameter $\nu$ is the sum of the cone-factor parameters.

The input audit checks all dimensions, exact symmetry of $Q$, and full row rank of $A$ by rational elimination. It checks $Q\succeq0$ by finite exact symmetric Schur elimination: reject a negative diagonal; if a positive diagonal exists, permute it to the first position and recurse on its Schur complement; if every diagonal is zero, accept only when every off-diagonal entry is zero. This test is equivalent by completing the square at each positive pivot; with zero diagonal, a nonzero off-diagonal makes one of the vectors $e_i+e_j$ or $e_i-e_j$ have negative quadratic form. In symmetric-cone mode it also checks that each listed factor has a positive finite dimension, that the data match the declared product spaces, and that $A$ has full row rank. All these checks use exact rational arithmetic on the stored dyadic inputs.

In LP/QP mode form
$$r_d=Qx+c-A^Ty-s,\quad r_p=Ax-b,\quad \mu=x^Ts/n,\quad r_c=Xs-\sigma\mu\mathbf1.$$
In symmetric-cone mode form
$$r_d=A^Ty-G^*z-c,\quad r_p=Ax-b,\quad \mu=\langle s,z\rangle/\nu,\quad r_c=s\circ z-\sigma\mu e.$$
In either mode, $\epsilon_p$ bounds $\|r_p\|_2$, $\epsilon_d$ bounds both $\|r_d\|_2$ and $\|r_c\|$, and $\epsilon_g$ bounds the surrogate complementarity gap $n\mu=x^Ts$ in LP/QP mode or $\nu\mu=\langle s,z\rangle$ in symmetric-cone mode. On product cones use Euclidean norms on orthant and Lorentz factors and Frobenius norms on matrix factors. Norm tests compare exact squared values with squared tolerances. The output is a record containing `status`, the last accepted iterate when one exists, update count, audited residuals, and audited gap; it carries the exact audited gap as an objective-suboptimality bound only for status `certified-gap`. The possible statuses are `invalid-input`, `strict-start-unavailable`, `nonpositive-gap`, `certified-gap`, `residual-candidate`, `singular-system`, `lost-range`, `uncertified-newton-solve`, `boundary-status-unavailable`, and `budget-exhausted`. `invalid-input` has no iterate. A residual candidate is diagnostic, never a certificate.

**Interior audits.** For an orthant factor, require every coordinate to be positive. For a Lorentz factor $(t,u)$, require $t>0$ and $t^2-\|u\|_2^2>0$. For a symmetric matrix factor $Y$, test positive definiteness by exact rational Schur elimination: require $Y_{11}>0$, form $S=Y_{2:n,2:n}-Y_{2:n,1}Y_{1,2:n}/Y_{11}$, and repeat on $S$ until the matrix is empty. Completing the square gives $v^TYv=Y_{11}(v_1+Y_{1,2:n}v_{2:n}/Y_{11})^2+v_{2:n}^TSv_{2:n}$, so this finite test succeeds exactly for $Y\succ0$.

**Instructions.** First reject invalid dimensions, nonfinite data, parameters outside their stated domains, or a negative cap with `invalid-input`. Reject an LP/QP start unless $x,s>0$, or a cone start unless $s,z$ pass the interior audits, with `strict-start-unavailable`; this is not an infeasibility claim. Set the accepted-update count to zero and repeat the following audit and update loop.

Compute the residuals and complementarity gap exactly as rational expressions in the stored inputs; compare exact squared norms with squared tolerances. A nonpositive or nonfinite gap returns `nonpositive-gap`. Return `certified-gap` in LP/QP mode only when $Ax=b$, $x,s\ge0$, $Qx+c-A^Ty-s=0$, and $x^Ts\le\epsilon_g$; in cone mode require $Ax=b$, $s=h-Gx\in K$, $z\in K^*$, $A^Ty-G^*z=c$, and $\langle s,z\rangle\le\epsilon_g$. Otherwise, if $\|r_p\|_2\le\epsilon_p$, $\|r_d\|_2\le\epsilon_d$, $\|r_c\|\le\epsilon_d$, and the surrogate gap is at most $\epsilon_g$, return `residual-candidate`. If the update count equals $N$, return `budget-exhausted`.

Assemble the Newton derivative specified in [[def-barrier-central-path-and-newton-residuals]]. In LP/QP mode solve its displayed block system. In symmetric-cone mode solve
$$A\Delta x=-r_p,\qquad A^T\Delta y-G^*\Delta z=-r_d,\qquad \Delta s=-G\Delta x,\qquad \Delta s\circ z+s\circ\Delta z=-r_c.$$
The exact equations form a square system after eliminating $\Delta s$. Form each system coefficient as an exact dyadic expression in the stored inputs, then round that coefficient once to the nearest normal representable value, preserving exact zeros; any failed conversion returns `lost-range`. Convert the exact rational right-hand side $(-r_d,-r_p,-r_c)$ componentwise by the same nearest-normal rule, preserving exact zeros; a failed conversion also returns `lost-range`. In LP/QP mode, [[lem-primal-dual-lp-qp-newton-matrix-nonsingular]] proves nonsingularity of the exact Newton matrix under the stated rank and strict-start hypotheses; in either mode an exact rank audit detects a singular stored system.

Stored floating-point numbers are treated as exact dyadic rationals (rationals with denominator a power of two) for audits; the unit roundoff $u$ and failure behavior of elementary operations are those of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. For a matrix $M$, $\|M\|_F^2$ is the sum of the squares of its entries. Check exact rank by rational row elimination: scan columns from left to right, find the first nonzero entry at or below the next pivot row, swap it into that row, subtract exact multiples to clear entries below, and count pivots. If fewer pivots than rows are found, return `singular-system`. For a full-rank matrix, use a reduced QR solve: for each active column apply [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] to the column and trailing block, store the reflector, apply the stored reflectors in order to the right-hand side using the same sequential dot, scale, multiply, and subtraction order as that procedure, and solve the resulting upper-triangular system by descending substitution $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(q_i-\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j>i}\widehat R_{ij}\widehat d_j))$, $\widehat d_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/\widehat R_{ii})$. A range exception returns `lost-range`; a zero pivot returns `singular-system`. Let $d$ be the system dimension and $\gamma_{d+3}=(d+3)u/(1-(d+3)u)$. Require $(d+3)u<1$, $\gamma_{d+3}<1/8$, and, for the computed triangular factor $\widehat R$, verify with exact dyadic arithmetic that
$$\gamma_{d+3}^2\|\widehat R\|_F^2\|\widehat R^{-1}\|_F^2<1.$$
If the test fails, return `uncertified-newton-solve`. Otherwise [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] applies: the returned direction solves a nearby system with a nonsingular perturbed factor. Compute exactly and report the direction residual both against the rounded stored Newton system and against the original exact rational Newton equations.

For LP/QP mode set
$$\bar\alpha=\min\left(1,\min_{\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i},\min_{\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i}\right),$$
where an empty minimum is $+\infty$, and use $\alpha=\eta\bar\alpha$. In symmetric-cone mode compute a positive safe fraction $\beta$ for each primal-slack and dual factor, and use $\alpha=\eta$ times the minimum of those bounds. For an orthant factor use the same coordinate ratios. For a Lorentz factor at $(t,u)\in\operatorname{int}\mathcal L$ with direction $(\dot t,v)$, set $q=t^2-\|u\|_2^2$ and $c=|\dot t|+\sum_i|v_i|$; take $\beta=1$ if $c=0$, and otherwise $\beta=\min(1,q/(2tc))$. For a positive-semidefinite factor at $Y\succ0$ with symmetric direction $D$, let $L(M)=\sum_{i,j}|M_{ij}|$, compute $Y^{-1}$ by exact rational elimination, and set $C=L(Y^{-1})L(D)$; take $\beta=1$ if $C=0$ and otherwise $\beta=\min(1,1/C)$. These calculations are finite and use exact rational comparisons; their safety is proved by the fraction-to-boundary theorem on the A page.

Round $\alpha$ downward to a positive normal representable value; if none exists, return `lost-range`. Update each stored coordinate as $\operatorname{fl}(v+\operatorname{fl}(\alpha\Delta v))$ under the operationwise model. Any failed operation returns `lost-range`. Before accepting the candidate update, verify exactly that LP/QP variables $x,s$ remain positive, or that cone variables remain interior and $s=h-Gx$ still holds. Input a finite complex matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$, a branch request selecting principal

$F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^2$ in the componentwise sense of

[[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]]. Require $C^3$ on any subtube
where a fold check is requested. A valid seed consists of a center
$\bar z_0$, a radius $r_0$, and a certified ball containing exactly one
zero $z_0^*$ of an initial augmented section
$$G_{-1}(z):=\bigl(F(z),\tau_{-1}^T(z-z_{p,-1})\bigr),$$
where $\tau_{-1}$ is unit and the section is transverse to the regular local
solution branch. Thus the seed certifies one solution point of $F=0$ by
intersecting the branch with a hyperplane; it does not claim that $F=0$ has an
isolated zero in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$. The seed also includes a neighborhood
in which every zero of $F$ lies on the certified local curve chart and a
