Write $\partial_x f=u_x+iv_x$ and $\partial_y f=u_y+iv_y$ after transport back to $U$.

At a point where the four real partial derivatives exist, define

$$ \partial_z f:=\frac12(\partial_x f-i\partial_y f)=\frac12(u_x+v_y)+\frac{i}{2}(v_x-u_y), $$

$$ \partial_{\bar z}f:=\frac12(\partial_x f+i\partial_y f)=\frac12(u_x-v_y)+\frac{i}{2}(v_x+u_y). $$

Real total differentiability means total differentiability of $\widetilde f$ under [[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]], with a real-linear derivative as in [[def-euclidean-linear-map]]. Its transported real-linear map $Df$ is supplied by [[thm-complex-coordinate-map-preserves-real-total-differentiability]]. If $f$ is real totally differentiable, put $A=\partial_x f$ and $B=\partial_y f$. The remainder definition along the two coordinate axes gives $Df(1)=A$ and $Df(i)=B$. Real linearity then gives $Df(s+it)=sA+tB$ for real $s,t$, whereas direct expansion of $\frac12(A-iB)(s+it)+\frac12(A+iB)(s-it)$ gives the same expression. Thus

$$ Df(h)=(\partial_z f)h+(\partial_{\bar z}f)\overline h. $$

A real-differentiable map is **antiholomorphic** on $U$ when $\partial_z f=0$ at every point of $U$. Thus its differential is conjugate-linear at every point; no complex differentiability is asserted unless the other Wirtinger derivative also vanishes.

Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Definition

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:D\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$
([[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]), let $x\in D$, and let
$p\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$. Define the open parameter set $S_{x,p}:=\{t\in\mathbb R:x+tp\in D\}$,
which contains $0$, the feasible ray $T_{x,p}:=S_{x,p}\cap[0,\infty)$,
and $\phi(t):=f(x+tp)$ for $t\in S_{x,p}$. At every $t\in S_{x,p}$,
including $0$, the chain rule gives $\phi'(t)=Df(x+tp)p$.
By [[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],
the matrix of $Df$ is the Jacobian, whose scalar-field row is the transpose
of the gradient. Hence
$\phi'(t)=\langle\nabla f(x+tp),p\rangle$, using the gradient convention
of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and the Euclidean inner product of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. A direction is a **descent direction** at
$x$ when $\phi'(0)=\langle\nabla f(x),p\rangle<0$.

Assume for the line-search conditions below that $p$ is a descent direction
at $x$.
Fix constants $0<c_1<c_2<1/2$. A feasible step $t>0$ is a **Wolfe step**
when
$$
\phi(t)\le\phi(0)+c_1t\phi'(0),\qquad \phi'(t)\ge c_2\phi'(0).
$$
It is a **strong Wolfe step** when it satisfies the first inequality and
$$
|\phi'(t)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|.
$$
The first inequality is the Armijo sufficient-decrease condition. The second
Wolfe inequality is the curvature condition. Every strong Wolfe step is a
Wolfe step, because $\phi'(0)<0$ and the strong curvature bound implies
$\phi'(t)\ge-c_2|\phi'(0)|=c_2\phi'(0)$.

For a descent direction define its **descent angle** $\theta\in[0,\pi/2)$ by
$$
\cos\theta:=-\frac{\langle\nabla f(x),p\rangle}{\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\|p\|_2}.
$$
The denominator is nonzero for a descent direction. The Cauchy–Schwarz
inequality [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]] ensures $0<\cos\theta\le1$.

$F(P)$ from [[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]] and

frame $X\in\operatorname{St}_{\mathbb C}(n,r)$ represents $P=XX^*$, and
unitary frame changes preserve $P$. The model-specific Grassmann gradient is
$$\operatorname{grad}E([X])=2(I-P)F(P)X.$$

$x_0=[X_0]$. Choose $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$,
$0<\gamma_{\rm dec}<1<\gamma_{\rm inc}$, $0<\theta_C\le1$,
$\Delta_{\max}>0$, $0<\Delta_0\le\Delta_{\max}$, and
$0<\varepsilon\le1$; use an outer cap at least the bound in
[[thm-riemannian-trust-region-first-order-complexity]].

[[alg-riemannian-trust-region]], with the inner subproblem routine returning
failure immediately so the method uses its explicit Cauchy fallback. Since
$M_B=0$, the small-radius safeguard also selects the Cauchy step at every
positive radius. The polar map preserves the projector's Hermitian, idempotent,
rank-$r$ constraints at every trial; rejected trials
leave the current projector unchanged. Because the finite-basis energy is
$C^2$ on a neighborhood and the complex Grassmannian is compact, its pullback
gradients are uniformly Lipschitz on every fixed bounded tangent disk. Choose

hypotheses of [[thm-riemannian-trust-region-first-order-complexity]] hold, and
its first-order target is reached within the theorem's explicit

cap is chosen accordingly. This is a finite-dimensional optimization
guarantee; no claim is made that an arbitrary selected exchange-correlation

v_1=\frac{h}{1+h},\qquad i_1=\frac1{1+h}.

solve the Newton equation approximately from $p^{(0)}=0$ by
$$
p^{(j+1)}=p^{(j)}-(1-\omega)(p^{(j)}+x),\qquad 0<\omega<1.
$$

satisfies $0<\eta\le c_2<1/2$. With the exact strong Wolfe search from
[[alg-bracketing-zoom-strong-wolfe-search]], the unit step is accepted. The
number $j$ of inner iterations grows as $\eta$ is tightened, while the outer
error contracts by a factor at most $\eta$; choosing $\eta_k=|x_k|$ gives a
quadratic outer error bound for $0<|x_0|\le c_2$.

For each finite horizon $N\ge1$, let $j_k$ be the least integer with
$\omega^{j_k}\le\eta_k$ on the first $N$ steps of the displayed recurrence,
and choose the single inner budget $M_N\ge\max_{0\le k<N}j_k$.
Use $M=M_N$, $\bar\eta=c_2$, $\sigma=1/2$, $J=0$, $E,Z\ge1$,
$\gamma=2$, and $\lambda_0=\lambda_{\max}=1$.

performs the displayed iteration until $|p+x|\le\tau$, where $\tau$ is its
absolute requested residual tolerance, or until $M$ iterations are used;

contract (and $p^{(0)}=0\in K_0$).

claim do not assert realization by one fixed finite inner budget.

Example

Encode a one-dimensional zero-boundary function by its derivative. The exact Hilbert space is the mean-zero subspace $V:=\{g\in L^2(0,1):\int_0^1g=0\}$, with $a(g,h)=\int_0^1gh$. Its associated function is $U_g(x):=\int_0^xg(t)\,dt$. The source functional is $F(h):=\int_0^16xU_h(x)\,dx$. Its exact solution is $g_u(x)=1-3x^2$, whose associated function is $U_{g_u}(x)=x-x^3$.

For the nonconforming discrete space, take broken piecewise-affine functions on $[0,1/2]\cup[1/2,1]$ that vanish at $0$ and $1$, with no continuity imposed at $1/2$. Identify each such function with its two cellwise slopes, a two-dimensional space $V_h$ of piecewise-constant fields. For $\omega_h=s_L\mathbf1_{[0,1/2]}+s_R\mathbf1_{(1/2,1]}$, define its associated broken function by $U_{\omega_h}(x)=s_Lx$ on the left cell and $U_{\omega_h}(x)=s_R(x-1)$ on the right cell. Use $\widetilde a_h(g,\omega_h):=\int_0^1g\omega_h$ and $F_h(\omega_h):=\int_0^16xU_{\omega_h}(x)\,dx$. The left basis function $\phi_L(x)=2x$ on the first cell and $0$ on the second corresponds to slope field $\omega_L=2\mathbf1_{[0,1/2]}$; it has residual $F_h(\omega_L)-\widetilde a_h(g_u,\omega_L)=-1/4$. Thus the exact solution does not satisfy the broken discrete equation on $V_h$: its consistency residual is nonzero. This is the term retained by the second Strang estimate in place of an exact Galerkin identity. The conforming Céa hypothesis $V_h\subseteq V$ is also false.

Statement

Let $0<\alpha<1$ and let $(\omega_j)$ be the weights from
[[alg-backward-euler-convolution-quadrature]]. Then $\omega_0=1$,
$\omega_j<0$ for every $j\ge1$, and for every complex $z$ with $|z|<1$,
$$\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\omega_jz^j=(1-z)^\alpha_{\operatorname{Log}}.$$
For $n\ge0$ define
$$p_n:=\sum_{j=0}^n\omega_j.$$
Then
$$p_n=\prod_{k=1}^n\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{k}\right) =\frac{\Gamma(n+1-\alpha)}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)\Gamma(n+1)}>0,$$
where the empty product for $n=0$ is $1$. For every $n\ge1$,
$$p_n\ge\frac{(n+1)^{-\alpha}}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)}.$$

Let $F=-\nabla V:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be globally Lipschitz, have linear growth $|F(q)|\le C(1+|q|)$, and have bounded first and second derivatives. Fix the model data in [[def-underdamped-langevin-equation-and-canonical-gibbs-density]], a finite starting state $Z_t=(q,p)$, and $0<h\le1$. Couple the exact SDE and one BAOAB step by the same Brownian increment, taking the BAOAB OU noise to be the standardized exact OU integral from [[lem-exact-ornstein-uhlenbeck-momentum-substep]]. Put $b(q,p)=(M^{-1}p,F(q)-\gamma p)$ and $G=(0,S)^T$ with $S=\sqrt{2\gamma\beta^{-1}}M^{1/2}$. There are remainders $R^B,R^E$ such that
$$Z^B_{t+h}=Z_t+h b(Z_t)+G(W_{t+h}-W_t)+R^B,\qquad Z_{t+h}=Z_t+h b(Z_t)+G(W_{t+h}-W_t)+R^E,$$
and, conditionally on the starting sigma algebra,
$$|\mathbb E[R^B\mid\mathcal F_t]|+|\mathbb E[R^E\mid\mathcal F_t]|\le C h^2(1+|Z_t|),\qquad \mathbb E[|R^B|^2+|R^E|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\le C h^3(1+|Z_t|^2).$$
For fixed Brownian noise in the step, the BAOAB residual also satisfies $|R^B(z)-R^B(\tilde z)|\le Ch|z-\tilde z|$ for all starting states $z,\tilde z$. Constants depend on the model parameters and force bounds, not on the starting state or $h$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ have continuous first and second partial derivatives. Put $g(x):=\nabla f(x)$ and $G(x):=\nabla^2 f(x)$, using the conventions of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and [[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]. Let $K\subseteq U$ be convex. Suppose that for every $x\in K$, $G(x)$ is symmetric and, for constants $0<\mu\le\Lambda<\infty$,
$$ \mu\|w\|_2^2\le w^TG(x)w\quad(w\in\mathbb R^n),\qquad \|G(x)\|_2\le\Lambda, $$
where $\|A\|_2:=\sup_{\|w\|_2=1}\|Aw\|_2$. Then for all $u,v\in K$, with $d:=u-v$,
$$ \|g(u)-g(v)\|_2\le\Lambda\|d\|_2, \qquad (g(u)-g(v))^Td\ge\mu\|d\|_2^2, $$
and
$$ \frac\mu2\|d\|_2^2\le f(u)-f(v)-g(v)^Td\le\frac\Lambda2\|d\|_2^2. $$
Separately, let $W\subseteq U$ be convex, let $x_*\in W$, and suppose $G$ is $L_G$-Lipschitz on $W$ in operator norm. Then for all $u,v\in W$, with $d:=u-v$,
$$ \|g(u)-g(v)-G(x_*)d\|_2 \le L_G\max\{\|u-x_*\|_2,\|v-x_*\|_2\}\,\|d\|_2. $$

Let $B_1,\ldots,B_m$ be independent centered random Hermitian $q\times q$ matrices, $q,m\ge1$. Suppose $R>0$, $v\ge0$, and
$$\|B_i\|_{\rm op}\le R\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad\|\mathbb E B_i^2\|_{\rm op}\le v\quad(1\le i\le m).$$
Writing $Y=\sum_{i=1}^m B_i$, for $0<s<3/R$ one has
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\exp(sY)\le q\exp\left(\frac{ms^2v}{2(1-sR/3)}\right).$$
Consequently, for $u>0$ when $v>0$,
$$\mathbb P\{\lambda_{\max}(Y)\ge u\}\le q\exp\left(-\frac{u^2}{2(mv+Ru/3)}\right).$$
For every $b>0$, the following convenient forms also hold:
$$\mathbb P\left\{\lambda_{\max}(Y)>\sqrt{2mvb}+\frac{2Rb}{3}\right\}\le qe^{-b},\qquad\mathbb P\left\{\|Y\|_{\rm op}>\sqrt{2mvb}+\frac{2Rb}{3}\right\}\le2qe^{-b}.$$
If $v=0$, all $B_i$ and $Y$ vanish almost surely, so the displayed positive-threshold conclusions remain valid.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. If $U\subseteq\Omega$ is open, then
restriction defines a contraction
$$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K),\qquad u\longmapsto u|_U.$$ 
If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, multiplication defines a bounded
map $u\mapsto\eta u$ on $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. More precisely, for
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ with $|\alpha|\le k$ put
$$C_\alpha(\eta):=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}\|D^\beta\eta\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}.$$
Then
$$\|\eta u\|_{W^{k,p}}\le\begin{cases}\left(\displaystyle\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}C_\alpha(\eta)^p\right)^{1/p}\|u\|_{W^{k,p}},&1\le p<\infty,\\\displaystyle\max_{|\alpha|\le k}C_\alpha(\eta)\,\|u\|_{W^{k,\infty}},&p=\infty.\end{cases}$$
The displayed constants involve only finitely many sup norms of derivatives of
$\eta$ through order $k$. AC is used only to invoke the Countable Choice
interfaces for weak-derivative uniqueness, the Sobolev quotient norm, and the
smooth-factor Leibniz rule.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then $U=\varnothing$ and both maps are the unique
maps on the zero Sobolev space.

A bounded function continuous on the closed strip, holomorphic inside, and of modulus at most one on both boundary lines has modulus at most one throughout the strip.

Precisely, let $S=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Re}z\le1\}$. If $g:S\to\mathbb C$ is bounded and continuous, is holomorphic on $0<\operatorname{Re}z<1$, and satisfies
$$|g(iy)|\le1,\qquad |g(1+iy)|\le1\qquad(y\in\mathbb R),$$
then $|g(z)|\le1$ for every $z\in S$.

Let $Q_{ad}=Q_{ad}(q_a,q_b)\subset L^2(E;\mathbb R)$ be as in [[def-pde-box-control-set]], and let $r\in L^2(E)$. Define
$$
P_{Q_{ad}}r(x)=\min\{q_b(x),\max\{q_a(x),r(x)\}\}\quad\text{a.e.}
$$

$$
(q-r,v-q)_{L^2(E)}\ge0\qquad(v\in Q_{ad}).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $p_t$ and $P_t$ be the Brownian transition
kernel and operators of [[def-brownian-transition-semigroup]].

1. **Expectation form.** If $B$ is a standard Brownian motion
   [[def-brownian-motion]], then for every $t\ge0$, every $x\in\mathbb R$ and
   every bounded Borel $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
   $$P_tf(x)=E\bigl[f(x+B_t)\bigr].$$
2. **Semigroup identity.** For all $s,t\ge0$, $P_sP_t=P_{s+t}$ as operators on
   bounded Borel functions.
3. **Kernel identity.** For all $s,t>0$ and all $x,z\in\mathbb R$,
   $$\int_{\mathbb R}p_s(x,y)\,p_t(y,z)\,dy=p_{s+t}(x,z).$$
   Conversely, the kernel identity for all $x,z$ implies the semigroup identity
   for all bounded Borel $f$.
4. **Probability kernels.** $P_t1=1$ for every $t\ge0$, so each $P_t$ is a
   probability kernel operator and $\|P_tf\|_\infty\le\|f\|_\infty$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open
and let $\Phi:U\to V$ be a $C^k$ diffeomorphism with inverse
$\Psi:=\Phi^{-1}:V\to U$. Fix open sets $U_0\subset\subset U$ and
$V_0\subset\subset V$ with $\Phi(U_0)\subseteq V_0$, and suppose that on
$\overline{U_0}$ the derivatives of $\Phi$ through order $k$ are bounded and
that on $\overline{V_0}$ the derivatives of $\Psi$ through order $k$ are
bounded; in the situation of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] these are exactly the compact
patches on which the flattening chart and its inverse have bounded derivatives
through order $k$. Then:

1. for every $u\in W^{k,p}(V_0;\mathbb K)$ the composition
$u\circ\Phi$ belongs to $W^{k,p}(U_0;\mathbb K)$, and for every
$1\le|\alpha|\le k$ its weak derivatives satisfy, almost everywhere on
$U_0$,
$$D^\alpha(u\circ\Phi)=\sum_{1\le|\beta|\le|\alpha|}\bigl((D^\beta u)\circ\Phi\bigr)\,P_{\alpha\beta}\bigl(D\Phi,\dots,D^k\Phi\bigr),$$
where $P_{\alpha\beta}$ is a universal polynomial with integer coefficients,
whose values on $\overline{U_0}$ are bounded by a constant depending only on
$n,k$ and the stated bounds for $\Phi$;

2. there is a constant $C$, depending only on $n$, $k$, $p$ and the two sets of
chart bounds, with
$$\|u\circ\Phi\|_{W^{k,p}(U_0)}\le C\,\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(V_0)}\qquad\text{for all }u\in W^{k,p}(V_0;\mathbb K).$$
If in addition $\Psi(V_0)\subseteq U_0$ (equivalently, under the stated
$\Phi(U_0)\subseteq V_0$, $\Phi(U_0)=V_0$), the same assertion holds for
composition with $\Psi$ from $W^{k,p}(U_0)$ to $W^{k,p}(V_0)$.

For $k=1$ only the first derivatives of $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ enter, so bounded
$C^1$ chart and inverse data suffice; no $C^1$-only claim is made for $k>1$.

Assume Countable Choice. In the setting of
[[lem-weak-divergence-form-equations-are-invariant-under-c-two-boundary-charts]]
with $W$ compactly contained in the domain of a flattening chart of a bounded
$C^2$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), suppose
$\Lambda\ge1$ bounds $|D\Phi|,|D\psi|,|\det D\Phi|$ and $|\det D\psi|$
together with their reciprocals on the relevant closure:
$\Lambda^{-1}\le|\det D\psi(y)|\le\Lambda$ and
$|\zeta|\le\Lambda|D\Phi(\psi(y))\zeta|$ for all $\zeta$. Then the transformed
coefficients $\widetilde a^{\,ij}$ of
[[lem-weak-divergence-form-equations-are-invariant-under-c-two-boundary-charts]]
satisfy, for a.e. $y$ in the flattened half-ball,
$$\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}\widetilde a^{ij}(y)\xi_j\overline{\xi_i}\ \ge\ \theta\,\Lambda^{-2}\inf|\det D\psi|\ |\xi|^2\qquad(\xi\in\mathbb C^n),$$
so the transformed operator is uniformly elliptic with an explicitly
computable constant depending only on $n,\theta,\Lambda$, while the transformed coefficients satisfy
$|\widetilde a^{\,ij}|\le n^2M_a\Lambda^3$. The first-order and zero-order
coefficients satisfy $|\widetilde b^{\,i}|\le nM_b\Lambda^2$ and
$|\widetilde c|\le M_c\Lambda$, hence also the scaffold's non-sharp bounds
$C(n)(M_a+M_b)\Lambda^3$ for $|\widetilde b^{\,i}|$ and
$C(n)(M_a+M_b+M_c)\Lambda^3$ for $|\widetilde c|$, since $\Lambda\ge1$.
The constants are not asserted sharp. Ellipticity alone does not imply the
coefficient regularity required for an $H^2$ estimate. If additionally
$a\in W^{1,\infty}$ on the original patch, then the transformed principal
coefficients are $W^{1,\infty}$ on the compact half-patch, with bounds also
depending on $\|Da\|_\infty$ and the second chart/inverse derivatives.

Let $a<b$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be open, and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^1$. Let $K\subseteq\Omega$ be compact and convex, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open. $$S(t;s)=I_d+\int_a^t D_yf(r,\phi(r;s))S(r;s)\,dr,$$

and hence satisfies $\partial_tS=D_yf(t,\phi(t;s))S$, $S(a;s)=I_d$. The claim is local to the stated common compact tube; it does not assert differentiability beyond it.

Let $R:J\to\mathbb R^d$ be a unit-speed $C^3$ curve on an open interval $J$ containing $[0,1]$, and suppose $\max_j\sup_{s\in J_0}|R_j'''(s)|\le M_3/\sqrt d$ on the stencil interval $J_0$. For $s-h,s+h\in J_0$, define

$$d_h:=\frac{R(s+h)-R(s-h)}{2h},\qquad \widehat t_h:=\frac{d_h}{\|d_h\|_2}.$$

If $\delta_h:=M_3h^2/6\le1/2$, then $d_h\ne0$ and

$$\|d_h-R'(s)\|_2\le\delta_h,\qquad \|\widehat t_h-R'(s)\|_2\le4\delta_h.$$

For unequal positive steps $h_-,h_+$ with $s-h_-,s+h_+\in J_0$, define

$$d_{h_-,h_+}:=\frac{h_+}{h_-(h_-+h_+)}(R(s)-R(s-h_-))+\frac{h_-}{h_+(h_-+h_+)}(R(s+h_+)-R(s)).$$

If $\delta_{h_-,h_+}:=M_3h_-h_+/6\le1/2$, then it is nonzero and its unit normalization differs from $R'(s)$ by at most $4\delta_{h_-,h_+}$. In particular, equal steps give an $O(h^2)$ unit-tangent error; quasiuniform unequal steps give an $O(h_-h_+)$ error. No second-order claim is made for a one-sided tangent branch.

$$\|I-AB\|_2\le d<1,\qquad \|b-A\widehat x\|_2\le\rho,\qquad \|B\|_2\le M,\qquad K=\frac{M}{1-d}.$$
Then $A$ is invertible; writing $x=A^{-1}b$, the fixed linear derivative approximations $\widetilde J_bh=Bh$ and $\widetilde J_AH=-BH\widehat x$ obey
$$\|\widetilde J_b-J_b\|\le\eta_b=Kd,\qquad \|\widetilde J_A-J_A\|\le\eta_A=Kd\|\widehat x\|_2+K^2\rho.$$
Use Euclidean vector norms and Frobenius matrix-input norm. For any stored matrix $B$ and stored cotangent $c\in\mathbb R^n$, the exact adjoints are $B^Tc$ and $-(B^Tc)\widehat x^T$. Let $u$ be the unit roundoff in [[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]], and assume $nu<1$. For each $j=1,\ldots,n$, compute $\widehat\lambda_j$ by the sequential real dot rule: $p_i=\operatorname{fl}(B_{ij}c_i)$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$, $s_1=p_1$, and $s_i=\operatorname{fl}(s_{i-1}+p_i)$ for $i=2,\ldots,n$, with each product and addition rounded separately; set $\widehat\lambda_j=s_n$. Assume every operation succeeds in the operationwise model [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]: each exact intermediate is zero or normal and every rounded output is finite. $2\kappa\theta\ge\sigma^2$, and put
$$a=\frac{4\kappa\theta-\sigma^2}{8}.$$

included for the numerical root statement; the CIR solution theorem below

Assume countable choice, let $n\ge1$, and use Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^n$. Translation $\tau_hf(x)=f(x-h)$ is an isometry of complex $L^p$ for $1\le p\le\infty$ and depends norm-continuously on $h$ for $p<\infty$.

For complex $K\in L^1$ and $f\in L^p$, the convolution
$$(K*f)(x)=\int K(y)f(x-y)\,dy$$
exists absolutely a.e., defines a measurable class independent of representatives, and satisfies $\|K*f\|_p\le\|K\|_1\|f\|_p$.

If $K_\varepsilon\in L^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$ satisfy
$$\int K_\varepsilon=1,\qquad M:=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\|K_\varepsilon\|_1<\infty,\qquad \int_{|y|\ge\delta}|K_\varepsilon(y)|\,dy\longrightarrow0\quad(\delta>0),$$
then $K_\varepsilon*f\to f$ in $L^p$ for $p<\infty$, and uniformly for $f\in C_0(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. For fixed $K\in L^1$, $K*f\in C_0$ when $f\in C_0$. These assertions allow complex and sign-changing kernels. In particular $K_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}K(x/\varepsilon)$ is such an approximate identity whenever $K\in L^1$ and $\int K=1$.

If $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R)$ has mass one, $\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$, and $f$ is complex locally integrable, then $\rho_\varepsilon*f$ is smooth and
$$\partial^\alpha(\rho_\varepsilon*f)=(\partial^\alpha\rho_\varepsilon)*f.$$
A compactly supported input gives a compactly supported output. No general $L^\infty$ translation-continuity or approximate-identity convergence is asserted.

$$\delta_h^i\big(\eta^2\delta_h^iu\big)=\eta^2\delta_h^i\delta_h^iu+(\delta_h^i\eta^2)\,(\tau_{-he_i}\delta_h^iu).$$
The statement is quantitative in $\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty}$ and does not assume
any regularity of $u$ beyond $W^{1,p}$.

**Sobolev multiplier and support facts used below.** For every integer
$m\ge0$, $q\in W^{m,\infty}(U)$ and $z\in H^m(U)$ on an open set $U$,
$qz\in H^m(U)$ and
$$D^\alpha(qz)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}(D^\beta q)D^{\alpha-\beta}z,\qquad |\alpha|\le m,$$
with $\|qz\|_{H^m(U)}\le C(n,m)\|q\|_{W^{m,\infty}(U)}\|z\|_{H^m(U)}$.
Also, every compactly supported $z\in H^m(U)$ lies in $H^m_0(U)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $n\ge1$,
let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and fix $h\ne0$ and
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. Write
$\Omega_{i,h}=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}$ and
$\Omega_{i,-h}=\{x\in\Omega:x-he_i\in\Omega\}$
([[def-first-difference-quotient]]), so that
$\Omega_{i,-h}=\Omega_{i,h}+he_i$. Then:

(i) **Integration by parts, two-domain form.** Whenever the displayed
integrals converge absolutely,
$$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx+\frac1h\Big(\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}uv\,dx-\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}uv\,dx\Big).$$
Consequently, if
$$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}uv\,dx=\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}uv\,dx,$$
in particular if $uv$ vanishes almost everywhere outside
$\Omega_{i,h}\cap\Omega_{i,-h}$ — for instance when $uv$ has compact support in
$\Omega$ and $|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}(uv),\partial\Omega)$
— or if $\Omega_{i,h}=\Omega_{i,-h}$, then
$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx$,
with the integrals taken over their respective shrunken sets. For $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$
and $u\in L^p(\Omega)$, $v\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$p'$ the Hölder conjugate exponent of [[def-conjugate-exponents]]
($1/p+1/p'=1$), both sides are absolutely convergent and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx.$$

(ii) **Product rule.** If $uv\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, then a.e. on
$\Omega_{i,h}$,
$$\delta_h^i(uv)=\big(\tau_{-he_i}u\big)\,\delta_h^iv+\big(\delta_h^iu\big)\,v=u\,\delta_h^iv+\big(\delta_h^iu\big)\big(\tau_{-he_i}v\big),$$
with the translation $\tau_{-he_i}$ of [[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]].
The identity is a pointwise a.e. algebraic identity; no local integrability of
its shifted cross-products is asserted beyond the hypothesis $uv\in L^1_{\rm loc}$,
which makes the left side well defined.

(iii) **Commutation with weak derivatives.** If $u$ and all its weak
derivatives $D^\gamma u$ with $|\gamma|\le|\alpha|$ have locally integrable
representatives on $\Omega$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), then
$$D^\alpha(\delta_h^iu)=\delta_h^i(D^\alpha u)\qquad\text{weakly on }\Omega_{i,h}.$$

All identities are identities of almost-everywhere classes
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and the proof uses no
choice beyond the Sobolev interfaces.

Let $V\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, let $x\in U$, and let $v\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|v\|_2=1$ and $x\pm\epsilon v\in U$ for $\epsilon>0$. Assume the segments $x+[-\epsilon,\epsilon]v$ lie in $U$. Define

$$D_\epsilon(x,v):=\frac{\nabla V(x+\epsilon v)-\nabla V(x-\epsilon v)}{2\epsilon}.$$

If approximate gradient evaluations $\widehat g_\pm$ satisfy $\|\widehat g_\pm-\nabla V(x\pm\epsilon v)\|_2\le\eta$, and $M_4$ bounds the third derivatives of each gradient coordinate in the Taylor remainders on these segments, then

$$\left\|\frac{\widehat g_+-\widehat g_-}{2\epsilon}-\nabla^2V(x)v\right\|_2\le\frac{\sqrt d\,M_4}{6}\epsilon^2+\frac{\eta}{\epsilon}.$$

Thus the deterministic truncation error is $O(\epsilon^2)$ and the force-evaluation error contributes $O(\eta/\epsilon)$. This is an error bound for the Hessian action on the supplied direction; it is not an operator-norm bound for a full Hessian approximation.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ be open, let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb C$ be holomorphic
and let $\Gamma$ be a complex chain which is a cycle, with trace in $\Omega$ and
null-homologous in $\Omega$
([[def-null-homologous-and-homologous-complex-cycles]]). Let $g$ be the filled
difference quotient of $f$ on $\Omega\times\Omega$
([[lem-holomorphic-difference-quotient-is-jointly-continuous]]) and put

$$h_0(z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma g(\zeta,z)\,d\zeta\ \ (z\in\Omega),\qquad \Omega_0=\{z\in\mathbb C\setminus\Gamma^\ast:n(\Gamma,z)=0\},\qquad h_1(z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma\frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta\ \ (z\in\Omega_0).$$

Then $\Omega_0$ is open, $\Omega\cup\Omega_0=\mathbb C$, $h_0$ is holomorphic on
$\Omega$, $h_1$ is holomorphic on $\Omega_0$, and $h_0=h_1$ on
$\Omega\cap\Omega_0$. Consequently the function $h$ equal to $h_0$ on $\Omega$
and to $h_1$ on $\Omega_0$ is a well-defined entire function; it is bounded, and
for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $R>0$ with $|h(z)|<\varepsilon$ whenever
$|z|>R$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. In the symmetric case of [[def-ltwo-operator-associated-with-a-symmetric-elliptic-form]] with $\Omega$ nonempty bounded open, let $\{e_j\}$ and $\{\lambda_j\}$ be the eigenbasis and eigenvalues of [[thm-discrete-spectrum-of-a-symmetric-elliptic-dirichlet-operator]] and fix $\mu\ge\beta$. 1. for every $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ the series $\sum_j(u,e_j)_{L^2}e_j$ converges to $u$ in the $H^1_0(\Omega)$ norm (equivalently in the inner-product norm $a_\mu$), and
$$a_\mu(u,u)=\sum_{j\ge1}(\lambda_j+\mu)\,|(u,e_j)_{L^2}|^2;$$
2. for every $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ the series $\sum_j(f,e_j)_{L^2}e_j$ converges to $f$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ and $\|f\|_{L^2}^2=\sum_j|(f,e_j)_{L^2}|^2$ (Parseval);
3. consequently $a(u,u)=\sum_j\lambda_j|(u,e_j)_{L^2}|^2$ for every $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, the series being absolutely convergent.
This expansion is the form-domain companion of the $L^2$ eigenbasis of the spectral theorem.

$$Y_i=x+h\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}f(t_n+c_jh,Y_j,\theta),$$
$$\Psi_n=x+h\sum_i b_if(t_n+c_ih,Y_i,\theta),\qquad L_n=h\sum_i b_i\ell(t_n+c_ih,Y_i,\theta).$$

On a common compact convex subset with positive margin in $\mathcal D$, their derivatives through order two are uniformly bounded. All admitted local exact trajectories, all numerical trajectories and stages, and all needed joining segments lie in this domain and common tube, uniformly over the fixed parameter neighborhood and $h\le h_0$. $$t'=1,\quad \vartheta'=0,\quad u'=f(t,u,\vartheta),\quad C'=\ell(t,u,\vartheta),$$
$$V'=f_u(t,u,\vartheta)V+f_\theta(t,u,\vartheta)E_\theta,$$

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space with norm $\|\cdot\|$ and
unit sphere
$$S=\{v\in V:\|v\|=1\}.$$

subsequence $(v_{k_j})$ converging in the norm metric of $V$ to some $v\in S$.

$$S_pM=\{v\in T_pM:|v|_g=1\},$$

vector at $p$.

two-point sphere (dimension one) are included.

$$I_n=\frac12\bigl((\Delta W_n)^2-h\bigr),\quad \mathbb E[I_n\mid\mathcal F_{t_n}]=0,\quad \mathbb E[I_n^2\mid\mathcal F_{t_n}]=\frac{h^2}{2},\quad \mathbb E[\Delta W_n I_n\mid\mathcal F_{t_n}]=0.$$

$$\sum_{i,j}L_i\sigma_j(Y_n)I_{ij,n}=\frac12\sum_{i,j}L_i\sigma_j(Y_n)\bigl(\Delta W_n^i\Delta W_n^j-\delta_{ij}h\bigr).$$

   Hilbert space ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]).

$L^2$ norm.

$S_1=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\operatorname{dist}(y,S)\le1\}$ and assume $S_1\subseteq U$.

$\max\{\|D\|_2,\|D^T\|_2\}\le d_+$, and parameters

$$C_D:=d_+^2+M^2/\lambda_{\min},\quad C_E:=\tfrac L2(R_0+M)+\tfrac{L^2}{8},\quad P:=\min\{1,\Delta/(2d_+)\},$$

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$ with Jacobian $J=DF$. Take $x_0\in U$ such that $A:=J(x_0)$ is invertible, and let $\beta>0$ be any bound with $\|A^{-1}\|_{\rm op}\le\beta$. Suppose $\epsilon:=\|F(x_0)\|_2>0$, set $r:=2\beta\epsilon$, and assume the open ball $B_2(x_0,2r)$ lies in $U$ and

$$\|J(x)-J(y)\|_{\rm op}\le L\|x-y\|_2\qquad(x,y\in B_2(x_0,2r))$$

for some $L\ge0$ with $\beta Lr\le\tfrac12$. Then $F$ has exactly one zero $x_*$ in the closed ball $\overline B_2(x_0,r)$, and

$$\|x_*-x_0\|_2\le2\beta\|F(x_0)\|_2.$$

If $F(x_0)=0$, then $x_0$ itself is a zero; this separate case makes no local uniqueness assertion.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$. For $x\in\mathbb R^n$ define $\|x\|_\infty:=\max_{j<n}|x_j|$, and for a linear map $B:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ define its induced norm by $\|B\|_\infty:=\sup_{z\ne0}\|Bz\|_\infty/\|z\|_\infty$. Let $x_0\in U$, $A:=DF(x_0)$ be invertible, and suppose $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty\le\beta$ for some $\beta>0$. Put $\epsilon:=\|F(x_0)\|_\infty\ge0$, and choose $r>0$ with $\beta\epsilon\le r/2$. Assume $B_\infty(x_0,2r)\subset U$ and

$$\|DF(x)-DF(y)\|_\infty\le L\|x-y\|_\infty\qquad(x,y\in B_\infty(x_0,2r))$$

for some $L\ge0$ with $\beta Lr\le\tfrac12$. Then $F$ has exactly one zero $x_*$ in $\overline B_\infty(x_0,r)$, and

$$\|x_*-x_0\|_\infty\le2\beta\|F(x_0)\|_\infty.$$

In particular, when $F(x_0)=0$ the unique zero in this ball is $x_0$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]], let
$f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, let $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a local weak
solution of $Lu=f$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]) and let
$\zeta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Then $\zeta u\in H^1(\Omega)$ and
for every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$
$$a(\zeta u,v)=\int_\Omega\zeta f\,\overline v\,dx+\int_\Omega a^{ij}(D_j\zeta)\,u\,\overline{D_iv}\,dx+\int_\Omega b^i u\,(D_i\zeta)\,\overline v\,dx-\int_\Omega a^{ij}(D_i\zeta)\,D_ju\,\overline v\,dx .$$
The three commutator terms are bounded by
$(2nM_a+\sqrt n M_b)\|D\zeta\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$ and
form a bounded sesquilinear form in $(u,v)$ with coefficients of first and
zero order bounded by $3nM_a\|D\zeta\|_\infty$ and $\sqrt n M_b\|D\zeta\|_\infty$,
while $\zeta f\in L^2(\Omega)$ with
$\|\zeta f\|_{L^2}\le\|\zeta\|_\infty\|f\|_{L^2(\operatorname{supp}\zeta)}$.
The identity supplies an $H^{-1}$ commutator for bounded coefficients;
it does not by itself supply an $L^2$ datum for a regularity theorem.
If additionally $a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$, the localized datum is
$$g_\zeta=\zeta f-(D_i\zeta)a^{ij}D_ju-D_i(a^{ij}uD_j\zeta)+b^iuD_i\zeta\in L^2(\Omega),$$
with $\|g_\zeta\|_2\le C(\|\zeta\|_{W^{2,\infty}},M_a,M_b,\|Da\|_\infty,n)
(\|f\|_{L^2(\operatorname{supp}\zeta)}+\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)})$.
Expanding the divergence uses the second derivatives of $\zeta$ and the
first derivatives of $a$; these costs cannot be omitted.

Let $f$ be meromorphic on a neighbourhood of $a\in\mathbb C$.

1. If $a$ is a zero of $f$ of order $m\ge1$, then
   $$\operatorname{Res}\!\left(\frac{f'}{f},a\right)=m.$$
2. If $a$ is a pole of $f$ of order $m\ge1$, then
   $$\operatorname{Res}\!\left(\frac{f'}{f},a\right)=-m.$$

In either case $f'/f$ has a simple pole at $a$.

Let $X$ solve the finite-dimensional autonomous SDE in [[def-milstein-scheme-and-iterated-integrals]] with $b,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m\in C_b^3(\mathbb R^d)$, using the $C_b^3$ convention in that Definition. $$X_{t+h}=X_t+b(X_t)h+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_j(X_t)\Delta W^j+\sum_{i,j=1}^mL_i\sigma_j(X_t)I_{ij}+R_{t,h},$$

$$|r_{t,h}|\le Ch^2,\qquad \mathbb E[|R_{t,h}|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\le Ch^3\quad\text{almost surely},$$
where $C$ depends only on $d,m$ and the coefficient bounds, not on $t,h$ or $X_t$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$ and give $\mathbb R^n$ its Euclidean metric
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). In this item relabel its zero-based coordinates
by $x_i:=x(i-1)$ for $1\le i\le n$; $D_i$ and $e_i$ refer to these
coordinates. Define the open half-space
$H:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ and its boundary hyperplane
$\partial H=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_n=0\}$. For $r>0$, write
$B_r(x_0):=\{x:|x-x_0|<r\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), so the boundary
half-ball is $Q=\{x:|x-x_0|<r,\ x_n>0\}$ with $(x_0)_n=0$. Let
$u\in H^1_0(H)\cap H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ be such that the tangential second
derivatives $D_kD_iu$ ($k<n$) and the derivatives $D_nD_iu$ for $i<n$ exist
in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$; suppose $u$ solves $Lu=f$ weakly on $H$ with
$a^{ij}\in W^{1,\infty}(H)$ uniformly elliptic with constant $\theta$,
$b^i,c\in L^\infty(H)$ and $f\in L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$
([[def-local-weak-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]). Then the
missing normal derivative $D_nD_nu$ exists in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(H)$ and
satisfies throughout $H$, in the almost-everywhere strong form,
$$D_nD_nu=\frac{1}{a^{nn}}\Big(-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}a^{ij}D_iD_ju-\sum_{i,j}(D_ia^{ij})D_ju+b^iD_iu+cu-f\Big)$$
almost everywhere, with the pointwise bound
$|D_nD_nu|\le\theta^{-1}(M_a\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}|D_iD_ju|+C(n)(M_1+M_b)|Du|+M_c|u|+|f|)$
and the corresponding $L^2$ estimate on each boundary half-ball $Q=B_r(x_0)\cap H$, $x_0\in\partial H$, on which $f$ and all the nonnormal second derivatives on the right are in $L^2(Q)$. In particular those hypotheses imply $D_n^2u\in L^2(Q)$, with
$$\|D_n^2u\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C\left(\sum_{(i,j)\ne(n,n)}\|D_iD_ju\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|Du\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|u\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|f\|_{L^2(Q)}\right).$$
Uniform ellipticity gives $\operatorname{Re}a^{nn}\ge\theta$ and hence $|a^{nn}|\ge\theta$, which makes division legitimate for real or complex coefficients.

Assume the Axiom of Choice through the ACL interface of
[[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]]. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded open
interval, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ have weak derivative $u'$ and unique absolutely
continuous representative $u^*$
([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]).
Then for every $0<\varepsilon<b-a$:

(i) if $1<p<\infty$,
$$|u^*(a)|^p\le2^{p-1}\Bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^{p-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\Bigr),$$
and the same inequality holds at $b$ with $(b-\varepsilon,b)$ in place of
$(a,a+\varepsilon)$;

(ii) if $p=1$,
$$|u^*(a)|\le\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|,$$
and likewise at $b$.

The endpoint values are those of the absolutely continuous representative and
do not depend on the chosen representative of the class. In the form used by
the half-space estimates, multiplying by $\varepsilon$ gives
$$\varepsilon\,|u^*(a)|^p\le2^{p-1}\Bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\Bigr),$$
which at $p=1$ is the unsquared inequality $\varepsilon|u^*(a)|\le\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|+\varepsilon\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$ since $2^{0}=1$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(V,H,V^*)$ be the real evolution triple of
[[def-parabolic-evolution-triple-and-energy-space]], and let
$u,v\in W(0,T;V)$. Each has a unique representative in $C([0,T];H)$, and
for all $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\|u(t)\|_H^2-\|u(s)\|_H^2 =2\int_s^t\langle u'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\,dr,$$
$$(u(t),v(t))_H-(u(s),v(s))_H =\int_s^t\bigl(\langle u'(r),v(r)\rangle_{V^*,V} +\langle v'(r),u(r)\rangle_{V^*,V}\bigr)\,dr.$$
Writing $c_i=\|i:V\to H\|$, the trace obeys
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|u(t)\|_H^2 \le \frac{c_i^2}{T}\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}^2 +2\|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;V^*)}\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;V)}.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a separable real Hilbert space and $Y$ a real Hilbert space, and
let $u\in H^1(0,T;X)$ (meaning
$u,u'\in L^2(0,T;X)$ with distribution derivative). It has a unique
continuous representative on $[0,T]$. Let
$P\in\mathcal L(X,Y)$ be a fixed bounded linear map. Then
$Pu\in H^1(0,T;Y)$ and $(Pu)'=Pu'$.

If instead $P:[0,T]\to\mathcal L(X,Y)$ is continuously differentiable in
operator norm, then $P(t)u(t)\in H^1(0,T;Y)$ and
$$\frac{d}{dt}(P(t)u(t))=P'(t)u(t)+P(t)u'(t)\quad\text{a.e.}$$
In particular, a differentiable time-dependent Ritz comparison contributes
the term $P'(t)u(t)$ to its residual derivative.

Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\Theta$ be open, and let $f:D\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuously differentiable. Let $V_\theta\subseteq\Theta$ be open and $u_0:V_\theta\to\mathbb R^d$ be $C^1$. Assume there is a bounded convex open set $O\subset D$ with compact closure in $D$ such that for every $\theta\in V_\theta$ the unique solution of $u'=f(t,u,\theta)$, $u(0)=u_0(\theta)$, exists on $[0,T]$, and all triples $(t,u_\theta(t),\theta)$ lie in $O$. $$S'(t)=D_u f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0)S(t)+D_\theta f(t,u_{\theta_0}(t),\theta_0),\qquad S(0)=D u_0(\theta_0).$$
The result is local to the stated common compact tube and claims no differentiability outside it.

At a phase-fixed periodic point $x_*$ with period $T$, let $M=D_x\phi_T(x_*)$, let $f_*=f(x_*)\ne0$, and let $c=D\psi(x_*)$ for the affine phase $\psi(x)=c^\top(x-x_{\rm ref})$. The derivative of the phase-bordered shooting residual is
$$ J=\begin{bmatrix}M-I_d&f_*\\c^\top&0\end{bmatrix}. $$
It is invertible if and only if $1$ is an algebraically simple eigenvalue of $M$ and $c^\top f_*\ne0$. In the simple case choose real left/right eigenvectors $w,f_*$ with $w^\top f_*=1$, put $Q=I-f_*w^\top$ and $W=\ker w^\top$, and let $K_W=\|((M-I_d)|_W)^{-1}\|_{2\to2}$. All vector and matrix norms below are Euclidean and induced Euclidean norms, and the product norm on $(u,\tau)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$ is Euclidean. Then
$$ \|J^{-1}\|_{2\to2}\le K_W\|Q\|_2+\|w\|_2+ \frac{\|f_*\|_2\bigl(1+\|c\|_2K_W\|Q\|_2\bigr)}{|c^\top f_*|}. $$
The period column is the exact time-sensitivity $f_*$.

Let $P\in\mathbb Q[x]$ be nonzero of degree $d$, and put $f=P/\operatorname{lc}(P)$, so $f$ is monic. Set $p_0=f$ and, recursively, let $p_k$ be the monic greatest common divisor of $p_{k-1}$ and $p_{k-1}'$ for $k\ge1$, with $\gcd(1,0)=1$. For $1\le k\le d$, put $s_k=p_{k-1}/p_k$ and put $s_{d+1}=1$. Then each $q_k=s_k/s_{k+1}$ is a monic polynomial in $\mathbb Q[x]$, the $q_k$ are squarefree and pairwise coprime, and
$$
f=\prod_{k=1}^{d}q_k^k.
$$
The complex roots of $q_k$ are exactly the roots of $P$ having multiplicity $k$. In particular, $\prod_{k=1}^{d}q_k$ is squarefree and has exactly the distinct roots of $P$. For $d=0$, the product is empty and $P$ has no roots.

Here a polynomial is called **squarefree** when each of its complex roots has multiplicity one.
---

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be open, and let
$F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^2$. Suppose $F(z_0)=0$ and
$\operatorname{rank}DF(z_0)=n$. Let $t\in\ker DF(z_0)$ be a unit vector.
There is an interval about $0$ and a unique local $C^2$ curve
$\gamma(r)$ satisfying
$$F(\gamma(r))=0,\qquad \gamma(0)=z_0,\qquad t^T(\gamma(r)-z_0)=r.$$
There is a neighborhood $V$ of $z_0$ in which every solution $z$ of $F(z)=0$
has the form $z=\gamma(t^T(z-z_0))$. It has $\gamma'(0)=t$. After reparameterization by Euclidean arclength,
the same local curve is represented by a $C^1$ unit-speed curve $c(s)$ with
$c(0)=z_0$ and $c'(0)=t$.

Let $K\subseteq U$ be convex, let $c(s)$ and the segment from
$c(s)$ to $c(s)+h c'(s)$ lie in $K$ for a step $h>0$, and suppose
$$\|DF(u)-DF(v)\|_{\rm op}\le L\|u-v\|_2\qquad(u,v\in K).$$
For $z_p:=c(s)+h c'(s)$, the augmented pseudo-arclength residual
$$G_{s,h}(z):=\bigl(F(z),c'(s)^T(z-z_p)\bigr)$$
satisfies
$$\|G_{s,h}(z_p)\|_2=\|F(z_p)\|_2\le\frac{\sqrt n L}{2}h^2.$$
Thus the predictor defect is quadratic in the step length on the stated tube.

continuous on its trace $\gamma^\ast$, let $a=t_0<t_1<\dots<t_r=b$ be a partition

$\gamma_i$ for the restriction $\gamma|_{[t_i,t_{i+1}]}$ and

$$\omega_i:=\sup\bigl\{\,|f(u)-f(v)|\ :\ u,v\in\gamma([t_i,t_{i+1}])\,\bigr\},$$

which is a nonnegative real number. Then

$$\left|\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz-\sum_{i<r}f(\gamma(\xi_i))\bigl(\gamma(t_{i+1})-\gamma(t_i)\bigr)\right|\ \le\ \sum_{i<r}\omega_i\,L(\gamma_i).$$

$u,v\in\gamma^\ast$, then the left-hand side is at most $\omega\,L(\gamma)$.

modulus of continuity for $f$ on $\gamma^\ast$ converts directly into an error
estimate. For a singleton parameter interval $[a,a]$ there is no partition, and
both the integral and the empty tagged sum are $0$.

Let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric, let $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and
let $\Delta>0$. Every global minimizer $p_*$ of
$$q(p):=\langle g,p\rangle+\tfrac12p^TBp\quad\text{over }\|p\|_2\le\Delta$$
has a multiplier $\lambda\ge0$ such that
$$(B+\lambda I)p_*=-g,\qquad B+\lambda I\succeq0,\qquad \lambda(\Delta-\|p_*\|_2)=0.$$
Conversely, every feasible $p_*$ satisfying these conditions is a global
minimizer. A global minimizer always exists.

The singular hard case is included as follows. Let $\mu$ be the least
eigenvalue of $B$ and $E_\mu$ its eigenspace. If $\mu<0$, $g\perp E_\mu$,
and the solution $p_0$ of
$(B-\mu I)p_0=-g$, $p_0\perp E_\mu$, has $\|p_0\|_2\le\Delta$, then
$$p_*=p_0+z,\qquad z\in E_\mu,\qquad \|z\|_2^2=\Delta^2-\|p_0\|_2^2$$
is a global minimizer with the singular multiplier $\lambda=-\mu$. If
$\|p_0\|_2<\Delta$, both signs of any chosen nonzero $z$ of the required
length give distinct minimizers.

Statement

**Reversal.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to\mathbb C$ be a closed complex contour and let
$p\notin\gamma^\ast$. Then the reversal $\gamma^-(t)=\gamma(a+b-t)$ is a closed
complex contour with the same trace, and

$$n(\gamma^-,p)=-n(\gamma,p).$$

**Concatenation.** Let $\alpha,\beta:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$ be complex contours with
$\alpha(1)=\beta(0)$. Then $\alpha*\beta$ is a complex contour with trace
$\alpha^\ast\cup\beta^\ast$, and for every
$p\notin\alpha^\ast\cup\beta^\ast$

$$\int_{\alpha*\beta}\frac{dz}{z-p}=\int_\alpha\frac{dz}{z-p}+\int_\beta\frac{dz}{z-p}.$$

If moreover $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are themselves closed, then $\alpha*\beta$ is
closed and

$$n(\alpha*\beta,p)=n(\alpha,p)+n(\beta,p).$$

The hypothesis $\alpha(1)=\beta(0)$ is what makes the concatenation a contour,
and closedness of $\alpha*\beta$ is what makes its index defined; the integral
identity needs neither $\alpha$ nor $\beta$ to be closed.

the fundamental theorem of calculus for absolutely continuous functions), for
the countable selections of cutoffs and mollifier scales below, and through the

Let $n\ge1$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ and bounded
below by $f_{inf}$.
Run [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with exact Hessians and parameters
$0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, $\gamma_{up}>1$, $0<\gamma_{down}<1$,
$0<\kappa<1$, $0<\kappa_\theta<1$, and
$0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_k\le\sigma_{max}$ with $\sigma_{max}\ge3L$.
Suppose the Hessian is $L$-Lipschitz on every trial segment, and let
$0<\varepsilon\le1$. Let $R\in\mathbb N_0$ satisfy
$\gamma_{up}^R\sigma_{min}\ge3L$ (take $R=0$ if
$\sigma_{min}\ge3L$).

The algorithm has two complexity guarantees.

1. **Exact model minimizers.** If every solver call returns an exact global
   minimizer, define
   $$C_g:=\sigma_{max}+\sqrt n\,L,\qquad c_g:=\frac{\eta_1\sigma_{min}}{6C_g^{3/2}}.$$
   Through the first iterate with gradient norm at most $\varepsilon$, the
   numbers $N_s$ of accepted steps and $N_u$ of rejected trials satisfy
   $$N_s\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c_g^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\qquad N_u\le R N_s.$$

2. **Admissible inexact model steps.** Suppose each solver-success candidate
   passes the cubic solution, residual, and Cauchy-decrease checks in
   [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]], and $\nabla f$ is $K$-Lipschitz
   on every trial segment. If the solver succeeds at every nonterminal
   trial, define
   $$D_g:=\frac{\sigma_{max}+\sqrt n\,L+\kappa_\theta K} {1-\kappa_\theta},\qquad c_a:=\frac{\eta_1\sigma_{min}}{6D_g^{3/2}}.$$
   Then the same counts satisfy
   $$N_s\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c_a^{-1}\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\qquad N_u\le R N_s.$$

In either case the uncapped process reaches a stationary or target-achieved
iterate with gradient norm at most $\varepsilon$. For the finite-cap
algorithm, an outer cap at least
$$(R+1)\left(\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c\,\varepsilon^{3/2}}+1\right)$$
suffices, where $c=c_g$ in case 1 and $c=c_a$ in case 2. The resulting
number of outer trials, and their function, gradient, and Hessian evaluation
counts, are $O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. These counts do not bound the internal
work of the model solver.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$ and let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ map a reference
simplex to an affine cell with $\det A>0$. The contravariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v=(\det A)^{-1}A\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{div},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{div},K)$ and
$$\operatorname{div}(\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v) =(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}.$$
The covariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}\widehat v=A^{-T}\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{curl},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{curl},K)$;
in $d=2$ its scalar curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$,
and in $d=3$ its vector curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}A(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$.
For every $\widehat u\in W^{1,2}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$, the scalar
pullback $u=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)$ and
its gradient satisfies
$$\nabla u=\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}(\widehat\nabla\widehat u).$$
For smooth fields, contravariant normal fluxes satisfy
$v\cdot n\,dS=\widehat v\cdot\widehat n\,d\widehat S$; covariant tangential
pullbacks satisfy $v(F(\widehat x))\cdot A\widehat\tau=
\widehat v(\widehat x)\cdot\widehat\tau$ for every reference tangent
$\widehat\tau$. Thus edge line integrals and normal-flux moments are
preserved, and face tangential moments transform with this pullback and
the induced facet surface Jacobian. These formulas record the chosen
orientation; reversing a facet orientation reverses its signed moment.

Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to\mathbb C$ be a closed complex contour, let
$f$ be meromorphic on a neighbourhood of $\gamma^\ast$, and suppose
$f(z)\ne0$ for every $z\in\gamma^\ast$. Then $f\circ\gamma$ is a closed complex

$$\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\gamma \frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz=n(f\circ\gamma,0).$$

Equivalently, if $\theta$ is any continuous argument of $f\circ\gamma$, then

$$\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\gamma \frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz=\frac{\theta(b)-\theta(a)}{2\pi}.$$

which $f$ is meromorphic, then the same integer equals $Z(f,\gamma)-P(f,\gamma)$
by [[thm-argument-principle-null-homologous-cycle]].

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and convex, and let $f\in C^2(U,\mathbb R)$ have an attained global minimum $f^*=f(x^*)$ at $x^*\in U$. Fix $x_0\in U$ and suppose $K:=\{y\in U:f(y)\le f(x_0)\}$ is compact. Let $V\subseteq U$ be convex and open, contain $K$ and every backtracking trial segment under consideration, and satisfy

$$mI\preceq H_f(y)\preceq MI\qquad(y\in V)$$

for $0<m\le M$. Run [[alg-gradient-descent]] in backtracking mode with Armijo parameter $a\in(0,1/2)$ and shrink factor $b\in(0,1)$. For every accepted update at a nonstationary iterate $x_k$, the accepted step satisfies

$$t_k\ge\tau:=\min\left\{1,\frac{2b(1-a)}{M}\right\},$$

and

$$f(x_{k+1})-f^*\le(1-2am\tau)(f(x_k)-f^*).$$

Consequently, for every generated $k\ge1$,

$$f(x_k)-f^*\le(1-2am\tau)^k(f(x_0)-f^*).$$

The factor lies in $(0,1)$. If the algorithm's caller-stop predicate fires, no later iterate is asserted. These are objective-gap bounds, not iterate-error bounds.

Form the exact Box–Muller vector from the same ideal uniforms, assigning $Z=(0,0)$ when $U_1=0$ so the null endpoint is defined. Let $\eta_\ell,\eta_s,\eta_t$ be fixed finite upper bounds for its respective reported certificates over all those calls. Such bounds can be obtained as maxima over that finite set after every call has certified success; success on a single sampled input or conditioning on a random success event does not meet this hypothesis. Put
$$R_\delta=\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)},\quad R_b=\sqrt{2(b+1)\log2},\quad p=\delta+\delta_b,$$
$$e=\sqrt{\frac{2\delta_b}{\delta}}+2\pi R_\delta\delta_b+ \bigl(\sqrt{2\eta_\ell}+\eta_s\bigr)(1+\eta_t)+R_\delta\eta_t.$$
For the exact ideal Box–Muller vector $Z$ and the computed midpoint output $\widehat Z$, the bounded-Lipschitz distance, defined by the supremum over functions with supremum norm and Lipschitz constant at most $1$, is at most $e+2p$. The 1-Wasserstein distance, defined as the infimum of $\mathbb E\|X-Y\|_2$ over couplings, is at most
$$e+\sqrt{2p}+(R_b+\eta_r)(1+\eta_t),\qquad \eta_r=\sqrt{2\eta_\ell}+\eta_s.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice, let $B$ be a standard Brownian motion
[[def-brownian-motion]] with raw natural filtration $(\mathcal F^0_t)$ and
usual augmentation $(\mathcal F_t)$
[[def-natural-and-usual-augmented-brownian-filtrations]], and let $\mu$ be
Wiener measure on $C([0,\infty),\mathbb R)$
[[def-wiener-measure-on-continuous-path-space]].

Write $u\mapsto u(t)$ for a point of the product space
$\mathbb R^{[0,\infty)}$, whose product sigma-algebra is by definition
generated by all finite coordinate cylinders (it exists by
[[thm-generated-sigma-algebra-exists-and-is-minimal]]). Here Borel on the
product means measurable for that sigma-algebra. The inclusion
$j:C([0,\infty),\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R^{[0,\infty)}$ is measurable
because its coordinates are continuous. For a bounded Borel
functional $\Phi:\mathbb R^{[0,\infty)}\to\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi_\Phi(x):=\int_{C([0,\infty),\mathbb R)}\Phi(x+w)\,\mu(dw),\qquad x\in\mathbb R,$$
where $x+w$ denotes the point $t\mapsto x+w(t)$.

1. **Increment process.** For every $s\ge0$ the random element
   $Z:=(B_{s+t}-B_s)_{t\ge0}$ is independent of $\mathcal F_s$ and has the law
   of $B$; that is, for every finite cylinder event
   $\Gamma=\{z:z(t_1)\in B_1,\dots,z(t_k)\in B_k\}$ and every $A\in\mathcal F_s$,
   $P(A\cap\{Z\in\Gamma\})=P(A)\,\mu_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\Gamma)$, where
   $\mu_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\Gamma)=\mu(\{w:w(t_i)\in B_i\ \forall i\})$, and the
   analogous identity holds for every Borel set of the product sigma-algebra.
2. **Conditional future law.** For every $s\ge0$ and every bounded Borel
   functional $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^{[0,\infty)}$,
   $$E\bigl[\Phi\bigl((B_{s+t})_{t\ge0}\bigr)\bigm|\mathcal F_s\bigr] =\Psi_\Phi(B_s)\quad\text{almost surely},$$
   and the same identity holds with $\mathcal F^0_s$ in place of $\mathcal F_s$.
   In particular $E[\Phi((B_{s+t})_{t\ge0})|\mathcal F_s]$ is a function of the
   single state $B_s$.

The continuous-path formulation uses a common measurable probability-one
event $A_*$ on which all paths of $B$ are continuous. Define
$V^s(\omega)(t)=B_{s+t}(\omega)$ on $A_*$ and let $V^s(\omega)$ be the zero
path off $A_*$. For every bounded Borel $\phi:C([0,\infty),\mathbb R)\to\mathbb R$,
the same conditional identity holds with $\phi(V^s)$ on the left and
$\int\phi(B_s+w)\mu(dw)$ on the right, for either past sigma-algebra.
This convention is independent almost surely of the choice of $A_*$.

Let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^2$ on an open set $U$. Let $T_+>0$, let $W\subset U$ be open, and suppose every solution from $x\in W$ exists on an open time interval containing $[0,T_+]$ and stays in one compact convex set $K\subset U$ for all $t\in[0,T_+]$. $$
\partial_t S=Df(\Phi)S,\qquad S(0,x)=I_n,
$$

$$
\partial_t H[u,v]=Df(\Phi)H[u,v]+D^2f(\Phi)[S u,S v],\qquad H(0,x)[u,v]=0.
$$

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C$ be open, let $a\in U$, and write $f=u+iv:U\to\mathbb C$. The following are equivalent:

1. $f$ is complex differentiable at $a$.
2. Under $\mathbb C\cong\mathbb R^2$, the map $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and $Df(a)$ is multiplication by a complex number.
3. The map $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and $\partial_{\bar z}f(a)=0$.
4. The map $f$ is real totally differentiable at $a$ and satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations

$$ u_x(a)=v_y(a),\qquad u_y(a)=-v_x(a). $$

When these conditions hold,

$$ f'(a)=u_x(a)+iv_x(a)=v_y(a)-iu_y(a)=\partial_zf(a). $$

When $Q$ is a nonzero constant, $D=\mathbb C$; when $Q$ is the zero polynomial, $D=\varnothing$ and no rational function is defined there.

Fix a mesh and a finite transcription generated from the pointwise smooth data in [[def-ctrl1-smooth-transcription-data]]. Suppose its NLP functions have continuous derivatives through order three on an open neighborhood of a KKT point $(z_*,\mu_*)$, LICQ holds there, every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive, and the second-order sufficient condition holds on the critical cone. Then, after the correct active set is identified, the exact-Hessian full-step branch using [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]] is well-defined from a sufficiently close primal-dual start and converges quadratically to $(z_*,\mu_*)$. The finite-budget dispatch of [[alg-ctrl1-finite-budget-transcription-solver-dispatch]] may terminate before this local convergence is realized.

This also has the following conditional mesh-family conclusion. For each mesh index $N$, let $\mathcal K_N:Z_N\to Y_N$ be the square active-set KKT residual map of a finite transcription, with finite-dimensional normed spaces $Z_N,Y_N$, and let $z_N^0\in Z_N$ be a reference primal-dual pair. Let $Z$ be a common Banach space containing the continuous primal and multiplier fields, with bounded linear reconstruction maps $E_N:Z_N\to Z$ that use the same fixed norms and satisfy $\sup_N\|E_N\|\le C_E$. Suppose a continuous KKT pair $z^\dagger\in Z$ and mesh-consistent constraints satisfy $\|E_Nz_N^0-z^\dagger\|_Z\to0$ and $\|\mathcal K_N(z_N^0)\|_{Y_N}\le\varepsilon_N\to0$. Suppose the discrete sensitivity maps $D\mathcal K_N(z_N^0):Z_N\to Y_N$ are invertible with $\|D\mathcal K_N(z_N^0)^{-1}\|\le\beta$ uniformly, and $D\mathcal K_N$ is $L$-Lipschitz on a common radius $r$ about each $z_N^0$, with constants independent of $N$. For all sufficiently large $N$, require $2\beta\varepsilon_N\le r$ and $2\beta^2L\varepsilon_N\le\frac12$. Then there is a unique active-set KKT root $z_N^*$ in the radius-$2\beta\varepsilon_N$ ball, and $\|E_Nz_N^*-z^\dagger\|_Z\le\|E_Nz_N^0-z^\dagger\|_Z+2C_E\beta\varepsilon_N\to0$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice.

For the LQR data of [[def-ctrl1-linear-lqr-control-problem]], let $\mathcal F$ be nonempty and convex and let $u\in\mathcal F$. Put $g(t)=B(t)^Tp(t)+R(t)u(t)$, with the adjoint from [[def-ctrl1-lqr-adjoint-equation]]. If $u$ minimizes $J$ on $\mathcal F$, then
$$\int_0^T g(t)^T(v(t)-u(t))\,dt\ge0\qquad(v\in\mathcal F).$$
Conversely, if this variational inequality holds at $u$, then $u$ is the unique minimizer on $\mathcal F$.

If $\mathcal F=\mathcal U_c$, the variational inequality is equivalent (under Dependent Choice, hence Countable Choice) to the existence of one null set $N$ such that $g(t)^T(c-u(t))\ge0$ for every $t\notin N$ and every $c\in U_c$. The pointwise condition is not asserted for additional state or terminal constraints.

Let $u^*$ minimize the LQR objective $J$ on a convex feasible set $\mathcal F$, with control weight $R(t)\succeq rI$ for $r>0$. Let $u_N\in\mathcal F$ and let $v_N\in\mathcal F$ be a recovered comparison control. Suppose the computed objective $J_N$ satisfies $|J_N(w)-J(w)|\le\delta_N$ for $w=u_N,v_N$, and $J_N(u_N)\le J_N(v_N)+\eta_N$. If $J(v_N)\le J(u^*)+\rho_N$, then $J(v)-J(u^*)\ge\frac r2\|v-u^*\|_2^2$ for every $v\in\mathcal F$, and
$$0\le J(u_N)-J(u^*)\le2\delta_N+\eta_N+\rho_N,\qquad \|u_N-u^*\|_{L^2}\le\sqrt{\frac{2(2\delta_N+\eta_N+\rho_N)}{r}}.$$
The conclusion is conditional on the stated objective consistency and comparison bounds. A raw embedded RK error estimate is not a certified value of $\delta_N$.

Here are sufficient bounds that derive the two error terms from transcription errors and recovery. Set $C_s=e^{\|A\|_\infty T}\|B\|_\infty\sqrt T$, $M_c=\sup_{c\in U_c}\|c\|_2$, $M_x=e^{\|A\|_\infty T}(\|x_0\|_2+\|B\|_\infty T M_c)$, $E=\sqrt T M_x+\|x_d\|_2$, and $M_T=M_x+\|x_T\|_2$. Suppose, for $w=u_N,v_N$, a pointwise representative and sampling rule are fixed, $J_N(w)$ has the form
$$J_N(w)=\sum_k\omega_{Nk}\widetilde\ell_{N,w}(\tau_{Nk})+\tfrac12(\widetilde x_N[w](T)-x_T)^TP(\widetilde x_N[w](T)-x_T),$$
where $\widetilde\ell_{N,w}(t)=\tfrac12((\widetilde x_N[w](t)-x_d(t))^TQ(t)(\widetilde x_N[w](t)-x_d(t))+w(t)^TR(t)w(t))$, $\omega_{Nk}\ge0$, $\sum_k\omega_{Nk}=T$, and the chosen samples satisfy $\|Q(\tau_{Nk})\|_2\le\|Q\|_\infty$. Suppose $\|\widetilde x_N[w]-x_w\|_\infty\le e_N$, $\|x_w(\tau_{Nk})-x_d(\tau_{Nk})\|_2\le E_N$, $\|x_w(T)-x_T\|_2\le M_T$, and
$$\left|\sum_k\omega_{Nk}\ell_w(\tau_{Nk})-\int_0^T\ell_w(t)dt\right|\le q_N,$$
where $\ell_w(t)=\tfrac12((x_w(t)-x_d(t))^TQ(t)(x_w(t)-x_d(t))+w(t)^TR(t)w(t))$. Then one may take
$$\delta_N=q_N+\tfrac T2\|Q\|_\infty(2E_N+e_N)e_N+\tfrac12\|P\|(2M_T+e_N)e_N.$$
If a feasible recovery sequence also satisfies $\|v_N-u^*\|_2\le\sigma_N$, then one may take $\rho_N=C_J\sigma_N$, where
$$C_J=\|Q\|_\infty E\sqrt T C_s+\|P\|M_T C_s+M\sqrt T M_c,$$
with $M$ any essential upper bound for $\|R(t)\|_2$. In the control-only case, under Countable Choice the cell-average lemma supplies $v_N=P_Nu^*$ and $\sigma_N\to0$. If $u^*$ is Lipschitz with constant $L_u$, then $\sigma_N=\sqrt T L_u h_N$ is a valid rate for mesh size $h_N$. For a general $L^2$ minimizer, no rate for $\sigma_N$ is asserted.

Fix a constant-step $k$-step method from [[def-linear-multistep-method-consistency-order-and-root-condition]] on $[0,T]$, with $N\ge k$ and $h=T/N$. For exact solutions with two continuous derivatives, choose a compact state set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with the exact trajectory in its interior and suppose $f$ is Lipschitz in the state on $[0,T]\times K$. Convergence means that for every IVP satisfying these conditions and every sequence of starting values whose errors at $t_0,\ldots,t_{k-1}$ tend to zero as $h\to0$, each selected run is defined through $t_N$ and its maximum grid error tends to zero. For the sufficiency assertion and order estimates of an implicit method, assume a uniformly local selected branch near the exact trajectory: there are $\eta,\varepsilon>0$, independent of $N$ and the step index, such that for all sufficiently small $h$ and each $n=0,\ldots,N-k$, whenever the preceding history satisfies $\max_{0\le j<k}\|Y_{n+j}-y(t_{n+j})\|_\infty\le\eta$, the step equation has exactly one root in $\overline B(y(t_{n+k}),\varepsilon)\subset K$, and the method selects that root. Explicit methods need no branch hypothesis. The method converges for every such IVP if and only if it is consistent and satisfies the root condition. More precisely, if its order is at least $p\ge1$, the exact solution has $p+1$ continuous derivatives, and the starting errors are $O(h^p)$, then its global error is $O(h^p)$.

The necessity tests $y'=0$ and $y'=1$ have a unique implicit root in all of $\mathbb R^d$ at every step because $\alpha_k\ne0$ and their right-hand sides are independent of the new state. Those runs therefore remain defined even when an unstable mode leaves the sufficiency tube. The sufficiency estimate establishes existence along the selected local branch by keeping every computed history in its neighborhood; it does not assert an implicit root for arbitrary IVPs or step sizes.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and convex, let $f\in C^2(U,\mathbb R)$ have an attained global minimum $f^*=f(x^*)$ at $x^*\in U$, and fix $x_0\in U$. Suppose $K:=\{y\in U:f(y)\le f(x_0)\}$ is compact and is contained in a convex open $V\subseteq U$ that contains every Newton backtracking trial segment under consideration. For constants $0<m\le M$, assume

$$m\|v\|_2^2\le v^TH_f(y)v\le M\|v\|_2^2\qquad(y\in V,\ v\in\mathbb R^d).$$

Assume also that there are $R>0$ and $L_H\ge0$ with $B(x^*,R)\subseteq V$ and $\|H_f(y)-H_f(z)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_H\|y-z\|_2$ for $y,z\in B(x^*,R)$, where $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Av\|_2$. Run [[alg-damped-newton]] with $a\in(0,1/2)$, $b\in(0,1)$, and positive decrement tolerance $\varepsilon$. Let $\rho>0$ and $C<\infty$ be constants furnished by [[thm-newton-local-quadratic-convergence-under-lipschitz-hessian]] for these data, and set

$$\tau_N:=\min\left\{1,\frac{2b(1-a)m}{M}\right\},\qquad q_N:=1-\frac{2am\tau_N}{M}.$$

For every accepted update before entry into $B(x^*,\rho)$,

$$f(x_{k+1})-f^*\le q_N(f(x_k)-f^*),\qquad 0<q_N<1.$$

Thus, after finitely many such updates the method either has stopped at its positive decrement test or has entered $B(x^*,\rho)$. More explicitly, if $\varepsilon<m^2\rho^2/(2M)$, the decrement test cannot stop outside that ball, so the method reaches it after finitely many accepted updates. Once in this ball, every later attempted update has step $t_k=1$ and satisfies

$$\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|_2\le C\|x_k-x^*\|_2^2.$$

The last assertion is conditional on the decrement test not stopping first. No post-stop iterate or update is asserted. This is a strongly convex objective result; it does not apply to arbitrary vector roots or indefinite Hessians.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$;
write $\delta_hu=(\delta_h^1u,\dots,\delta_h^nu)$ and
$Du=(D_1u,\dots,D_nu)$ for the difference-quotient and gradient vectors, with
$$\|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|\delta_h^iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega')},\qquad \|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|D_iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
(1) If $1\le p\le\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, then for every
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)$ and every coordinate
direction $i$,
$$\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le n^{|1/p-1/2|}\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
At $p=2$ the vector estimate has constant one. The coordinate bound also
holds on any open $U\subseteq\Omega$ for a fixed $i,h$ for which every
segment $[x,x+he_i]$, $x\in U$, stays in $\Omega$; compact containment
is unnecessary. In particular, $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(H)}\le
\|D_iu\|_{L^p(H)}$ for tangential directions on a half-space $H$.
(2) Conversely, if $1<p<\infty$, $u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and there is $C$
with $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$ for every coordinate $i$ and all
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)/2$, then
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega')$ with $D_iu\in L^p(\Omega')$,
$\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$, and
$\delta_h^iu\rightharpoonup D_iu$ weakly in $L^p(\Omega')$ as $h\to0$.
For $1\le p<\infty$, tangential quotients on $H$ also converge strongly:
$\delta_h^iu\to D_iu$ in $L^p(H)$ as $h\to0$.
Both parts are identities of classes and hold without any regularity of
$\partial\Omega$. At $p=1$ the converse in (2) is deliberately not asserted;
the companion remark records why only a measure derivative survives there.

compact sets. Write

for its Lebesgue decomposition on the Borel sigma-algebra relative to the restriction of Lebesgue measure, and choose a Borel

$$\lim_{r\to0^+}\frac{\nu(E_r(x))}{\lambda(E_r(x))}=f(x).$$

Let $d\ge2$, let $V\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ using the convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], and let $x_*$ be a critical point with Hessian $H_*:=\nabla^2V(x_*)$ ordered as $\lambda_1(H_*)\le\cdots\le\lambda_d(H_*)$. Suppose

$$\lambda_1(H_*)\le-2\gamma,\qquad \lambda_j(H_*)\ge2\gamma\ (j\ge2),\qquad \|H_*\|_{\rm op}\le\Lambda$$

for $\gamma>0$ and $\Lambda\ge2\gamma$. Let the closed ball $\overline B_2(x_*,r)$ lie in $U$, let the Hessian be $L$-Lipschitz there, and assume $Lr\le\gamma$. At every iterate $x$ in this ball, suppose a validated Hessian enclosure gives $\lambda_1(H(x))\le-\gamma$ and $\lambda_j(H(x))\ge\gamma$ for $j\ge2$, and accepted dimer data satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-dimer-mode-perturbation-and-local-saddle-error]] with uniform rotation residual $\tau_{\rm rot}$ and HVP error bound $\delta\le\gamma/4$. Define

$$\alpha:=\frac{4(\tau_{\rm rot}+\delta)}{5\gamma},\qquad q:=\max\left\{|1+\sigma\lambda_1(H_*)|,\ \max_{2\le j\le d}|1-\sigma\lambda_j(H_*)|\right\},$$

where $0<\sigma<2/\Lambda$. Suppose the finite dimer saddle translation of [[alg-finite-budget-dimer-mode-following]] uses a unit direction $v$ from those accepted data and a computed gradient $\widehat g(x)$ with $\|\widehat g(x)-\nabla V(x)\|_2\le\eta$. Put

$$\kappa:=q+\frac{\sigma Lr}{2}+2\sigma\left(\alpha+\frac{Lr}{3\gamma}\right)\left(\Lambda+\frac{Lr}{2}\right).$$

If $\kappa<1$ and $\sigma\eta\le(1-\kappa)r$, then every attempted translation starting at $\|x_0-x_*\|_2\le r$ remains in the ball and obeys

$$\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|_2\le\kappa\|x_k-x_*\|_2+\sigma\eta,$$

and consequently

$$\|x_k-x_*\|_2\le\kappa^k\|x_0-x_*\|_2+\frac{\sigma\eta(1-\kappa^k)}{1-\kappa}.$$

Thus exact translation gradients give local contraction, while a fixed bounded translation-force error gives the stated finite noise floor. The conclusion is conditional on a validated gap and accepted dimer mode at every attempted iterate; a finite rotation cap or missing spectral enclosure gives no such guarantee.

Let $d\ge2$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, and let $V\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ using the convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. Fix $x\in U$. Let $v$ be a unit direction accepted by the rotation test of [[alg-finite-budget-dimer-mode-following]], with paired-force estimate $D_\epsilon$ and $\|(I-vv^T)D_\epsilon\|_2\le\tau_{\rm rot}$. Suppose each force evaluation has Euclidean error at most $\eta$, the third derivatives of each gradient coordinate are bounded by $M_4$ on the dimer segments, and set

$$\delta:=\frac{\sqrt d\,M_4}{6}\epsilon^2+\frac{\eta}{\epsilon}.$$

If $\delta\le\gamma/4$ and the measured Rayleigh estimate $v^TD_\epsilon\le-\gamma/2$, then the sine of the angle from $v$ to the lowest-eigenvalue line of $H$ satisfies

$$\sin\angle(v,q_1):=\sqrt{1-|q_1^Tv|^2}\le\frac{4(\tau_{\rm rot}+\delta)}{5\gamma},$$

where $q_1$ is any unit eigenvector for $\lambda_1(H)$. This is a conditional mode bound; rotation success alone is not an index certificate.

Let $\epsilon_g=\|\nabla V(x)\|_2$. If $\epsilon_g=0$, $x$ itself is an index-one critical point. If $\epsilon_g>0$, put $\rho=2\epsilon_g/\gamma$ and additionally assume $B_2(x,2\rho)\subset U$, $H(\cdot)=\nabla^2V(\cdot)$ is $L$-Lipschitz on that ball, and $L\rho/\gamma\le1/2$. Then there is a unique index-one critical point $x_*$ in $\overline B_2(x,\rho)$ and

$$\|x_*-x\|_2\le\rho=\frac{2\epsilon_g}{\gamma}.$$

The dimer direction bound does not replace the validated eigenvalue enclosure or the residual, inverse, and Hessian-Lipschitz conditions in this local saddle certificate.

$$\nabla J_h=b_h+\sum_{n=0}^N w_n\widehat q_n,\qquad \nabla J=b+\int_0^Tq(t)\,dt,\qquad \sum_{n=0}^Nw_n=T.$$

Gradients of scalar functions are Euclidean column vectors, with $Dg(\theta)[v]=\langle\nabla g(\theta),v\rangle$ under [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; vector expectations are taken coordinatewise.

Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, fix $\theta_0\in\Theta$, and choose an open ball $U$ with $\theta_0\in U\subseteq\Theta$. Let $d,m\ge1$, let $N\ge0$ be a finite integer, let the states lie in $\mathbb R^m$, and let $\xi=(\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_N)$ collect fixed simulation inputs on one probability space. The maps are $u_0:\Theta\times E_0\to\mathbb R^m$, $\Psi_k:\mathbb R^m\times\Theta\times E_{k+1}\to\mathbb R^m$, $\ell_k:\mathbb R^m\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$, and $\phi:\mathbb R^m\times\Theta\to\mathbb R$. Gradients of scalar functions are columns; $D_u\Psi_k$ is an $m\times m$ Jacobian and $D_\theta\Psi_k$ is an $m\times d$ Jacobian. Let
$u_0=u_0(\theta,\xi_0),\qquad u_{k+1}=\Psi_k(u_k,\theta,\xi_{k+1})\quad(0\le k<N).$
Assume the displayed step data maps are jointly measurable in all their arguments and, outside one probability-zero set, are continuously differentiable in their state and parameter variables on $U$. Define
$F_N(\theta,\xi):=\phi(u_N,\theta)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\ell_k(u_k,\theta),\qquad J_N(\theta):=\mathbb E[F_N(\theta,\xi)].$
Assume $F_N(\theta,\xi)$ is integrable for every $\theta\in U$, and that there is a nonnegative integrable random variable $M$ with $\|\nabla_\theta F_N(\theta,\xi)\|_2\le M$ for all $\theta\in U$ almost surely, while $\mathbb E\|\nabla_\theta F_N(\theta_0,\xi)\|_2^2<\infty$. Put $S_0=D_\theta u_0$, propagate
$S_{k+1}=D_u\Psi_k\,S_k+D_\theta\Psi_k,$
and define reverse variables by
$p_N=\nabla_u\phi(u_N,\theta),\qquad p_k=\nabla_u\ell_k(u_k,\theta)+(D_u\Psi_k)^\mathsf T p_{k+1}.$
Then the discrete adjoint integrand
$\Gamma_N=\nabla_\theta\phi+S_0^\mathsf T p_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\left(\nabla_\theta\ell_k+(D_\theta\Psi_k)^\mathsf T p_{k+1}\right)$
satisfies $\nabla J_N(\theta_0)=\mathbb E[\Gamma_N(\theta_0,\xi)]$.

For a family of discretizations indexed by $h$, if each discrete objective satisfies the preceding pathwise interchange hypotheses, $\mathbb E\|\Gamma_h(\theta_0)-\Gamma(\theta_0)\|_2\to0$, and the continuous-limit objective has derivative $\nabla J(\theta_0)=\mathbb E[\Gamma(\theta_0)]$ under the same pathwise interchange conditions, then $\nabla J_h(\theta_0)\to\nabla J(\theta_0)$. This conclusion gives no rate unless a quantitative bound on $\mathbb E\|\Gamma_h(\theta_0)-\Gamma(\theta_0)\|_2$ is also supplied. Euler–Maruyama is the special case $\Psi_k(u,\theta,\Delta W_k)=u+b(u,\theta)h_k+\sigma(u,\theta)\Delta W_k$, with $\Delta W_k$ the simulated Brownian increment.

All tangent, reverse and adjoint derivatives are evaluated on the common full-probability event where the sample maps are $C^1$. Define $\Gamma_N=0$ on its measurable null complement, and use this version in expectations.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. In the symmetric case of [[def-ltwo-operator-associated-with-a-symmetric-elliptic-form]], let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty, open and bounded, fix $\mu\ge\beta$, and let $K_\mu$ be the shifted solution operator of [[def-shifted-elliptic-solution-operator]] ([[lem-shifted-elliptic-solution-operator-is-compact-on-ltwo]]). Then the following hold.
1. There are real numbers $\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\lambda_j\to+\infty$, each eigenvalue repeated according to its finite multiplicity, and an orthonormal basis $\{e_j\}_{j\ge1}$ of $L^2(\Omega)$ with $e_j\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ and
$$a(e_j,v)=\lambda_j(e_j,v)_{L^2}\qquad\text{for every }v\in H^1_0(\Omega),$$
equivalently $e_j\in D(L)$ and $Le_j=\lambda_je_j$ in the sense of [[def-symmetric-elliptic-weak-eigenpair]]. Explicitly $\lambda_j=\nu_j^{-1}-\mu$, where $\nu_j>0$, $\nu_j\downarrow0$, are the nonzero eigenvalues of the compact self-adjoint positive operator $K_\mu$ with $K_\mu e_j=\nu_je_j$ ([[lem-symmetric-shifted-solution-operator-is-positive-and-self-adjoint]]).
2. Every weak eigenvalue of the Dirichlet problem occurs in the list, and each listed $\lambda_j$ is a weak eigenvalue with finite-dimensional eigenspace; eigenspaces belonging to distinct eigenvalues are $L^2$-orthogonal.
3. $\lambda_j>-\mu$ for every $j$, and $a(u,u)\ge-\beta\|u\|^2_{L^2}$ for every $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$.
The proof applies the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem once to $K_\mu$; since $\ker K_\mu=\{0\}$, no Hilbert basis of the kernel is ever selected, and the union of orthonormal bases of the nonzero eigenspaces of $K_\mu$ is already a Hilbert basis of $L^2(\Omega)$.

Assume Countable Choice and the flow-density hypotheses of [[thm-continuous-flow-log-density-equation]]. Let $T>0$, $h=T/N$, $N\ge1$, and $t_n=nh$. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact and convex, and let $U\subset\mathbb R^{1+d}$ be a bounded convex open subset of the ODE domain containing $[0,T]\times K$. Suppose $f\in C^2(U,\mathbb R^d)$, all partial derivatives of $f$ through order two are bounded on $U$, and the exact path and every Euler node lie in $K$. Thus $[0,T]\times K$ is a compact tube with positive margin inside $U$. Put $q(t,x):=-\operatorname{div}_x f(t,x)$ and define
$$B_f:=\sup_U\|f\|_2,\quad L_f:=\sup_U\|D_xf\|,\quad M_f:=\sup_U\|\partial_tf\|_2,\quad L_q:=\sup_U\|D_xq\|,\quad M_q:=\sup_U|\partial_tq|,$$
where matrix and linear-functional norms are induced by Euclidean norms. These constants are finite by the hypotheses. Apply forward Euler to the state and to the continuous-flow log-density equation:
$$x_{n+1}=x_n+h f(t_n,x_n),\qquad \widehat\ell_{n+1}=\widehat\ell_n+hq(t_n,x_n).$$
If $\|x_0-x(0)\|_2\le C_{x,0}h$ and $|\widehat\ell_0-\log p_0(x(0))|\le C_{\ell,0}h$, define
$$C_x:=\frac{M_f+L_fB_f}{2},\qquad D_q:=\frac{M_q+L_qB_f}{2},$$
and
$$K_x:=\begin{cases}C_{x,0}\exp(L_fT)+C_x\dfrac{\exp(L_fT)-1}{L_f},&L_f>0,\\ C_{x,0}+C_xT,&L_f=0.\end{cases}$$
Then, for every $0\le n\le N$,
$$\|x_n-x(t_n)\|_2\le K_xh,$$
and
$$|\widehat\ell_n-\log p_{t_n}(x(t_n))|\le\bigl(C_{\ell,0}+TL_qK_x+D_qT\bigr)h.$$
This is a first-order Euler result; it asserts no adjoint-gradient error bound.

After each event, both trajectories are compared at the reported event time, when both are in the outgoing mode. Let $E_j$ bound their state discrepancy at this aligned mode-segment start, with $E_0=0$.

For mode segment $j$, let $U_j$ be the accumulated piecewise dense reconstruction from the reported start, with a certified local error bound $\eta_j^{\rm loc}$ relative to the exact mode solution from that same start. Let $L_j$ be a state-Lipschitz bound, $H_j$ the segment duration, and $L_{g,j},\varepsilon_j$ the guard state-Lipschitz and reported guard-residual bounds. Let $D_j$ be a certified total error bound between $U_j$ and the exact reference incoming-mode continuation on the prefix. It may be supplied directly; a sufficient ledger calculation is
$$D_j:=\eta_j^{\rm loc}+e^{L_jH_j}E_j,$$
when the two exact mode solutions share the aligned start time, their initial discrepancy is at most $E_j$, and both remain in a common convex tube on which the field is $L_j$-Lipschitz. Then $D_j$ bounds the reference error on the incoming-mode prefix and
$$\Delta_{j+1}:=\frac{L_{g,j}D_j+\varepsilon_j}{\nu_{j+1}}$$
bounds $\widehat\tau_{j+1}-\tau_{j+1}$. Assume $\Delta_{j+1}<\delta/3$ for each event; the event separation then ensures no later exact event occurs before the reported reset time. At each event assume the reset has state and time Lipschitz constants $L_{R,j+1},L_{R,t,j+1}$ on the compared reset inputs, the incoming field is bounded by $M^-_j$ over the event-time bracket, and both outgoing solutions remain through their alignment time in a common tube where the outgoing field is bounded by $M^+_{j+1}$ and is $L^+_{j+1}$-Lipschitz in state. Then
$$E_{j+1}:=L_{R,j+1}D_j+(L_{R,j+1}M^-_j+L_{R,t,j+1}+M^+_{j+1})\Delta_{j+1}$$

Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, and let $V\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be an open time-state domain whose fibers $V_t:=\{z:(t,z)\in V\}$ are open and convex. Let $K\subset V$ be compact. Let $f:V\to\mathbb R^d$ have continuous first partial derivatives, and suppose $y$ is a solution of $y'=f(t,y)$, $y(0)=y_0$, on an open interval containing $[0,T]$, with graph on $[0,T]$ contained in $K$. For each local defect under consideration, require the Euler input and output time-state pairs to lie in $K$; the exact solution segment already lies in $K$.

For $1\le i,j\le d$, assume finite constants $F_j,M_{t,i},M_{ij},L\ge0$ satisfy throughout $V$

$$|f_j(t,z)|\le F_j,\qquad |\partial_t f_i(t,z)|\le M_{t,i},\qquad |\partial_{z_j}f_i(t,z)|\le M_{ij},\qquad \|D_yf(t,z)w\|_2\le L\|w\|_2\quad(w\in\mathbb R^d).$$

Here $D_yf$ is the matrix with entries $\partial_{z_j}f_i$, and the last inequality defines the operator bound used below. The forward Euler map is $\Psi_h(t,v)=v+h f(t,v)$. Then, with $B_i:=M_{t,i}+\sum_{j=1}^dM_{ij}F_j$, for every $t\in[0,T)$ and $h>0$ with $t+h\le T$ whose Euler input and output pairs lie in $K$, its local defect satisfies

$$\|\delta_h(t;y)\|_2\le \frac{h^2}{2}\left(\sum_{i=1}^d B_i^2\right)^{1/2},$$

so it has uniform local order one on $K$ along $y|_{[0,T]}$, with $h_0=T$. For every $t\in[0,T]$, every admitted $h>0$, and every $u,v\in V_t$,

$$\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2.$$

This is a local defect and one-step stability result. It does not assert a global error estimate or an order for any other named method.

Let $K\subseteq U$ be a set of Hermitian inputs and suppose $F:K\to\mathbb H_n$ is
$L_F$-Lipschitz in Frobenius norm. Assume that for some Hermitian $H_0$ with
occupied gap $g>0$, every $F(X)$ lies in the open operator-norm ball of radius
$g/4$ about $H_0$. Use the common circle $\Gamma$ of
[[lem-spectral-gap-persistence-and-uniform-resolvent-bound]], with
$R=(\lambda_r(H_0)+\lambda_{r+1}(H_0))/2-\lambda_1(H_0)$. Then
$$\|\Phi(X)-\Phi(Y)\|_F\le q\|X-Y\|_F,\qquad q:=\frac{16R}{g^2}L_F.$$
Thus $q<1$ is a checkable contraction certificate when also $\Phi(K)\subseteq K$;
a positive gap by itself does not establish that inequality.
